stories.title: Story of mother-in-law entangled in love relationships:Woman seeks son-in-law's arrest; know reality behind marriage with brother-in-law
stories.summary: Anita Devi from Aligarh has 3 children, 2 sons and 1 daughter. Anita arranged her daughter's marriage. The engagement was also done. She gifted a phone to the son-in-law after the engagement. The son-in-law used that phone to talk to his would-be wife. Gradually, conversations started between Anita and the son-in-law. To such an extent that the son-in-law now talked more with his mother-in-law than with his fiancée. When 10 days remained before the wedding, both left their homes. They ran away to live together. Son-in-law Rahul and mother-in-law Anita lived together for about 10 months. Then they had a fight between themselves. Anita left the son-in-law and went to her brother-in-law Devendra's place. Rahul reached the police station. Made several serious allegations. On the other hand, Jitendra, the husband whom Anita had left, also got married. When Anita went home, he didn't talk to her. The daughter whose marriage was to take place is still the same today. There are many questions in this whole matter. Husband Jitendra has accusations. Wife's defense and then allegations regarding the son-in-law. A story has also emerged about brother-in-law Devendra. Today in Sunday Big Story, we learn about this entire matter from one side... Got daughter engaged, used to talk with son-in-law for 15-20 hours Madrak police station is located about 13 kilometres from the Aligarh district headquarters and includes Manoharpur Kayasth village. Farmer Jitendra lived there with his wife Anita and their three children. The couple had been married for around 20 years, while Jitendra worked in Bengaluru. Last year, the family began searching for a match for their daughter Shivani. Through relatives, they were introduced to Rahul, a resident of Nagla Machhariya village in the Dadau police station area. At the time, Rahul worked as a supervisor in a private company in Rudrapur, Uttarakhand. Both families approved of the match, and the engagement was finalised in January, with Rahul’s brother-in-law, Yogesh, playing a key role in arranging the alliance. After the engagement, Anita gifted Rahul a mobile phone. He began speaking with his fiancée Shivani, and the two slowly got to know each other, though Shivani’s shy nature meant their conversations remained limited. For this reason, when Rahul would call, Anita would pick up the phone. Gradually, this pattern increased. Rahul and Anita started talking to each other on the phone. When Anita's husband Jitendra would call from Bangalore, the number would show as busy. When asked, it would turn out she was talking to her son-in-law. Jitendra would also think that since he's the son-in-law, it's okay. Both ran away 10 days before the wedding and kept running Shivani and Rahul's wedding was scheduled for April 16, 2025. All preparations were underway. Wedding cards were being distributed. However, on the other side, Anita and Rahul grew closer. On April 6, Rahul left his house, saying he was going to buy a sherwani and never returned. Similarly, Anita also left alone, saying she was going shopping, and went with Rahul. When both didn't return at night, the search began. A missing persons report was filed. Later, it was discovered that both had run away together. Anita's husband, Jitendra, complained at the police station that his wife fled with three and a half lakh rupees kept for the wedding and jewellery worth 5 lakhs. Police filed a report and began the search. Meanwhile, Rahul and Anita kept running from one place to another. First, they went to Delhi, then to Bihar. From there, they went all the way to Nepal. For 10 days, they kept moving from one place to another. During these 10 days, both travelled 2826 kilometres. Tired and exhausted, they returned to Aligarh. They surrendered themselves to the police at Dado police station. Children started crying together, husband was ready to take them At Dado police station, police also called the family members of Anita and Rahul. Jitendra came with both children. The 9-year-old son started crying while clinging to Anita. Police started counselling both of them. Asked them to go back to their respective homes. However, both were not ready to separate. Jitendra had also agreed that if Anita agreed to come home, he would take her along. But Anita was not ready. She said that Rahul understands her feelings. Respects her. She spent 9 days with him and got to know him well. She can spend her entire life happily with him. Anita said about Jitendra - He would only beat me up. He would beat me up even for ₹100-200. On the other hand, Rahul's father Omvir and others were trying to explain to him. But, he was also not ready to understand. Omvir even said that Anita had tied a black thread around my son's neck and controlled him. My son is not listening because of black magic. One more thing was discovered here. Even 2 months before the marriage was fixed, Rahul had eloped with a woman from the village. On February 6, Anita was freed from Rahul's captivity. She returned to Aligarh from Sitamarhi. She reached her brother-in-law Devendra's house in Bhawanipur. On the other hand, Rahul went to the Dadri police station and filed a complaint. Rahul alleged that over the past two to three months, Anita’s behaviour changed as she began speaking frequently with her brother-in-law, Devendra and quarrelling over minor issues. He claimed she demanded ₹1,500 to send to her sister, leading to a dispute, after which he transferred the money. In his complaint, Rahul also alleged that Anita left with ₹2 lakh in cash and jewellery and accused her of plotting to poison him and flee. Expressing regret, Rahul said eloping with Anita was a mistake and that he should have married her daughter instead. He claimed Anita has a pattern of running away and will not stay anywhere for long. Anita, however, rejected his claims, calling her decision to go with Rahul the biggest mistake of her life. She accused him of daily beatings, confinement and exploitation, and demanded legal action against him. Police called both to the station, but no resolution was reached, and Anita’s family has refused to accept her back. After the police station, Anita went to her home in Manoharpur. After going there, she found out that her husband Jitendra had married again last month. He married a woman from near Atrauli. No one at home talked to Anita. They didn't even let her stay at home. Troubled by this, Anita went back to her brother-in-law Devendra's house in Bhawanipur. Regarding the allegation of running away with brother-in-law Devendra, she says this is all lies. Rahul is defaming her. Her brother-in-law has his own complete family. He is a simple person who drives vehicles. 'The talk of affair with me is wrong' Dainik Bhaskar spoke to Anita's brother-in-law, Devendra, about this matter. Devendra was previously a driver at Trans India. He had an accident recently, after which he is currently at home. Regarding the affair with Anita, he says - This is a very wrong rumour being spread. I have no such involvement. I have my own family. Rahul is spreading all this; he should understand himself. Rahul is a bad person. His marriage was fixed with the daughter, but he developed a relationship with the mother-in-law herself. Regarding bringing Anita with them, he says - Initially, when she came to Aligarh, she first went to the police station. After that, she went to her village, Manoharpur. No one talked to her there. A panchayat meeting was held in front of the SSP. Then the police told me that Anita's family members are not keeping her, so you take her with you. We brought her. She stayed here for 1 day, and on February 13, she left my house. Don't we know where she is now? No truth in allegations of taking cash and jewellery In this entire matter, complaints reached the police several times. When the son-in-law and mother-in-law fled, Anita's husband alleged that she took ₹3 lakh and a half and jewellery. At that time, Anita had said that she left home with only ₹200. Now, Anita is accusing Rahul of taking ₹2 lakh, 500 grams of silver and other jewellery. Here, the question also arose that when Anita left home with only ₹200, then where did the jewellery and money come from? On the other hand, Rahul alleged that Anita took ₹2 lakh in cash and jewellery from the house. These allegations also don't seem to have any merit. Because whatever Rahul had remained at his house. The business he was currently doing didn't generate much income, according to him. It was just enough to run the household. Police are trying to resolve this matter through the panchayat rather than the law. However, they don't seem to be successful here either. Anita's first husband has gotten married. Because of this, Anita's return has become difficult. However, divorce hasn't happened between them. The girl Shivani, whose marriage started all this, still hasn't gotten engaged.

stories.title: Shankaracharya raises concern over safety threats:Says, 'How can I ask security from those plotting my murder'
stories.summary: "How can we seek protection from those who want to kill us? We have already presented our side before the court. Those who are criminals themselves are making allegations against us. Ashutosh is in contact with cow slaughterers.” These statements were made by Shankaracharya Swami Avimukteshwaranand. Ashutosh Brahmachari, a disciple of Jagadguru Rambhadracharya and Shakumbhari Peethadhishwar, has filed a case in court against the Shankaracharya, accusing him of sexually exploiting two disciples. Following the hearing, the court has reserved its order. On February 21, it will decide whether an FIR should be registered against the Shankaracharya or the case should be dismissed. During this period, Dainik Bhaskar spoke with Shankaracharya Swami Avimukteshwaranand in Varanasi regarding the allegations and the ongoing legal proceedings. Here is what he had to say. Question: What do you have to say about the sexual harassment allegations? Shankaracharya: Look, the person making these allegations against us has a criminal background himself. Reports have previously appeared in the media stating that he was in contact with individuals involved in cattle smuggling and cow slaughter. He was also accused of being caught offering bribes to get trucks cleared. Being accused by such a person speaks for itself. We have already said that the campaign being run against us is a result of our stance on cow protection and our call to stop cow slaughter. Today, those whose interests are connected to cow slaughter are the ones actively targeting us. Question: Do you believe this is a conspiracy against you? Shankaracharya: We believe that whatever attacks are taking place are driven by ideology. When you speak about protecting the cow, it is natural that those involved in cow slaughter will oppose you. This is not surprising. Question: Will you demand additional security from the government? Shankaracharya: We have never asked anyone for security, and we do not intend to do so now. It is the responsibility of the state to ensure the safety of its citizens. If the government feels that security should be increased, that is its decision. We will not approach anyone to request protection. We have faith in God. Our scriptures say that one who is under the Lord’s protection cannot be harmed by anyone. Our security comes from our Sanatan Dharma community and our faith in God. How can we ask those who want to kill us to protect us? Question: Has political interference in religious matters increased? Shankaracharya: There is a need to reflect on the relationship between religion and politics. It appears that certain forces want to bring religious institutions under their influence. In Hindu tradition, the roles of religious leaders and rulers have remained separate. If political power begins positioning itself at the centre of religious leadership as well, it disrupts the natural balance. Society must reflect seriously on this. Question: How do you view the 2027 Assembly elections? Shankaracharya: We do not work with any particular election or year in mind. Our clear view is that whoever becomes Chief Minister should be law-abiding and treat the people like their own children. A person driven by ego, revenge, or oppression cannot be suitable to govern a state. Uttar Pradesh is a fertile land with no shortage of capable and hardworking individuals. They should be given opportunities. Question: Are you questioning the Chief Minister’s leadership? Shankaracharya: We speak about principles, not individuals. In a democracy, no position belongs permanently to anyone. There are many capable people in society, and leadership is ultimately judged by the public. Question: Had you previously praised Keshav Maurya? Shankaracharya: At that time, his statement appeared balanced and thoughtful, so we welcomed it. It was not an expression of political support, but a response based on the situation. After that, there was no further significant discussion on the matter. What happened during the Mauni Amavasya bath... On January 18, during the Magh Mela on Mauni Amavasya, Avimukteshwaranand was going for a bath in a palanquin. The police stopped Shankaracharya Swami Avimukteshwaranand's palanquin. The police asked him to walk to Sangam. The disciples of Shankaracharya did not agree and started moving forward with the palanquin. On this, a scuffle broke out between the disciples and the police. Police had detained several disciples. Police had also beaten a sadhu at the police post. This angered Shankaracharya and he insisted on getting the disciples released. Officers tried to reason with him, folded their hands, but he did not agree. After this, police detained several more supporters of Shankaracharya. Shankaracharya's palanquin was dragged 1 km away from Sangam. During this, the canopy of the palanquin also broke. Shankaracharya could not even take a bath. Shankaracharya remained on protest outside his camp until January 28. Then returned to Varanasi. Shankaracharya had said- High-ranking officers were beating our saints. At first we were returning, but now we will bathe and not go anywhere. They cannot stop us. They must have orders from above to harass us. This is happening at the government's behest because they are angry with us. When there was a stampede in Mahakumbh, I had held them responsible. Now they must be telling officers to take revenge. stories.title: Panchayat elections to be held after UP Assembly polls:OBC Commission report may take 6 months, political parties yet to begin preparations
stories.summary: Panchayat elections in UP don't seem to be happening on time. The government has assured to form a commission for determining OBC reservation in the Allahabad High Court. Given this assurance and political parties' election preparations, it's clear that UP panchayat elections will now be held only after the 2027 Assembly elections. A minister of the state government also said, on condition of anonymity, that panchayat elections will not be held on time. Elections will be conducted after the Assembly elections. What is the complete matter, what do political experts say... read the special report... Panchayat elections in UP were held in 2021. Based on this, the term of Gram Pradhans, Gram Panchayat members, Kshetra Panchayat members and Zila Panchayat members will end on May 2. Panchayat elections are proposed from April to June 2026. Panchayati Raj Minister Om Prakash Rajbhar is also making statements that panchayat elections will be held on time. However, the stance of political parties and the Panchayati Raj department regarding the elections indicates that the elections will not be held during the proposed period. Why do Panchayat elections appear to be getting delayed? Political experts say that currently the matter is stuck in forming a commission to determine OBC reservations. This could take about 6 months. If the panchayat elections are not held during the proposed period from April to June 2026, then after that the government, administration, Election Commission of India and political parties will be busy preparing for the assembly elections. Assembly elections are many times more important than panchayat elections for everyone. In such a situation, it is almost certain that panchayat elections will be held only after the assembly elections. Rajbhar himself not ready An official of Panchayati Raj Minister Om Prakash Rajbhar's Suheldev Bharatiya Samaj Party (SUBHASP) also said that the party does not have ground-level preparation for panchayat elections yet. Preparations had begun a few months ago. However, there are no discussions or preparatory meetings happening now. Organization officials have also been indicated that panchayat elections will not be held on time, therefore they should focus on preparing for assembly elections. Political parties also don't want elections on time In the current situation, political parties including BJP, SP and Congress also don't want elections to be held on time. Meanwhile, most ministers in the Yogi government are also not in favor of holding elections on time. They believe that holding panchayat elections before assembly elections will increase political confrontation in villages. According to sources, in recent days there has been a principled agreement in both the party and government to postpone panchayat elections. Political analyst Anand Rai also believes that since panchayat elections are not held on party symbols, multiple workers from the same party contest against each other. This increases political animosity between them. Anand Rai says that if suitable candidates are not selected in panchayat elections, workers may take tickets from other parties, weakening the party. This could affect the assembly elections. If the party's performance is not good in the district panchayat member and area panchayat member elections, it will directly impact the assembly elections as well. Now the big question is why the Panchayati Raj Minister is making statements that elections will be held on time. Regarding this, political analyst Akhilesh Bajpayee says that there are political reasons behind Panchayati Raj Minister Om Prakash Rajbhar's statement. Rajbhar and BJP officials do not want the announcement of postponing panchayat elections to be made right now. Doing so will not only discourage workers engaged in election preparations, but they will also stop ground-level preparations. Term ends in May... how will panchayats run then? According to sources in the Panchayati Raj department, receivers will be appointed in gram panchayat, block panchayat and district panchayat by the last week of April. Until panchayat elections are held, receivers will manage the three-tier institutions of panchayati raj. However, Additional Advocate General Kuldeepati Tripathi says - The government has told the High Court that the OBC Commission will be formed before the panchayat elections. The government will conduct elections only after forming the commission and determining reservations according to rules. However, no discussion has been made regarding the date of panchayat elections. The government said preparations are underway to form the commission. Court path also clear for conducting timely elections Former Additional Commissioner of State Election Commission JP Singh believes that the path remains open for candidates to approach the High Court regarding panchayat elections. While there may be some delay in panchayat elections, it will be difficult to postpone them for a very long time. If any party files a petition in the High Court, the government will have to explain on what solid grounds the election is being postponed. If the government does not provide any concrete reason, the High Court and Supreme Court can also issue orders to conduct the elections.

stories.title: UP STF arrests Amit Yadav in codeine syrup racket:Links to Shubham Jaiswal syndicate; case registered in Lucknow
stories.summary: The investigation revealed that codeine-containing Phensedyl cough syrup is allegedly being diverted and misused as a narcotic substance. Authorities claim its demand is particularly high in West Bengal and Bangladesh. According to the STF, Amit Yadav allegedly purchased nearly one lakh bottles of cough syrup through his firm ‘G.L. Surgical’, located in Saptasagar Drug Market under Kotwali police station limits in Varanasi. The consignment was reportedly worth several crores of rupees. Police allege that fake sales were shown to other firms, and the bottles were sold to smugglers at higher prices to generate illegal profits. Five key points: How the network was exposed Allegations against Shubham Jaiswal Police have registered a case at Kotwali against alleged interstate gang leader Shubham Jaiswal, his father Bhola Jaiswal, and 28 drug traders from Kashi. They are accused of purchasing and selling around 89 lakh bottles of cough syrup worth nearly Rs 100 crore. Of these, 84 lakh bottles were allegedly traded under the names of 93 medical stores in Varanasi. Many of these stores were reportedly found non-existent at the listed addresses. Investigators also found that syrup was shown as sold to nine closed firms, including Srishti Pharma, GT Enterprises, Shivam Pharma, Harsh Pharma, DSA Pharma, Mahakal Medical Store, Nishant Pharma, VPM Medical Agency and Shri Balaji Medical. Officials allege that fake firms were created solely for the illegal trade of codeine-containing syrup. Cases against Shubham Jaiswal have been registered in Sonbhadra, Jaunpur, Varanasi, Ghaziabad and Chandauli. Kingpin claims innocence Fourteen days ago, Shubham Jaiswal released a video claiming innocence. He stated that he had not sold any “poisonous syrup” and denied allegations that children had died due to medicines supplied by him. He said Phensedyl syrup is neither poisonous nor banned and urged leaders not to politicise the matter. He also appealed to Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath for a fair investigation, claiming he possessed evidence to prove his innocence. Has anyone died from Phensedyl? The Uttar Pradesh Health Department has stated that no death linked directly to Phensedyl cough syrup has come to light so far. Officials clarified that the recent deaths of more than 24 children in Madhya Pradesh and Rajasthan were linked to a different cough syrup — Coldriff — manufactured by a Tamil Nadu-based pharmaceutical company. One batch was reportedly found to contain 48.6 per cent diethylene glycol, a toxic chemical previously linked to child deaths in Gambia, Uzbekistan and parts of India. Phensedyl, manufactured by Abbott, is meant for adult cough treatment and contains triprolidine hydrochloride and codeine phosphate. Authorities maintain that while it can be misused as an intoxicant, no deaths have been officially attributed to it as a medicine. The STF said further investigation is underway, and more arrests are likely as the probe into the interstate codeine syrup racket continues.

stories.title: Rinku’s proposal changed her wedding plans:Priya Saroj opens up on how love, family, and IPL schedules shaped their engagement
stories.summary: Indian cricket team player Rinku Singh and Samajwadi Party MP Priya Saroj are once again in the spotlight with their romantic journey. Rinku shared a lighthearted video on Instagram detailing their journey from meeting to engagement, with playful anecdotes about their relationship. Rinku says he fell for Priya at first sight. Priya, smiling, described their story as nothing short of a film script. The couple is now engaged and plans to marry in June 2026 in Kashi. Their ring ceremony took place last year on 8 June 2025 in Lucknow. Rinku’s elder brother Sonu Singh revealed that the wedding date will be final after Rinku completes the IPL, scheduled between 26 March and 31 May 2026. The ceremony will be in Kashi, with a reception in Aligarh. Now read the love story in sequence... It started with an Instagram like When asked if she had “stalked” Rinku on Instagram, Priya denied it. She explained that she liked his page while promoting her sister’s page. Rinku quickly corrected her, saying, “Not once, but twice.” Priya laughed and admitted, “Yes, twice—but he sent the first message saying ‘Hi.’” Rinku arrived 4 hours late for first meeting Rinku arrived four hours late to their first meeting, prompting Priya to scold him. He jokes that Priya wore a long dress while he showed up in shorts. Rinku proposed to Priya, but initially her father, Toofani Saroj, was reluctant. This period lasted about three years, during which Rinku focused on securing his place in Team India while Priya aimed to become a judge. Not 'Dates', but meetings with family Priya revealed that she never went on a date. Early meetings always involved family, and in the first three years, they met only once every 3–4 months. Attempt to arrange marriage with an IAS In 2022, Priya’s father had tried to arrange her marriage with an IAS officer, which she narrowly avoided. Soon after, Rinku received a call from Priya’s brother confirming the marriage. Without hesitation, Rinku agreed. Wedding date postponed twice Fans eagerly awaited their wedding, but dates were postponed twice—first on 18 November 2025 due to a cricket series, and then in February 2026 due to the T20 World Cup. The wedding is now scheduled immediately after IPL concludes. Now get to know Priya Saroj Priya Saroj hails from Karkhiyanv, Pindra Tehsil, Varanasi and was born on 23 November 1998. She joined the Samajwadi Party soon after turning 18 and actively participated in party programs. At just 25, she defeated BJP’s BP Saroj to become an MP. Her father, Toofani Saroj, had previously won three Lok Sabha elections (1999, 2004, 2009). Rinku Singh's father used to work as a cylinder delivery man Rinku Singh comes from Aligarh, UP. He has five brothers, and his father delivered gas cylinders. The siblings often helped with deliveries. Rinku began playing cricket with a leather ball and tennis ball, practicing at government stadiums when club cricket was unaffordable. His mother supported him financially, even lending Rs 1,000 from her shop for a local tournament.

stories.title: UP Evening Wrap:PM Modi’s plane lands on Assam highway; Avimukteshwaranand hits back at CM Yogi more
stories.summary: Bhaskar English brings you the biggest news from Uttar Pradesh and around the world. Here are the top news headlines of the day: 1. Modi’s plane lands on Assam highway, calls North-East ‘Ashtalakshmi' Prime Minister Narendra Modi, on a visit to Assam on Saturday, addressed a public meeting in Guwahati where he launched a sharp attack on the Congress, alleging that the party had endangered national security during its tenure. The aircraft landed at the Emergency Landing Facility (ELF) on the Moran Bypass, making Modi the first Prime Minister to land on a highway airstrip in Assam. 2. If you are a Yogi then why on CM's chair?: Avimukteshwaranand hits back CM, says, 'Shankaracharya doesn't need govt certificate' Shankaracharya Swami Avimukteshwaranand, responding to CM Yogi Adityanath’s remarks in Varanasi, said the identity of a Shankaracharya in Sanatan Dharma cannot be decided by any government or political certificate. He criticised the issuance of such recognition to Swami Vasudevanand, noting that courts have restrained him from being called Shankaracharya. 3. Shoaib killing- 4 bullets in body, 5 in car: Police pick up three from Lucknow, wife lodges FIR in Barabanki In Barabanki, Shoaib Kidwai alias Bobby, a close associate of Mukhtar Ansari and a known history-sheeter, was shot dead on Friday afternoon. He was 50 years old. The attack took place around 1:30 PM while he was travelling by car from Lucknow to Barabanki. 4. Rahul says US trade deal will ‘ruin textile industry’ LoP Rahul Gandhi criticised Prime Minister Narendra Modi and his government over the India-US interim trade agreement, claiming it could harm India’s cotton farmers and textile exporters. Gandhi highlighted that Indian garments face an 18% tariff in the United States, while Bangladesh gets a zero per cent tariff on its garment exports, provided it imports American cotton. 5. Yogi inaugurates Kalyan Mandapam in Gorakhpur: Built with capacity for 300 people; performs Jalabhishek at Shiva temple Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath will inaugurate a newly constructed Kalyan Mandapam in Gorakhpur today during his three-day visit to the city. The facility has been built at a cost of Rs 2.47 crore and can accommodate up to 300 people. The project has been executed by the Gorakhpur Development Authority (GDA), with funds contributed from the Chief Minister’s MLA fund. 6. Lover shoots girlfriend on Valentine's Day: Noida man ends his own life; both bodies found inside car On Valentine's Day in Noida, a lover shot and killed his girlfriend in a car, then committed suicide by shooting himself. Both bodies were found inside the car. People nearby arrived after hearing the gunshot. They called the police. When the Tata Altroz car door was opened, both bodies were found on the front seat. A pistol was lying beside them. Police took possession of both their mobile phones. The couple is said to be residents of Trilokpuri in Delhi. 7. BNP’s India-inspired poll tactics paid off Relations between India and Bangladesh may not be warm at the moment, but India’s influence on the Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP) and its chairman, Tarique Rahman’s campaign was evident. This influence played a key role in giving the BNP an advantage in the elections. 8. What does SP want to achieve with Nasimuddin's entry?: Alliance fear or perception war between Owaisi and Mayawati SP-Congress fought together in the 2024 Lok Sabha election in UP. Both are preparing to contest the 2027 assembly under the grand alliance banner. But in the discussions is Nasimuddin Siddiqui, who left Congress and is about to join SP. Why is SP going to include a major Congress leader in the party? Does SP fear losing the Muslim vote bank in 2027, or are they trying to find a counter to the potential Owaisi-Mayawati alliance? 9. Wife kills husband with brother-in-law, stages suicide: Family performs last rites in Agra, affair exposed on Chocolate Day “She had called her brother-in-law to celebrate Chocolate Day. Both of us were on the bed together. When my husband returned home and saw us, he became furious. That is why we had to kill him.” This is what a woman from Agra allegedly told police after she, along with her brother-in-law, murdered her husband. To make it appear like suicide, they later hanged the body. The family performed the last rites, believing it was a case of suicide. 10. SEBI gives nod to 5 IPOs, including Duroflex and Hexagon SEBI has given the green light to the public issues of a total of 5 companies, including Duroflex and Hexagon Nutrition. On February 13, SEBI issued its 'observations' on the draft papers of these companies. Now these companies will be able to launch their IPOs in the market in the coming months.

stories.title: IIT Kanpur student hangs herself after argument with fiancé:Cuts call on Valentine’s Day, says she will take her life
stories.summary: On Saturday, a young woman’s body was found hanging in her room at IIT Kanpur. The junior technician was on the phone with her fiancé on Valentine’s Day morning when an argument broke out. During the call, she said, “I am going to end my life,” and then disconnected. By the time her fiancé sent a friend to check on her, it was too late. The woman’s body was found hanging from a ceiling fan. After being informed, the Kalyanpur police, along with a forensic team, arrived to investigate. Her family was informed, and the body was sent for post-mortem. Fiance yelled at her, Anju hung up the phone Anju Kumari (26) from Jamtara, Jharkhand, worked as a junior technician at IIT Kanpur for three years. ADCP Kapildev Singh stated that her marriage had been arranged with Pankaj, who is posted at a power house in Odisha. Their engagement was scheduled in a few days. On Valentine’s Day morning, Anju was speaking with her fiancé as usual, when a quarrel erupted over some issue. The fiancé shouted, after which Anju said she would hang herself and disconnected the call. Friend sent to room, young woman had already hung herself Pankaj then called his friend Suraj, who was busy, so Suraj’s brother Suresh was sent to Anju’s room. Suresh found the door locked. Despite knocking repeatedly, there was no response, so the warden was informed. Suresh and the warden then broke the door. Inside, Anju’s body was found hanging from the ceiling fan. She was taken to the IIT campus hospital, where doctors declared her dead. The young woman was to be engaged in a few days ADCP Kapildev Singh said that the diary contained many personal notes. Reading the diary revealed that her engagement was due in a few days. Police are investigating to determine the exact reason behind her suicide. Young woman was depressed after brother's suicide Anju Kumari, originally from Jharkhand, had lost her brother to suicide about a year ago. Since then, she had been suffering from depression but had started to recover after her engagement was fixed. According to her family, she never discussed these matters with them. The news of her death has left the family in shock. They have already left Jharkhand for Kanpur, and the post-mortem will be conducted on Sunday. IIT Kanpur records highest 10 suicides among all IITs in two years In the past two years, 30 IIT students across India have committed suicide, including 10 at IIT Kanpur—the highest among 23 IITs nationwide. IIT Kharagpur recorded seven suicides during the same period, despite having 1.5 times more students than Kanpur. Questions raised on IIT's counseling cell after suicide IIT Kanpur regularly conducts mental health awareness workshops for faculty, staff, security guards, doctors, paramedical staff, library employees, hostel managers, and mess and cleaning staff. A 24-hour support system is coordinated between the CMHW and health centre for any emergency. Peer mentoring is in place for UG and PG students, where senior students guide new entrants. However, the consecutive suicides have raised serious questions about the effectiveness of IIT Kanpur’s counselling cell, suggesting that the system has failed to prevent such tragedies.

stories.title: Man beaten, dragged on Ghaziabad Expressway after car collision:Assaulted for 20 minutes; ₹22,000 and gold chain looted
stories.summary: A minor collision between two cars on NH-9 in Ghaziabad turned violent on Friday night. Four to five men allegedly beat a young man for nearly 20 minutes, dragged him on the highway and robbed him before fleeing. The incident took place around 10:30 pm near NH-9, close to the Delhi-Meerut Expressway. The collision was between a Hyundai i20 and a Maruti Brezza. Victim says he was hit over 50 times Pankaj Kumar, a resident of Wave City, Ghaziabad, filed a complaint at Kavi Nagar police station. He said he was driving from Lalkuan to Wave City when his i20 car hit a white Brezza from behind. The Brezza was allegedly parked in the middle of the highway. According to Pankaj, four to five men stepped out of the Brezza. He also got down from his car. He alleged that the men were drinking and started abusing and threatening him. Pankaj said he offered to pay for the damage to the car. However, the men allegedly snatched his mobile phone and started beating him. “They hit me with more than 50 kicks and punches,” he said in his complaint. First see 3 pictures... Dragged for 50 metres, forced to pay Rs 1 lakh Pankaj alleged that the accused dragged him for nearly 50 metres on the highway. He said they pressed their feet on his chest, kicked him repeatedly and even tried to choke him. He further claimed that the men took Rs 22,000 from his wallet and snatched a two-tola gold chain from his neck. The accused allegedly demanded Rs 1 lakh for car repairs. “I kept apologising with folded hands and told them to file a police complaint if it was my fault. But they did not listen,” he said. Bystanders filmed, but did not help The victim said the assault continued for more than 20 minutes. People passing by allegedly recorded videos of the incident but did not intervene. When some people started calling the police and making videos, the accused fled the spot in their Brezza car. A video of the incident was later posted on social media platform X. Police reached the spot and took Pankaj to a government hospital for medical examination. He suffered serious injuries on his face and near his eyes, police said. Additional Police Commissioner Rajkaran Nair said an FIR has been registered. “The main accused has been arrested. Action is being taken against others involved. Such incidents will not be tolerated. All those responsible will be sent to jail,” he said.

stories.title: Kharge warns Masood against letting ‘Hyderabad figure’ into UP:Comment sparks speculation over possible reference to Owaisi
stories.summary: AIMIM, led by Owaisi, has begun strengthening booths in Uttar Pradesh to contest panchayat and assembly elections. This has unsettled the Congress. Party president Mallikarjun Kharge appears keen to stop Owaisi at any cost. A video of Kharge from the Parliament complex has surfaced. He is heard saying, “Don’t let him come. He will come once and finish, because he isn’t a national party. But he will finish us. Who… the Hyderabad man.” Standing with Kharge were Saharanpur MP Imran Masood and former Charanjit Singh Channi. The “Hyderabad man” remark is being linked to Owaisi. AIMIM has decided to treat UP’s panchayat polls as a litmus test. The party has launched village-level membership drives, booth-level micro-management, and formed 121-member committees at gram panchayat level. Owaisi’s brother Akbaruddin Owaisi has also claimed he is coming to UP. Their growing activity has raised concerns among opposition parties such as the Samajwadi Party and Congress. What did Kharge say in the video? Mallikarjun Kharge is in the video. He says to Imran Masood- Don't let him enter UP. He will come once, he will be finished because he is not a national party. But he will finish us before leaving. Who... the one from Hyderabad. You know, Hyderabad is famous for three things - first Sherwani, second Biryani, and third Pareshani (trouble). Although Kharge did not directly name anyone, social media users are connecting this statement to Hyderabad resident Asaduddin Owaisi and his party AIMIM. Friendship in Telangana, Distance in UP? Interestingly, in Telangana the Congress has often called AIMIM a “friendly party.” During the Jubilee Hills by-poll, Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy openly defended coordination with AIMIM. Who will suffer the most if Owaisi contests? In the 2024 Lok Sabha elections, SP and Congress fought together under a grand alliance, with SP receiving strong Muslim voter support and achieving its best performance yet. Both parties are preparing to contest the 2027 assembly elections under the same banner. However, their Muslim vote base now appears under threat. In recent Maharashtra civic polls, AIMIM won more than 125 seats, including Muslim-dominated areas like Govandi-Mankhurd in Mumbai, snatching SP’s traditional strongholds. SP was reduced to just two seats. These results worry SP. In Maharashtra, AIMIM dented SP’s vote base where leaders like Abu Asim Azmi had long been influential. Owaisi had openly targeted Akhilesh Yadav, saying if Muslim leadership rises, Akhilesh’s “shop will shut.” In 2017, SP suffered losses due to division of Muslim voters In the 2017 UP assembly elections, the Bharatiya Janata Party returned to power. Analysts cited division of Muslim votes as a major factor, with votes split between SP and BSP. As a result, BJP won 62 of 82 Muslim-dominated seats where Muslim voters made up about one-third of the population. Data shows that on nearly two dozen seats, division of Muslim votes benefited BJP. These included Muzaffarnagar, Shamli, Saharanpur, Bareilly, Bijnor, Sardhana (Meerut), Khalilabad (Gorakhpur), Tanda (Ambedkar Nagar), Shravasti, Gainsari, and Moradabad. BJP even won Deoband, which has around 125,000 Muslim residents, as the community split between SP’s Mavia Ali and BSP’s Majid Ali. From Rudauli in Faizabad, BJP’s Ramchandra Yadav defeated SP’s Abbas Ali Zaidi by 30,000 votes. Similar outcomes occurred in Thana Bhawan, Lucknow East, Lucknow Central, Aligarh, Siwalkhas, Nanpara, Shahabad, Baheri, Firozabad, Chandpur and Kundarki seats.

stories.title: Cricketer kills girlfriend on Valentine’s Day, shoots himself in Noida:Bodies found inside car; had bought her ₹1 crore flat
stories.summary: In Noida, on Valentine’s Day, a man allegedly shot dead his girlfriend inside her car and then killed himself by shooting himself. Hearing the gunshot, people nearby reached the spot. They saw that the car was locked from inside. They then informed the police. Police broke the window of the Tata Altroz car and found both bodies lying on the front seat. Both had gunshot wounds to the head. A pistol was in the man’s hand. Two empty cartridges were lying beside him. The couple had been missing from their homes since 13 February. The 26-year-old girlfriend, Rekha, was a resident of Salarpur in Noida, while her boyfriend Sumit, 32, was from Trilokpuri in Delhi. He was a divisional-level cricketer. It is being said that the two had been in a relationship for 15 years. They were planning to get married, but had a dispute over some issue. After this, on 13 February, Sumit sent a message to Rekha saying, “I am going to die. Rekha is responsible for this. She was with me for 15 years. She had promised to marry me, but now she is going to marry someone else. Rekha has betrayed me. That is why I am committing suicide.” After this, he left home in a car and went missing. The girl also disappeared from her house. Her family lodged a missing person complaint at Noida’s Sector-58 police station on Friday. Today at around 1:30 pm, the bodies of both were found in the Sector-39 police station area. Cousin says he bought a ₹1 crore flat for girlfriend Sumit’s father Rajeev works as a Health Inspector with the Municipal Corporation of Delhi (MCD). Rekha and Sumit studied together in school. Rekha frequently visited Sumit’s house. Elder cousin Sachin said that apart from playing cricket, Sumit also ran a water plant. He had bought a flat for Rekha, reportedly worth around ₹1 crore. Family instigated girl against him, says brother The brother said that Rekha and Sumit had been in a relationship for 15 years. They were planning to get married soon. The girl’s family allegedly instigated her against Sumit. After this, an argument took place between the two. 3 visuals from crime scene “He sent a message to his girlfriend, then went missing from home” Sachin said that Sumit had sent a message to the girl’s mobile phone at 3:39 pm yesterday afternoon, writing that he was going to commit suicide. After this, he left home in his car. He did not return till night. The family searched for him but could not find any trace. This afternoon, they received information that his body had been found. Meanwhile, police said that in the preliminary investigation, the case appears to be suicide. The car (DL 14 CL 6473) has been taken into custody. The forensic team has also collected evidence. The youth’s family members reached the police station and were questioned.

stories.title: 'If you're a Yogi, then why sit on CM's chair?':Avimukteshwaranand hits back at CM; says, 'Shankaracharya doesn't need govt certificate'
stories.summary: Shankaracharya Swami Avimukteshwaranand, responding to CM Yogi Adityanath’s remarks in Varanasi, said the identity of a Shankaracharya in Sanatan Dharma cannot be decided by any government or political certificate. He criticised the issuance of such recognition to Swami Vasudevanand, noting that courts have restrained him from being called Shankaracharya. He also accused both SP and the current government of disrespecting religious leaders, warning against political arrogance. Questioning Yogi’s dual role, he cited Nath tradition teachings that a yogi should remain detached from state power. His response came after the Chief Minister said in the Assembly that not everyone can claim the title of Shankaracharya and that no one is above the law. Read in the QA what Shankaracharya said- Question: CM said that no one can call themselves Shankaracharya. What would you say? Answer: His words seem correct, but the question is whether a person who is the Chief Minister won't write Chief Minister before their name? They surely will. Similarly, why can't someone who is Shankaracharya write Shankaracharya before their name? It's not like a Chief Minister or government can appoint a Shankaracharya by giving a certificate. There is no such tradition in Sanatan Dharma. The tradition of Shankaracharya is determined by religious-spiritual means, not by political approval. Question: What is the definition of Shankaracharya in Sanatan? Answer: A Shankaracharya is one who works for Sanatan. The first attribute of Sanatan is 'Truth'. One who speaks the truth, protects cow-mother and dharma is worthy of being called Shankaracharya. This definition is not new, it has been continuing for centuries. Question: Why are you questioning the CM being a "Yogi"? Answer: We haven't raised any personal questions, but rather traditional questions. We are asking how can a person who calls himself a yogi of the Gorakhnath tradition accept political power? This is a question of religious and sectarian dignity. Many saints of the Nath sect have contacted us saying that such conduct is not acceptable according to tradition. A person who knows the depth of dharma understands this. We are asking - how did they become Mahant? Everyone knows that the previous Mahant was their relative. Was this selection made through tradition or family influence? The MLAs wanted to choose someone else as leader-chief minister, but his name was proposed from above. In such a case, what are his qualifications? Family relations and support of a particular organization? The Chief Minister said in the house that we know how to follow the law and also know how to make others follow it. This language does not suit someone sitting in a constitutional position. The language of law is about punishment and procedure, not about arrogance and threats. Question: What is your objection regarding the police action? Answer: We are asking why the Chief Minister did not say a word about the police using force against children, the elderly and women? There must be accountability. The Chief Minister said people didn't know before, but we publicised it. This is arrogance. Kumbh Mela and Magh Mela have been the world's largest religious events for centuries. To say that nobody knew about it before is an insult to history. Question: In 2015, you faced a lathi charge during SP government. What would you say? Answer: We protested then, too. Power brings arrogance; it was there then, it's there now. Arrogance destroys power. Before becoming Chief Minister, he (Yogi) had several criminal cases against him. After coming to power, they were withdrawn. Can any person withdraw cases against themselves? If everyone is equal, why were only his cases withdrawn? Is this justified? Question: What is your demand regarding the entire controversy? Answer: We want Governor Anandiben Patel to take cognisance. Ask on what basis force was used against innocent people. CM should also clarify how he justifies the conflict between the Yogi tradition and state power. Know what Yogi said in the assembly one day before on Avimukteshwaranand controversy Yogi said - Not everyone can be Shankaracharya CM Yogi Adityanath spoke in the assembly on Friday regarding the Shankaracharya Avimukteshwaranand controversy. Yogi said - Not everyone can write Shankaracharya. No one is above the law. Not even me. I believe every person in India should follow the law. If SP people want to worship him, they can worship. The CM said - An issue was deliberately created in the Magh Mela, which wasn't there. Can every person roam around the entire state, becoming Chief Minister? Can someone roam around putting up a Minister's board? Can someone roam around the state becoming SP president? No... There is a system, there is an order. Akhilesh's counter-attack - Getting your ears pierced doesn't make you a Yogi SP chief Akhilesh Yadav hit back at CM Yogi. He said - Can he be a Yogi? Who gave him the certificate of being a Yogi? Many things are clear in the Hindu tradition. Where there are saffron robes, we look at them with respect. But Yogiji, who is our Chief Minister, has no respect. Wearing clothes and getting ears pierced doesn't make you a Yogi. If you have a desire within you, you cannot be a Yogi. Our revered Shankaracharya, whom everyone respects, was not allowed to take a bath. Since the earth exists, no one has stopped saints from taking a bath in the Ganges. He is the first one who has stopped them from bathing. Who will save him when he incurs sin? 'The same law applies to me as it does to any common person' Yogi said - This is the same system in India's Sanatan Dharma. In Sanatan Dharma, the position of Shankaracharya is considered supreme and sacred. Look at the system of the House; there is also tradition here. The House operates according to rules. On Mauni Amavasya in the Magh Mela, 4.5 crore people came. A system was created for everyone. The law is equal for all. The same law applies to me as it does to any common person. No person can be above the law. It is my belief that every person in India should follow the law. Asked SP - If he was Shankaracharya, then why did you order lathi charge on him CM said - There is a sacred tradition of Shankaracharya in the country. Jagadguru Shankaracharya established four seats in four corners of the country. Jyotish Peeth is established in the north, Sringeri in the south, Puri in the east and Dwarka in the west. The four seats have four Vedas. Rigveda, Yajurveda, Samaveda and Atharvaveda. They all have their own mantras. Adi Jagat Guru Shankaracharya made it mandatory that whoever is eligible for whichever seat would be recognised according to tradition. Yogi said - Not everyone can write Shankaracharya. Not everyone can go around as an Acharya and spoil the atmosphere. Everyone must follow the protocols. If he were Shankaracharya, then why did you (SP) people order a lathi charge in Varanasi? Why did you file an FIR? What kind of morality are you talking about? Blocked the road leading to Magh Mela Yogi said - There was a crowd of 4.5 crore at the Magh Mela that day (Mauni Amavasya). The road where people were going was blocked. This cannot be the work of any responsible person. No responsible person can behave like this. If SP people want to worship him, let them worship. But we are dignified people, we believe in rule of law, we follow rule of law, and we know how to enforce it too. We want to implement both things together. Stop misleading people in its name. Yogi called him Kalnemi without naming Avimukteshwaranand Amid the Shankaracharya controversy, CM Yogi was in Sonipat, Haryana, on January 22. Without naming Avimukteshwaranand, he had said - No one has the right to disrupt tradition. There are many Kalnemis who are conspiring to weaken Sanatan Dharma under the guise of religion. We need to be cautious of such people. For a sanyasi, nothing is above dharma and nation. The Kalnemi that Yogi mentioned was Ravana's maternal uncle and Mareech's son in the Ramayana. Ravana had sent him to stop Hanuman when Lakshmana was unconscious. Later, Hanuman killed Kalnemi. Yogi's statement was linked to Shankaracharya Avimukteshwaranand. Shankaracharya called Yogi a fake Hindu On this, Shankaracharya Avimukteshwaranand said - The robe is of a saint, but cow slaughter is happening. Now you tell me who Kalnemi is? Kalnemi was a demon who appeared disguised as a saint. What did the demon do? Kill Brahmins, humans, and cows while wearing a saint's robe. Look here, the robe is of a saint, but cow slaughter is happening. Now you tell me who Kalnemi is? In Muslims, the religious leader is the Caliph (head of state). This Caliphate tradition is being brought into Hinduism. The state government had asked me to provide proof of being Shankaracharya within 24 hours. I submitted this within the deadline. After this, I gave the government 40 days to prove they are real Hindus. But even after 10 days have passed, no proof has come from the government. Yogi is a fake Hindu. Now know what happened during the bath on Mauni Amavasya... On January 18, during Mauni Amavasya at the Magh Mela, Shankaracharya Avimukteshwaranand was going for a bath in a palanquin. The police stopped Shankaracharya Swami Avimukteshwaranand's palanquin. Police asked him to walk to Sangam. Shankaracharya's disciples did not agree and started moving forward with the palanquin. This led to pushing and shoving between the disciples and the police. Police took several disciples into custody. Police also beat up a sadhu at the police post. This angered Shankaracharya, and he insisted on getting his disciples released. Officials tried to reason with him, folded their hands, but he did not agree. After this, the police took several more supporters of Shankaracharya into custody. Shankaracharya's palanquin was dragged 1 km away from the Sangam. During this, the canopy of the palanquin also broke. Shankaracharya could not even take a bath. Shankaracharya remained on protest outside his camp until January 28. Then returned to Varanasi. Shankaracharya had said- High-ranking officers were beating our saints. Initially we were returning, but now we will take a bath and won't go anywhere. They cannot stop us. They must have orders from above to harass us. This is happening at the government's behest because they are angry with us. When there was a stampede in Mahakumbh, I had held them responsible. Now they must be telling officers to take revenge." Pictures of clash between Shankaracharya's disciples and police-

stories.title: Shoaib killing- 4 bullets in body, 5 in car:Police pick up three from Lucknow, wife lodges FIR in Barabanki
stories.summary: In Barabanki, Shoaib Kidwai alias Bobby, a close associate of Mukhtar Ansari and a known history-sheeter, was shot dead on Friday afternoon. He was 50 years old. The attack took place around 1:30 PM while he was travelling by car from Lucknow to Barabanki. The post-mortem examination was conducted later in the evening. According to police sources, Shoaib sustained four bullet injuries — one to the jaw, one to the right hand, one to the chest and one to the leg. The vehicle he was travelling in bore five bullet marks: one on the bonnet, three on the windows and one on the driver’s side door. The motive behind the murder remains unclear. Police have constituted seven teams to investigate the case. Apart from Barabanki police, teams from Lucknow are also assisting in gathering inputs related to the killing. Shoaib is scheduled to be buried on Saturday, and in view of possible tension, heavy police deployment has been made in the area. According to officials, Shoaib had just entered Barabanki from Lucknow. About 100 metres after taking a turn from the highway, two assailants on a motorcycle intercepted his car. Before he could react, they opened indiscriminate fire using pistols. Police sources say more than 15 rounds were fired. After carrying out the attack, the accused fled towards Ayodhya. On receiving information, police rushed to the spot and took Shoaib to a nearby hospital, where doctors declared him dead. The incident occurred near the Aseni turn on the Lucknow–Ayodhya highway in the Kotwali area. The car was found riddled with bullet marks at multiple points. See pictures related to the incident- Police have sealed the crime scene. The forensic team has collected evidence from the spot. IG Praveen Kumar, DM and SP reached the spot after receiving information about the murder. Bobby had 12 cases registered against him related to murder, extortion and gang wars. According to sources, there was an internal power struggle and mutual rivalry within the gang after Mukhtar's death. Shoaib was also a lawyer. He had been practicing law in court for about 15 years. In protest against the murder, lawyers first created a ruckus at the district hospital. After causing commotion at the district hospital for quite some time, the lawyers blocked the road in front of the bus stand. Seeing the situation escalate, the SP called a delegation of lawyers to the office to explain. The lawyers submitted a petition demanding the arrest of Bobby's attackers within 48 hours. Shoaib's one brother lives in England Shoaib has a house in Civil Lines in Barabanki. He was the second among three brothers. His family includes wife Shazia Khan and 15-year-old son Armaan Kidwai. Armaan is a 9th class student in a Lucknow school. His in-laws are in Malihabad, Lucknow and he also has a house in Gomti Nagar. Elder brother Javed is a lawyer in Barabanki. Younger brother Sohail Kidwai lives in England. He has one sister who is married. Shoaib was both a shooter and practiced law. He was also active in politics. He had contested as an independent candidate for the Block Pramukh position of Banki block in Barabanki. But he lost. He played an important role in land grabbing, interfering in contracts and eliminating opponents for the Mukhtar gang. Surveillance began right after leaving Lucknow According to police sources, Shoaib was coming to Barabanki from Lucknow. As soon as he left Lucknow, he was being tracked. The attackers couldn't strike on the highway due to the car's high speed. As soon as Bobby moved the car to the service lane and slowed down, the attackers found their opportunity and executed the attack. Eyewitness said - One shot from the front, the other came close and fired According to an eyewitness, as soon as Shoaib turned onto the service lane from Ayodhya highway to go to Barabanki in his Baleno car, two attackers on bikes who were following him came from the side and moved to the front. Before Shoaib could understand anything, one of them started firing bullets rapidly. The second attacker reached near the driver's side door, he went close and fired multiple shots. Within two minutes, after completing the murder, the attackers fled at full speed on their bike towards Ayodhya. During the incident, three bullets hit the front windshield of the car, one bullet hit the bonnet and one bullet mark is also visible on the driver's side door. Shoaib was also accused of arranging bulletproof ambulance for Mukhtar Bobby was a member of Mukhtar's gang IS 191. Mukhtar Ansari died of heart attack in Banda jail on March 28, 2024. Before this, he was imprisoned in Punjab's Ropar jail. Police had presented Mukhtar in Mohali court of Punjab by bringing him in a Barabanki number (UP 41 AT 7171) ambulance. After this, the ambulance was found abandoned near a dhaba on the roadside on Chandigarh-Nangal highway, 15 km away from Ropar jail in Rupnagar district. The ambulance had luxury amenities. It was bulletproof. The Barabanki Transport Department and Health Department investigated the documents. It was found that the letter from Shyam Sanjeevani Hospital located in Mau and Dr. Alka Rai's voter card were attached in the transport department. However, the registration document and house address were found to be fake. In this case, Barabanki's ARTO filed a case against Dr. Alka Rai at the City Kotwali under IPC sections 419, 420, 467, 468, and 471. The allegation then was that Shoaib helped Mukhtar Ansari register an ambulance in Barabanki using forged documents. Shoaib made headlines in jail superintendent murder case Shoaib Bobby's name came up in the high-profile murder case of jail superintendent Ramakant Tiwari. Ramakant Tiwari was murdered on February 4, 1999. He was returning at 7 PM after attending a meeting at the then Lucknow DM Sadakant's residence. As he reached near Raj Bhavan, criminals opened rapid fire on him. He died on the spot. In this murder case, more than a dozen people were named including bahubali MLA Mukhtar Ansari, rebel SP MLA Abhay Singh, Chandan Negi, Bauwa Tiwari. Chandan Negi was murdered in Lucknow on February 16, 2002. After this, Bauwa Tiwari was killed in a police encounter near Kukrail on March 13, 2002. The remaining accused were acquitted by the court Mukhtar's cousin withdraws bail petition amid murder case After Shoaib Kidwai's murder, mafia Mukhtar Ansari's cousin Gaus Mohiuddin alias Tannu withdrew his bail application from Ghazipur's MP-MLA court on Thursday. Everyone was surprised by his request during the court hearing. It is believed that he did this due to concerns about his safety. Gaus Mohiuddin alias Tannu, a resident of Muhammadabad, had a reward of 25 thousand rupees on him in a murder case. He had been absconding for the past 2 years. Police had recently arrested him and sent him to jail. Tannu's name is linked to accusations of being wanted in the 2001 notorious Usri gang war witness and Manoj Rai kidnapping-murder case. Buxar resident Shailendra Rai had filed a case regarding the kidnapping and murder of his son Manoj Rai. During the hearing in Judge Shakti Singh's court on Friday, the court framed charges against Gaus Mohiuddin. The next hearing of the case will be on February 26. He had filed a bail application in this case.

stories.title: Yogi inaugurates Kalyan Mandapam in Gorakhpur:Built with capacity for 300 people; performs Jalabhishek at Shiva temple
stories.summary: Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath will inaugurate a newly constructed Kalyan Mandapam in Gorakhpur today during his three-day visit to the city. The facility has been built at a cost of Rs 2.47 crore and can accommodate up to 300 people. The project has been executed by the Gorakhpur Development Authority (GDA), with funds contributed from the Chief Minister’s MLA fund. Multiple development projects on agenda Before the inauguration, the Chief Minister visited Jungle Kaudia, where he inaugurated the newly reconstructed main gate at the block premises, the BDO office building, and other strengthening, beautification, and boundary wall works. The Jungle Kaudia building was originally constructed in 1962. He also offered prayers at the Jharkhandi Shiva Temple. Between February 2025 and February 2026, four Kalyan Mandapams have already been inaugurated in Khorabar, Surajkund, Manbela, and Rapti Nagar Extension areas of the city. According to the GDA, construction is ongoing in Jungle Benimadhav, Basharatpur, Nakaha No. 2, Mahadev Jharkhandi Tukda No. 2, and Semra. Ahead of the inauguration ceremony, GDA Vice-Chairman Anand Vardhan inspected the site to review preparations. The Mandap now features Sheesh Mahal-style facilities, modern amenities for all income groups, and improved roads surrounding the area. CM to perform Jalabhishek at 3 Shiva Temples On the auspicious occasion of Maha Shivratri, CM Yogi, who is also the Gorakshpeethadhishwar, offered prayers at the Gorakhnath Temple. He performed Jalabhishek at three major Shiva temples in Gorakhpur — Mansarovar Temple, Mukteshwarnath Temple at Rajghat, and Piteshwarnath Shiva Temple in Bharohiya — praying for public welfare. On the eve of Maha Shivratri, he also visited the historically significant Mahadev Jharkhandi temple for darshan and worship. As per Nath tradition, Maha Shivratri holds special importance, and even after becoming Chief Minister, Yogi Adityanath continues to celebrate the festival in Gorakhpur, centered around the Gorakshpeeth. Tal Ring Road Project nears completion The Chief Minister also conducted a site inspection of the under-construction 4.8-kilometre Tal Ring Road project from Mohaddipur to Sahara Estate. Being developed by the Gorakhpur Development Authority under the Rapid Economic Development Scheme, the two-lane road is expected to improve traffic flow and enhance the beauty of the Tal area. The project is estimated to cost around Rs 28 crore and is likely to be completed by May 2026. The 12-metre-wide road will include a 7-metre-wide main carriageway and footpaths on both sides. The section along the Tal is being built using piling, concrete, and steel beams, with steel railings for safety and aesthetics. A proposal has also been sent to the government for Tal front development and construction of a boat jetty. Officials expect the project to significantly improve the city’s traffic management system once completed. Focus on education, environment, and infrastructure CM Yogi highlighted development in Jungle Kaudia with a new degree college named after Pujya Maharaj, educating over 2,000 students. Facilities for girls, youth, sports, and wrestling are now available. He emphasized clean air and environmental protection in Gorakhpur, contrasting it with Delhi’s high pollution levels, and noted the establishment of a forestry and horticulture university providing degrees linked to 100% employment guarantee. The CM also highlighted Sheesh Mahal-style facilities in the new Mandapam, improved roads to Lucknow and Varanasi, and enhanced infrastructure for public welfare.

stories.title: Naseem Solanki says, 'Zeher toh mein haste-haste pi gayi':SP MLA poetic flair in UP Assembly, alleges Lamborghini driver was intoxicated
stories.summary: 'Na mein giri, na meri ummedon ki minar giri, Par log mujhe girane mein kayi baar gire, Sawaal zeher ka nahi tha, woh toh mein haste-haste pi gayi Takleef logon ko tab hui, jab mein phir jeet gayi' Samajwadi Party MLA Naseem Solanki from Sisamau, Kanpur, recited this poetry in the Assembly on Thursday. She also raised the issue of the recent Lamborghini accident. She said that in the incident, the driver was allegedly intoxicated. She stated that rising drug addiction among young people is a serious concern. In the city, youth are increasingly falling prey to alcohol and narcotics. Those involved in this illegal trade are growing in number. Drug abuse is also spreading in areas around schools. Demand for women’s skill development centres Naseem said that the picture of the state appears different on paper compared to the reality on the ground. The Sisamau Assembly constituency continues to struggle with multiple problems. The most serious issues include women’s safety, rising incidents of molestation, crime and domestic violence, all of which are creating a sense of insecurity among women. She added that the city’s development infrastructure has deteriorated. Roads in the Sisamau constituency are repeatedly collapsing. Repair work is often delayed for days, causing inconvenience to residents. She said that until public grievances are addressed, claims of development remain incomplete. 5 key demands were placed before the House Naseem put forward five major demands- Naseem Solanki won the by-election over a year ago. Since then, she has spoken in the Assembly 11 times. This was the first occasion on which she recited poetry in the House. Concluding with her verse, she said- 'Jinke hausle sache hote hain, woh qaid mein rehkar bhi mukadar likhte hain…Toofano se keh do aukaat mein rahein, hum parinde nahi joh gharon mein qaid ho jaayein'

stories.title: Bride threatens groom on wedding night in Kanpur:Woman claims her love for another man; husband seeks police help after months of fear
stories.summary: On the wedding night in Kanpur, the bride threatened her husband. She said - Stay away from me. Don't touch me. I belong to someone else. If you touch me, you will lose your life. If you want what's good for you, send me to my boyfriend. For 2 months, the groom tried to convince the bride. But she didn't agree. One day, the bride put a noose around her neck. The young man somehow saved her. After this, the bride threatened him again. Two and a half months after the wedding, the frightened young man reached the police station. He pleaded with the police to save his life. The case is from the Ghatampur police station. A girl from a village in the Maharajpur police station area got married on November 23 to a boy from a village in the Sadh police station area. After the wedding, the bride reached her in-laws' house. The groom said that on the wedding night, he went to the bride. As soon as he tried to lift her veil, she stepped back. The bride told him to stay away from her. She said there is someone else in her life. This body and mind belong to him only. Don't even try to touch me. She said that she loves another boy. She wants to spend her life with him only. If you want to stay happy and want to live, then leave me. Drop me off at my boyfriend's house. I tried to convince her all night. But she didn't agree. She remained stubborn. I thought she would agree in a day or two. Every night, I tried to convince her. But she didn't agree. Young man said - I am in depression due to her threats The boy said - I have been trying to make her understand for two and a half months. But instead of understanding, she kept threatening me. I went into depression. I didn't tell anything to my family anything. On February 11, I was trying to make her understand, but she got angry. She threatened - If she can't be his (boyfriend's), she can't be anyone's. Then she went into the room. She locked the door from inside. She tried to take her life by hanging. When I saw this, I broke down the room door and saved her life. After this, my family learned the truth. Family members also tried to explain to her, but she didn't listen. On February 12, I reached the police station and filed a complaint. When she used to threaten me, I had recorded her threats on the phone. I have also given that recording to the police. Sadh Police Station in-charge Inspector Avanish Kumar Singh said that both families were called to the police station. No written complaint has been given by any party. Both families have been asked to resolve the matter through dialogue.

stories.title: What does SP want to achieve with Nasimuddin's entry?:Alliance fear or perception war between Owaisi and Mayawati
stories.summary: SP-Congress fought together in the 2024 Lok Sabha election in UP. Both are preparing to contest the 2027 assembly under the grand alliance banner. But in the discussions is Nasimuddin Siddiqui, who left Congress and is about to join SP. Why is SP going to include a major Congress leader in the party? Does SP fear losing the Muslim vote bank in 2027, or are they trying to find a counter to the potential Owaisi-Mayawati alliance? SP chief Akhilesh Yadav will induct Nasimuddin Siddiqui into the party on 15 February, along with several former MLAs, MPs, and workers from across districts. Ahead of the 2027 elections, SP aims to strengthen its Muslim support, which makes up about 19% of Uttar Pradesh’s voters and largely backs the party. While Azam Khan remains SP’s most prominent Muslim face, his legal troubles prevent him and his family from contesting elections. SP is expanding its base through the PDA (Backward, Dalit, Minority) formula, where Muslims play a decisive role. Bringing in Siddiqui is seen as a strategic move to reinforce Muslim confidence and counter the potential influence of Asaduddin Owaisi’s AIMIM, which is exploring alliances and planning to contest Muslim-majority seats. Through this induction, SP seeks to project unity and position itself as the strongest challenger to the BJP in the 2027 Assembly elections. If Owaisi contests it's a loss, if he doesn't then SP benefits In the 2024 Lok Sabha elections, SP and Congress contested together under the grand alliance. SP received massive support from Muslim votes, helping the party achieve its biggest success to date. Both parties are preparing to contest under the same banner in the 2027 assembly elections. However, there's a looming threat to the Muslim vote bank. Asaduddin Owaisi's AIMIM won more than 125 seats in the recent Maharashtra local body elections, including capturing SP's traditional strongholds in Muslim-majority areas like Govandi-Mankhurd in Mumbai. SP was reduced to just 2 seats. These results are a matter of concern for SP. In Maharashtra, AIMIM has breached SP's vote bank, where leaders like Abu Asim Azmi had been strong for a long time. Owaisi had openly targeted Akhilesh Yadav and said that when Muslim leadership emerges, Akhilesh's 'shop will close down'. AIMIM claims that SP and Congress consider Muslims only as a vote bank, don't give them representation. In UP's 2022 assembly elections, AIMIM contested on 100 seats but didn't win any. However, it damaged SP in several places. For example, SP lost the Kursi seat in Barabanki by 217 votes. While AIMIM got 8,541 votes. BJP benefited from this. When AIMIM did not field candidates in UP for the 2024 Lok Sabha, Muslim voters remained united and SP benefited. After victories in Bihar-Maharashtra, AIMIM has geared up for the 2027 UP Assembly elections. Its focus is on the western regions of UP where the Muslim population is higher. According to the 2022 CSDS-Lokniti survey, SP received 79% of Muslim votes while BJP got 8%. SP wants to gather all Muslim votes. In 2017, SP suffered losses due to division of Muslim votes BJP had returned to power in the state by winning the 2017 assembly elections. The division of Muslim votes was cited as a major reason then. At that time, Muslims were divided between BSP-SP. As a result, the BJP had won 62 out of 82 such Muslim-majority seats where Muslim voters constitute one-third of the population. Numbers show that the BJP benefited from the division of Muslim votes in about two dozen seats. These included Muzaffarnagar, Shamli, Saharanpur, Bareilly, Bijnor, Sardhana of Meerut, Khalilabad of Gorakhpur, Tanda of Ambedkar Nagar, Shravasti and Gainsari of Shravasti district, and Moradabad seat. BJP also won in Deoband, which has a Muslim population of 1.25 lakh. The Muslim community was split between SP's Mavia Ali and BSP's Majid Ali. From Faizabad's Rudauli seat, BJP's Ramchandra Yadav defeated SP's Abbas Ali Zaidi by 30 thousand votes. Similarly, other seats included Thana Bhawan seat of Shamli, Lucknow (East), Lucknow (Central), Aligarh, Siwalkhash, Nanpara, Shahabad, Bahedi, Firozabad, Chandpur, and Kundarki. In 2022, SP received strong support from Muslims Compared to 2017, SP received strong Muslim support in the 2022 assembly elections. According to the Lokniti-CSDS survey, SP received 77-79 percent of Muslim votes in this election. This was the reason that SP's vote bank reached 32 percent and its seat count increased to 111. While BSP had given the most tickets to Muslims. But it received only 6-7 percent of Muslim votes, and its vote bank fell from 22 to below 13 percent. Only one of its candidates, Umashankar Singh from Rasda, could win. In the 2024 Lok Sabha elections, SP received 90-92 percent Muslim support. Then SP, along with its alliance partner Congress won 43 seats in UP. This includes 6 Congress MPs. BSP is also trying to woo Muslims BSP has also been active for the last six months. Mayawati herself attended the Muslim Brotherhood meeting and openly offered that if the Muslim community supports her, she will defeat the BJP. She also argued that even with full Muslim support, SP is unable to defeat the BJP. Nasimuddin Siddiqui was in BSP before Congress. His political journey also started with BSP. He was most active in Western UP. In such a situation, the SP chief wants to counter BSP's influence through Siddiqui. Senior journalist Rajendra Kumar says - Nasimuddin was never a leader with mass support. Even in BSP, he could win an election only once. After that, he lost every election. It's a different matter that he remained influential in BSP and served as minister of several departments. His identity in BSP remained primarily as a fund manager. Nasimuddin Siddiqui's joining won't benefit SP much, but he himself could gain a significant advantage from it. He may be able to establish his son in politics. How much risk of dissatisfaction among old BSP members and Congress in SP Before Nasimuddin, many leaders, MLAs, and MPs in SP were once in BSP. However, they never had good relations with Nasimuddin while in BSP. Now that Nasimuddin Siddiqui is joining SP, it is inevitable for these leaders to feel uncomfortable. Sources connected to SP say that old BSP members, including Babu Singh Kushwaha, RK Chaudhary, Indrajit Saroj, Ram Achal Rajbhar, and Lalji Verma, are unhappy with the decision of Nasimuddin joining the party. However, due to it being the SP chief's decision, they are unable to openly oppose it. Second, like BSP, SP's other Muslim leaders are also not going to give importance to Nasimuddin. Everyone has their own support base in their respective areas. Many SP leaders are saying privately that they don't need a fund manager. But officially, everyone is avoiding saying anything. Regarding Congress's displeasure over Nasimuddin joining SP, Congress spokesperson Surendra Singh says that he had left the party long ago. Where he is going now and what he is doing should be his concern. Congress is focused on strengthening its organization. Why not aggressive against Congress, reason now revealed Nasimuddin was not aggressive against Congress. Even pictures of Congress leaders Rahul, Priyanka, and Sonia Gandhi are hung at his residence. Besides this, Kanshi Ram's picture is also hung at his residence. Nasimuddin Siddiqui had told Dainik Bhaskar that his intention was not to weaken Congress. Now, amid news of joining SP, it has become clear why he remained soft on Congress. SP and Congress have an alliance in UP. This alliance will continue in the 2027 assembly elections, as indicated by the national leaders of both parties. In such a situation, Nasimuddin was already cautious and was not making any comments about Congress that could become an issue for Congress. Nasimuddin Siddiqui's career was started as a railway contractor Nasimuddin Siddiqui's name has been prominent in Uttar Pradesh politics for a long time. Nasimuddin Siddiqui was born on June 4, 1959. There was no political background in the family. After leaving his army job due to his mother's illness, he became active in railway contracting. Around 1990, Nasimuddin came in contact with BSP founder Kanshi Ram. It started with the Palika (Municipal) elections. He joined BSP in 1984. In 1991, he was elected MLA for the first time from the Banda assembly seat. He was BSP's first Muslim MLA. Called Mini CM in BSP government Nasimuddin Siddiqui, once a powerful leader in the BSP and known as the “Mini CM” during the 2007–2012 Mayawati government, held 18 ministries and had major influence in party affairs. He later served as Leader of Opposition from 2012 to 2017 but was expelled by Mayawati in 2017. After forming his own party, he joined Congress in 2018 as a prominent Muslim face, but resigned on 24 January. Now, ahead of the assembly elections, he is set to join the Samajwadi Party on 15 February in the presence of Akhilesh Yadav.
