stories.title: Woman elopes with son-in-law, leaves him after 10 months:Accuses partner of abuse; regrets leaving children behind in Agra
stories.summary: Sapna Devi, who had eloped with son-in-law Rahul before daughter’s wedding, has returned in Aligarh after 10 months. She says she regrets leaving her children and now wants to live independently. Sapna has accused Rahul of harassment, while he claims she wanted to live with her brother-in-law Devendra. Devendra denies the allegations, calling Rahul a liar and questioning his intentions, noting that he ran away with his would-be mother-in-law instead of marrying her daughter. After returning from Bihar, Sapna approached multiple police stations. Following a local settlement, she stayed briefly at Devendra’s home but left on 13 February, and her current whereabouts are unknown. Devendra said - Wherever the police is calling, I am going and telling them that the talk of an affair between Sapna Devi and me is wrong. He says - A few days ago, I had an accident. I am a driver in Trans India, managing the family with great difficulty. My name has been forcefully dragged into this. Rahul should understand the difference between a mother-in-law and a mother; he has done a very dirty thing. Devendra says - When Sapna and Rahul left home, they both changed their mobile numbers. A few days ago, Sapna called. At that time, she was in the car, we talked for 2 to 3 days, but since our family members were angry with her, this contact was kept very limited. Rahul said - Did not marry, lived like husband and wife Rahul, who lives in Dado's Machhariya, said - I had not married Apna Devi; we were living like husband and wife. Black magic was performed on me. A black thread was tied on my foot. Living with Sapna was the biggest mistake of my life. I want to live a different life now. Sapna left me, that's okay, but now she should return my 2 lakh rupees, mangalsutra, ring, and mobile phone. Family also distanced themselves Rahul said that when he reached his village, Machhariya, after returning from Bihar, his family members refused to keep him at home. Currently, he is living outside the village, making ends meet. Wedding was to be on April 18, they ran away 12 days before Rahul says - Anita's daughter's wedding was scheduled for April 18, 2025. Before that, on April 6, Anita and I left Aligarh. We first went to Uttarakhand for some work, then came to the Bela area in the Sitamarhi district of Bihar. Here we rented a room. Got married in the temple. Rahul says - Sapna's family members started pressuring the police, then both of us voluntarily reached the Aligarh police station. People from both sides sat in one room, and after long discussions, it was agreed that the family would not trouble us anymore. We will live together. Sold clothes in Sitamarhi, fights started after 3 months We asked - When you left home, there were rumors that Anita was pregnant. To this Rahul says - Anita never got pregnant after our marriage; these are all baseless rumors. We asked - What did you do to run the household? Rahul says - We fell in love and got married. We didn't know anyone there, so I started selling clothes door to door. Some money started coming into the house, and everything was going well. We asked - So, when did the relationship turn sour? Rahul says - After 2 to 3 months, Anita started talking to her brother-in-law secretly. Gradually, her behavior also started changing. She started fighting with me over small things. I Money sent to sister's account, then she 'disappeared' We asked - Then what happened before dropping Anita home? Rahul says - About 5 days ago, Sapna asked to send 1500 rupees to her sister. I said I don't have money. After this there was a fight. After this, I first transferred 500 rupees, then 1 thousand rupees to her sister's account. Then everything was fine, but 5 days later Anita suddenly went 'missing' from home. Son-in-law said - Mother-in-law deceived, read the exact complaint Son-in-law Rahul filed a complaint at the Dado police station on Wednesday. In this, Rahul said - I work selling clothes by making rounds in Bihar. 15 days ago, my wife Anita contacted her brother-in-law. I have heard the audio recording of their phone conversation. In the audio, both were talking about living together. They had planned to poison me and run away together. On February 6, my wife Anita (previously mother-in-law) deceived me and left with her brother-in-law. She also took 2 lakh rupees in cash and jewelry with her. Therefore, my wife should be caught. Woman said - My decision turned out to be wrong After the case came to light in the media, Anita reached the police station on Thursday, February 12. She told the police - I left my children and went with my son-in-law. I deeply regret this now. Now I want to work and earn by living separately from Rahul. I want to live with my children, but Rahul has forbidden me from going to my children. Rahul beat me up, took away my jewelry and money. That's why I left him. The story of eloping with son-in-law from a year ago 1- Ran away with son-in-law 10 days before daughter's wedding Anita's first husband is Jitendra Kumar, and their daughter Shivani lives in the village Manoharpur Kayasth in the Madrak police station area. Jitendra had fixed his daughter's marriage on April 16, 2025, with Rahul, a resident of Riya Nagla village in Dado police station area. Rahul was a supervisor in a private company in Rudrapur, Uttarakhand. 10 days before the wedding, on April 6, 2025, Shivani's mother, Anita, suddenly disappeared from home. On the other hand, the groom-to-be, Rahul, also left his house, saying he was going to buy clothes, but did not return. As soon as they left Aligarh, both turned off their mobile phones. 2- After FIR was filed, surrendered at police station with son-in-law Family members searched extensively, but neither could be found. Five days later, Rahul called his father and said not to try to find him; he would not return. After this, Rahul's family learned that his mother-in-law-to-be was also missing. The family filed a complaint with the police. After this, the police conducted raids and search operations in several states, including Bihar. On April 18, both reached the police station and surrendered. Police took both into custody and interrogated them. 3- Refused to go to police station with husband, then started living with son-in-law Police tried to convince the woman and asked her to go with her husband, but she clearly refused. Anita said that she had been suppressing her desires for 20 years. She was mistreated over small matters. She could not tolerate all this anymore, so she left home. She said that she does not want to go with her husband now. After this, the police let both of them go. The woman had been living with her son-in-law since then.

stories.title: Devar-bhabhi caught on Chocolate Day:Duo murder husband and hang in Agra, family performs last rites considering suicide
stories.summary: “I had called my devar (brother-in-law) to celebrate Chocolate Day. Both of us were on the bed together. When my husband returned home and saw us, he became furious. That is why we had to kill him.” This is what a woman from Agra allegedly told police after she, along with her brother-in-law, murdered her husband. To make it appear like suicide, they later hanged the body. The family performed the last rites believing it was a case of suicide. The thirteenth-day ritual was being organised at home. During this, the women of the household grew suspicious of the wife’s behaviour. She did not appear grief-stricken. Instead, her attention seemed focused on her brother-in-law, Sundar. When the women questioned her and warned that the police could be informed, she broke down. Sundar’s mother later said she had no idea about the affair. “He used to speak on the phone at night. I didn’t know he was talking to his sister-in-law. He did wrong. He should not have killed. He will face punishment,” she said. Husband Lavkesh had returned home after a long day at work. He was tired. The door was not latched. As he was about to enter the room, he paused after hearing sounds from inside. Peering through the door, he allegedly saw his wife Gauri and his cousin Sundar together on the bed. Lavkesh became furious. However, mindful of family honour, he entered the room and angrily asked what was happening behind his back. Sundar tried to steady himself and looked towards Gauri. Both were frightened, knowing that once their affair became public, they would not be able to face society. Gauri pressed a pillow, Sundar held him down According to the police version, taking advantage of the tense moment, Sundar suddenly grabbed Lavkesh from behind and threw him onto the bed. To stop him from screaming, Gauri pressed a pillow over his face. Sundar held him down with force. Lavkesh struggled for about two minutes before going still. Afterwards, Sundar and Gauri sat on the floor near the bed, sweating despite the cold night. In another room, Lavkesh’s father, Suresh Chandra Tomar, was asleep. Sundar stepped out to check whether anyone had woken up and felt relieved to see his father still sleeping. They then decided to present the murder as suicide. Using a saree, they made a noose and tied it around Lavkesh’s neck. The other end was fixed to the fan hook, and the body was arranged to resemble a hanging. They adjusted his clothes and removed signs of struggle from the room. Relatives informed: ‘Lavkesh committed suicide’ By 2 am, everything was done. Sundar quietly returned to his own house, about 200 steps away. Gauri went to another room and pretended to sleep. At 6:30 am, Gauri began calling relatives, saying Lavkesh had committed suicide during the night. When his father entered the room and saw the body hanging, he believed it to be suicide. Gradually, friends and relatives gathered at the house. Neighbourhood women came and began mourning. Gauri sat among them. Sundar also joined the relatives, acting unaware. Even after the funeral, no one suspected foul play. Neither the police were informed nor was there any serious discussion. How Gauri was exposed On February 11, preparations were underway for the thirteenth-day ceremony. Women sat inside the house discussing why Lavkesh had taken such a step, especially as no suicide note had been found. While arrangements were being made outside, the women inside grew increasingly suspicious of Gauri’s behaviour. She did not seem visibly upset and appeared unusually attentive towards Sundar. The women informed a family member, and together they confronted her. They repeatedly asked what had happened on the night of February 9. Under mounting pressure and fear of police action, Gauri broke down and confessed that they had suffocated Lavkesh with a pillow and later hanged the body to stage suicide. Suresh Chandra then called the police. The saree used to make the noose was recovered from the house. Gauri was arrested from the home, while Sundar was arrested from a nearby market. Both have been sent to jail. What Sundar told police In custody, Sundar allegedly confessed. “On February 9 at around 11 pm, Gauri called me to celebrate Chocolate Day. Lavkesh usually returned home late, but that day he came early. That is how our affair was exposed. “Now I regret everything. I have lost both my love and my brother. The brother I grew up with is no longer in this world.” What the wife said... We didn't want to kill him, at that time we couldn't understand anything Gauri said in police custody - Lovekesh never misbehaved with me. Everyone at home is good people, Sundar is my brother-in-law, he is the son of my uncle-in-law Dharmendra Tomar. That's why there would be teasing incidents with him, he would also play pranks with me. Slowly I started liking all that. Our closeness increased. Sometimes he would come to my house, sometimes I would go to his house. Then one day Lovkesh read Sundar's messages on my phone. That's when he first became suspicious. On the night of February 9, Lovkesh went home early for this reason. We didn't want to kill him, but at that time we couldn't understand anything. Now know the village atmosphere People said - Sundar was from their family, so there was no suspicion After this incident, Dainik Bhaskar team reached Lodhai village in Ekta area of Agra. Here the villagers told that Lovkesh got married to Gauri on May 2, 2021. She is from Dholpur, Rajasthan. They also have a 3-year-old son. Villagers say - For a few months, Sundar was seen more with Gauri, but since he was a family member, who would suspect. Lovkesh was the only brother among 5 sisters in the house. After Lovkesh, whenever Gauri had to go somewhere, she would take Sundar along and he would do all her work there. Mother said - That 'murderer' will serve his punishment Sundar's mother Rekha Tomar says - No one knew that Sundar would do such a dirty thing. When he used to talk on the phone at night, I asked him many times who he was talking to, but he never told anything. He will serve punishment for whatever wrong he has done. All three of my sons work in electricity, the eldest brother works in electricity in Chandigarh and the second one in Guwahati. No one knew how long this had been going on between the two. After the incident, it was discovered that all this had been going on between them for four months. Brother-in-law said - Suspicion arose, how did she wake up at 4 AM when she usually wakes up at 10 AM We met Lovekesh's brother-in-law Sanjeev at home. He said - We received Gauri's call at 6 AM saying that Lovekesh had committed suicide. We were suspicious of Gauri because how did a girl who wakes up at 10 AM wake up at 4 AM that day? How did she find out first that Lovekesh had committed suicide? When she was asked about all this, she got nervous. After threatening to call the police, she confessed to the murder. Police statement Suspicion arose on the day of peace ritual, arrested and sent to jail DCP City Syed Ali Abbas says - Lovkush Tomar was married to Gauri 4 years ago. They have a 3-year-old child. Lovkush's father Suresh Chand Tomar works in Belanganj. On the morning of February 10, family members reported that Lovkush's body was found hanging from a fan. Thinking it was suicide, the family performed the cremation on February 10 itself. On February 11, there was a peace ritual at home. Family members became suspicious of Lovkush's wife Gauri's behavior. Family members began questioning her. What time did Lovkush go to sleep. Why did they fight. Police will come and investigate. Such conversations made Gauri very nervous. She confessed in front of family members that along with her cousin brother-in-law Sunder who lives in the village, she killed her husband and hung the body on the fan to make it look like suicide. Like her husband, Sunder is also an electrician.

stories.title: Pakistani woman arrested in Meerut:Living illegally in India for 30 years; also obtained fake voter ID cards
stories.summary: Police have arrested a Pakistani woman who has been living illegally in Meerut for the past 30 years. The entire case is from the Delhi Gate police station area of Meerut. She was living in the Nadir Ali Shah building. The woman is originally Pakistani. She has been living illegally in Meerut, India, for 30 years. A fake voter ID card was also found with the woman. Not only this, but she does not have Indian citizenship either. The woman is also accused of being an ISI agent, conducting espionage, and passing confidential information. Woman had filed complaint A woman and her daughter residing at Nadir Ali Kothi in Delhi Gate, Meerut, have been accused of living in Meerut for 30 years without citizenship. A woman resident of Delhi Gate complained to the SSP and SP City, accusing both of spying for ISI and passing confidential information. After the investigation confirmed the allegations, a report was filed at the Delhi Gate police station based on the woman's complaint. Marriage took place in 1988 Ruksana, wife of Ayaz Ahmad and resident of Kothi Atanas in Delhi Gate, said - Farhat Masood, son of Masood Ahmad, resident of Nadir Ali Building in Ali Kothi, went to Pakistan and married Pakistani citizen Saba aka Nazi in 1988. They had three children. In 1993, Saba went to Pakistan. There, she gave birth to her fourth daughter, Aiman Farhat, on May 25, 1993. On her return, she got Aiman Farhat's entry made on her Pakistani passport and came back to India. Got daughter admitted to Sophia School Here, Aiman was admitted to the prestigious Sophia School in Cantonment. Aiman Farhat was not given Indian citizenship. Saba and Aiman Farhat are Pakistani citizens till date. It is alleged that Saba prepared fake documents and got Aiman's fake passport. Saba got two voter cards made in her name as Saba Masood and Nazia Masood in the voter list. While both names belong to the same Pakistani woman. The mother-daughter duo has traveled abroad multiple times using fake passports. The woman alleges that Saba's Pakistani father, Hanif, is an ISI agent. She also accused Saba and Aiman of spying for ISI and setting up sleeper cells. She said - both collect information for ISI by moving around cantonment areas, army headquarters, and various ministries in Delhi. Allegations found to be true in the case SP City Ayush Vikram Singh said - A woman named Saba Farhat had come to India from Pakistan on a long-term visa. She was accused of traveling without permission and making a fake voter ID card. Some facts came to light during the investigation, and the allegations were found to be true. She will be arrested and presented in court on Tuesday. Other legal proceedings are underway. Accused of having links with Pakistan's intelligence agency The complaint also states that the mother-daughter allegedly created identification documents based on forged papers and used these for travel as well. Rukhsana has made serious allegations against Saba's family members of having connections with Pakistan's intelligence agency. There are also concerns about the mother-daughter gathering information from sensitive locations. Police officials said that a case has been registered. In this regard, documents are being thoroughly investigated, travel details and all citizenship-related records are being scrutinized. Further legal action will be taken based on the findings of the investigation. The woman's lawyer said - Police have wrongly arrested Saba Farhat because she had come to India legally from Pakistan. Her long-term visa is valid until 2027. Additionally, the police have shown such haste in making the arrest in this case that the FIR was registered on the 14th.

The Cyber Cell, Surveillance and Itaunja Police have arrested four accused, while the mastermind is absconding. Input Tax Credit (ITC) was sold to businesses through 16 bogus firms. The GST fraud came to light on a complaint from the Lucknow Income Tax Department. A case was registered based on Assistant Commissioner State Tax Abhimanyu Pathak's complaint regarding tax evasion through selling fake ITC via the fraudulent firm Swaraj Traders. Subsequently, four accused involved in tax evasion were arrested. DCP Crime Kamlesh Dixit said - Investigation revealed that Swaraj Traders, which showed sales of aluminium waste, ferrous waste, scrap, tube pipes, iron and steel after obtaining GSTIN on April 8, 2024, did not actually exist. The firm's registration was done using a fake rental agreement. Now read how the revelation happened... Investigation revealed that a gang was operating by creating more than 15 fake firms like Swaraj Traders. The gang included Tabassum, aka Gulchama,n aka Jahnavi Singh, wife of Narendra Singh from Saketnagar Juhi Colony, Prashant Benjwal (30) from Kalyanpur Kanpur, Sumit Saurabh (35), son of Jitendra Kumar from Indira Nagar Sector-11, and Daulat Ram, son of Badlu Ram from Naubasta Kanpur city. In the financial year 2024-25, tax worth Rs 52 lakh 266 was sold to other firms through ITC. Additional tax evasion of 19 lakhs People's Aadhaar, PAN, bank accounts, mobile numbers and addresses were collected through enticement. The gang leader, Ammar Ansari, would create fake rent agreements to obtain GST registration. Fake GST-R1 was filed in the firm's name to generate ITC. Prashant would create fake invoices and sell ITC for 1% commission. The investigation also revealed firms named SS Galaxy and SS Enterprises. Their owner, Sumit Saurabh, has been arrested. GST evasion of Rs 19,01,242 was done through these firms. As payment, two signed checks, one lakh in cash and one lakh were transferred to Swaraj Traders' account. The debit card of that account was recovered from Prashant and Tabassum. Now read who did what... Police said - Daulat Ram is a labourer in Kanpur. Provided documents for the lure of 20 thousand rupees. Tabassum used to run a tiffin service earlier. Got involved in a fake firm registration scheme due to greed for more earnings. Prashant Benjwal, who was involved in the gang, was previously a cashier at Vishal Mega Mart. Later quit his job and joined the gang. His job was to generate fake invoices and ITC. Tabassum and Prashant met at Vishal Mega Mart. Sumit Saurabh is the owner of the real firm, which used to buy bogus ITC for tax evasion. Sitapur resident Ammar Ansari is the gang leader. He handled the entire process of fake rent agreements and GST registration. He has previously been jailed for GST fraud. He is currently evading police arrest. A search is underway to find him. Formed gang due to greed for more money During interrogation, Tabassum revealed that her first marriage was to Ejaz Ahmad, who had sold her. After that, she married Narendra in Kanpur, but left him in 2017 after learning that he was already married. In 2020, she met Prashant, a cashier at V Mart in Kanpur. Prashant's salary was only 10 thousand rupees. Both started living together and started a tiffin service, but due to low income, they planned to earn more money in less time. During this time, both contacted Ammar Ansari and planned to sell ITC through fake GST. Accused used to take one lakh rupees per firm DCP said - Tabassum and Prashant would look for people who would provide their Aadhar cards, PAN cards, mobile numbers and bank accounts for creating fake firms. These documents were handed over to Ammar. Through which fake GST was registered. Tabassum and Prashant would receive one lakh rupees for each firm. Daulatram was made the owner of one of these firms.

stories.title: Suspended Bareilly magistrate targets PM Modi in Deoria:Says 'Will contest election against Modi'; claims BJP fuels Hindu-Muslim division
stories.summary: A major statement has come from the suspended City Magistrate of Bareilly, Alankar Agnihotri. In Deoria, he said, Prime Minister Modi will resign before 2029. If this doesn't happen and Modi contests from Varanasi in 2029, I will contest against him and defeat him. These people were badly defeated and humiliated in Ayodhya. They are going to lose in Kashi and Mathura in the coming time. Alankar Agnihotri had arrived at Maharani Chandika Hostel to attend the Mahapanchayat of Saman Nyay Sangharsh Samiti. There, he attacked PM Modi and Home Minister Shah. He also had a special conversation with Dainik Bhaskar. Read what else Alankar Agnihotri said... Major scam occurred in Har Ghar Nal Yojana across the country Alankar Agnihotri said - The biggest scam has occurred in the Har Ghar Nal Yojana across the country. Through this scheme, corruption money was shifted to Gujarat. In Lakhimpur Kheri, an empty tank collapsed. Fortunately, no one was there. In Mahoba, the new water tank started leaking. These things indicate corruption. Sanatani should strengthen their participation He said - All Sanatanis should ensure their strong participation in the Assembly and Lok Sabha. So that their voice can be raised effectively. No law can be made against their interests. These people will be sent back by making them do Dandi March again Alankar Agnihotri said - Neither the Prime Minister nor the Home Minister of the country spoke a word about UGC. A shameful incident happened with a woman in Delhi regarding this issue. There is a woman CM there, but not a single statement came from her. In the coming time, the OBC, Brahmin, Kshatriya, Vaishya, and Bhumihar communities of the country will unite and send them back by making them do the Dandi March on foot. The situation will not be the same as 2024. Major changes in the political landscape can be seen before that. I am preparing to form a new political party. This will be announced on February 23. Now read the conversation with Dainik Bhaskar Question- How will you unite the upper castes and Sanatani people in the country? Answer- Many universities have become battlegrounds in opposition to the UGC law in the country. Whether it's Banaras University or Delhi University, fighting has been instigated everywhere. The central government has worked to pit the General and OBC categories against each other under a divisive strategy. Their actions have come to light. People will not be misled by them anymore. The country is crying, protesting on the streets. Question: You announced forming a party. What is the strategy ahead? Answer: We will form our party incorporating the Sanatani culture. All paths will remain open for all Sananis who worship Ram-Krishna. Whether SC-ST, OBC, or general category, all people will be brought together. Question: Has Modi's craze ended? Answer: Not craze, their reality has come to the fore. The country has understood their intentions. They are shifting money to Gujarat by giving everything to Gujarati companies. These people were only creating a Hindu-Muslim divide in the country. But now everything has come to light. Question: Why did you resign when you could have served the upper caste society while in position? Answer: What services are those upper-caste people in positions able to do? So how could I have provided service? I had resigned from service, but those people suspended me out of frustration. If I had stayed in service bound by their guidelines, these people would have suspended me. That's why I resigned myself, because there are fools sitting on every branch here. The blindfold of blind faith that people of the country were wearing has broken. Now people understand their intentions. That's why I have also come to the field. If they contest against me in Banaras, I will defeat Prime Minister Modi and send him away.

stories.title: Groom returns ₹21 lakh dowry in Saharanpur:Engineer says marriage should not involve money; bride’s family gets emotional
stories.summary: In Saharanpur’s Chutmalpur, a groom returned ₹21 lakh given by the bride’s family during the wedding ceremony, saying marriage is a union of hearts and families, not a financial transaction. The incident took place on the night of February 14, when Praful Som and Sakshi Rana, both software engineers working in Noida, were getting married. During the jaimala ceremony, Praful took the microphone on stage and announced that he was respectfully returning the ₹21 lakh given by the bride’s father as shagun. He said that he and his family do not accept dowry in any form and only want the blessings of the bride’s family. Groom says marriage should not involve money Praful said, “Marriage is the union of two families and two hearts, not a transaction. We are both self-reliant. We do not want this relationship to become a medium of give and take. We respectfully return the ₹21 lakh given by Sakshi’s father.” He added that Sakshi was coming into their home not as a daughter-in-law but as a daughter, and her presence itself was the biggest blessing for the family. His announcement surprised the guests and soon turned into an emotional moment. Many people gathered near the stage and welcomed the decision with applause. Bride’s father accepts decision, praises groom’s family Sakshi’s father, Ravindra Rana, said he felt proud that his daughter was going to such a family. He respected the groom’s decision and took back the money. He said, “I am proud that my daughter has found such a family. They have taken only ₹1 as a symbolic gesture and refused everything else. I thank the groom and his family for setting an example.” Groom’s father, a police sub-inspector, supports decision Praful’s father, Yashpal Singh, who is a sub-inspector in Meerut Police, also supported his son’s decision. He said that as a police officer, he speaks about law and social responsibility, and it would be wrong to accept dowry. He said, “If we take dowry ourselves, how can we stop others? It is our duty to set the right example for society and the new generation.” His statement was also welcomed by the guests. Bride says she is proud of her new family After reaching her in-laws’ house, Sakshi shared her feelings and said she was proud to be part of a family that valued her education and values over money. She said, “I feel lucky to have such parents and in-laws. For my new family, the bride herself is the biggest dowry. This decision is a matter of pride and honour for both families.” She added that dowry-free marriages should be encouraged so that society moves towards equality and respect. Groom says dowry is a social evil Praful said the decision was taken jointly by him and his family before the wedding. He said dowry places financial pressure on families and promotes the wrong mindset that daughters are a burden. He said, “Relationships are built on respect, love and equality, not money. Marriage is a sacred bond, not a business. Both families together have given a message that daughters are not a burden but the pride of the house.” The couple’s decision has drawn appreciation from guests and locals, with many calling it an inspiring example against the dowry system.

stories.title: UP Evening Wrap:8 workers charred to death in Rajasthan's chemical factory blast; Naseemuddin Siddiqui joins SP more
stories.summary: Bhaskar English brings you the biggest news updates from Uttar Pradesh and around the world. Here are the top headlines: 1. 8 workers charred to death in Rajasthan's chemical factory blast 8 workers were burnt alive in a fire at a chemical factory in Bhiwadi (Khairthal–Tijara), and their bodies have been recovered. One worker is still believed to be trapped inside. 2. Naseemuddin Siddiqui joins SP; Akhilesh's remarks spark BSP reunion buzz Akhilesh Yadav inducted Naseemuddin Siddiqui in Lucknow, hinting at a shift in political equations in Uttar Pradesh. His comments on BSP triggered speculation about renewed ties with Mayawati and possible alliance recalculations. 3. Lucknow court gets bomb threat email; security sweep finds nothing suspicious An email warning of 12 RDX IEDs and naming LTTE and Pakistan’s ISI triggered a major security alert. Police, bomb squad and Cyber Cell investigation found no explosives; probe continues to trace the sender. 4. PM welcomes world leaders in India AI Impact Summit 2026 From presidents and prime ministers to tech CEOs and researchers, the world has landed in India’s capital for the India AI Impact Summit 2026, turning Bharat Mandapam into the centre of global AI conversations. 5. Mohan Bhagwat calls for Hindu unity above caste in Gorakhpur address The RSS chief urged focus on social cohesion, Sanatan values and grassroots leadership at the block level. He emphasised unity and harmony to strengthen cultural identity and collective community action. 6. Martyr laid to rest in Meerut; young son performs last rites amid grief Army Havaldar Rahul Bhadana, killed in a Himachal road accident, was cremated with full honours. Emotional scenes unfolded as his four-year-old son performed rituals; villagers gathered to pay tribute. 7. Rahman govt may order probe against Yunus The assets of the Chief Adviser of Bangladesh, Muhammad Yunus, saw a 11% rise after the coup witnessed by the country last year. This claim was made by the assets of ministers in the Mohammad Yunus government. 8. Shravasti robbery turns fatal; farmer killed before son, valuables looted Masked intruders stabbed farmer Nemraj Pathak to death and fled with jewellery and cash worth lakhs. Police registered murder and robbery cases, scanned CCTV and formed teams to track the suspects. 9. Retired soldier kills wife, son in Kanpur; dies by suicide on railway track Ex-serviceman Chet Ram Paswan allegedly shot his family before lying before a moving train. Police and forensic teams recovered bodies and launched an investigation into the motive behind the tragedy. 10. India's wholesale inflation rises to 10-month high Wholesale inflation (WPI) increased to 1.81% in January. Earlier in December, the wholesale inflation rate was 0.83%. This is the highest in 10 months. It was at 2.05% in March 2025. The commerce ministry released wholesale inflation figures on Monday, February 16, 2026.

stories.title: 11.5 lakh devotees reached Vishwanath Dham within 43 hours:Gulal offered in Sapt Rishi Aarti; darshan being conducted through 4 doors
stories.summary: On the auspicious occasion of Mahashivratri, an unprecedented crowd of devotees poured into Kashi Vishwanath Dham. In the last 43 hours, approximately 11.5 lakh devotees have visited Baba Vishwanath's court. Special arrangements have been made by the administration and temple management to manage the crowd systematically. Continuous darshan since Mahashivratri dawn The doors of Baba Vishwanath were opened for devotees from 3:15 AM on Mahashivratri dawn. Since then, the sequence of darshan and worship has been continuous. Devotees from India and abroad are bowing in Baba's court with chants of "Har-Har Mahadev". Entry through 4 gates Considering the large crowd of devotees, arrangements have been made for entry through all four gates of the temple. Devotees are being given smooth darshan by queuing them through different routes. Security arrangements are also tight to prevent any kind of disorder. Special four-time aarti A special aarti of Baba was performed four times on the occasion of Mahashivratri. A unique atmosphere of devotion prevailed from Mangla Aarti to afternoon, evening, and night aarti. During the Saptarishi Aarti, gulal was offered to Baba, which filled the entire temple premises with Shiva's presence. Prasad from temples across India and abroad was offered On this special occasion, Baba was offered prasad sent from 8 international and 54 major temples of the country. This event demonstrates Kashi's global spiritual significance. Prasad received from various pilgrimage sites was offered according to proper rituals. Administration alert, devotees enthusiastic Additional police force, NDRF, and volunteers have been deployed to control the crowd. Medical teams and emergency services are y. Great enthusiasm is being seen among the devotees, and all are having darshan with devotion and discipline.

stories.title: Minister’s ‘vote jihad’ claim in Varanasi proven false:CEO says, '9 duplicates found in 4,500'; notices issued to 1 crore people in UP
stories.summary: The UP Election Commission has completely denied Minister Ravindra Jaiswal's claim of vote jihad in Varanasi. Chief Electoral Officer (CEO) Navdeep Rinwa reached Varanasi on Monday. In the press conference, he said that the alleged list of fake voters provided by the minister had been investigated. In the first phase of verification, about 4500 voters were checked. Only 9 voters were found duplicate. He informed that DM Varanasi had received a list of a total of 9,000 names. The Minister had alleged deletion of one lakh votes. After which, a few names were found that were duplicates due to double form-filling or other reasons. The CEO said that notices are to be issued to a total of 3.26 crore voters, including 1.04 crore for 'no mapping' and 2.22 crore for 'logical discrepancies' in the draft list published on January 6. So far, about 1.09 crore notices have been issued. Along with issuing notices, the hearing process is moving quickly. Action will be taken after this. Understanding logical discrepancy and no mapping in simple language... Election team ready, final list to be released on April 10 Navdeep Rinwa said that the final voter list will be published on April 10, 2026. This list will be used as a permanent record for all future elections. The homework for voter list revision progress and upcoming phases has been completed. Filing fake forms confirmed, FIR will be registered The Chief Electoral Officer said that action will be taken according to rules only if the investigation proves that someone deliberately provided false information. No innocent voter will be harassed, and action will be taken only based on solid evidence. In the entire matter, the administration's priority is to maintain the accuracy of the voter list and maintain public trust. Citizens have been asked to check their names and details, and if there are any errors, get them corrected under the prescribed procedure. The Commission's effort is that the finally published list proves useful as a reliable and permanent document for all future elections. Notices are being sent to 1 crore 4 lakh people The Chief Electoral Officer said - notices are being sent to 1 crore 4 lakh people in UP. Action will also be taken after this. If anyone provides wrong forms or information to manipulate the system, action will be taken under Section 31. So far, 12 crore 55 lakh names have appeared in the first draft list. Work is ongoing to search and update those whose names are not included. Therefore, time has been extended by one month, and they will be added. Review is ongoing for names to be removed. Hearings have been completed on more than 86 lakh applications till date. Now read what allegations the minister had made... Minister Ravindra Jaiswal held a press conference in Varanasi on February 12. He questioned SIR's work. Said that the vote jihad is going on in Kashi. One lakh votes have been reduced from my assembly. This is all a game of Rahul's Congress party. Many married women aged 30 to 40 years are registered as voters under their father's name. Their names are registered two to three times at many booths. It's not that the address and father's name are different. All are same. They are also saved in the final list. This is a big irregularity. Ravindra Jaiswal submitted a memorandum to DM Satyendra Kumar regarding this voter discrepancy. He said - If we have caught 9200 out of 90 thousand, you should revise once so that the entire matter can be understood.

stories.title: Akhilesh Yadav says ‘weapons are ready, fielding is set’:Plays song ‘Dabdaba Bana Rahega’, claims BJP held a secret meeting
stories.summary: SP chief Akhilesh Yadav has accused the BJP of a conspiracy to cut votes. Speaking at a press conference in Lucknow on Monday, he said, 'It was decided in a secret meeting of the BJP that votes would be cut in every Lok Sabha constituency where SP has won. They got our own voters' votes cut using fake signatures of our city president. All this is happening in a planned manner. They are not winning the UP elections, so they are trying to entangle all of us by cutting votes.' Akhilesh said - The song 'Dabdaba' has been released. Whether there are Panchayat elections or not, at least listen to the song. Tomorrow, people from Delhi might come and say that socialists got the song made. That's why we have kept our weapons ready. We have set up the fielding perfectly. BJP finds joy in snatching rights. Akhilesh also played the song 'Dabdaba Bana Rahega' (Dominance will remain). After the song ended, Akhilesh said - People from Lucknow are making songs for people from Delhi. People's eyes are getting damaged in Gorakhpur. Who is taking care of Gorakhpur? Read Akhilesh's key points- 1- SP MLA's wife's vote was removed Akhilesh Yadav said that 16 voters' names were removed by filling Form-7 in the name of SP worker Nandlal. Votes were removed by forging the signatures of the city president. When a complaint was made to the District Magistrate, the DM stated that no such forms had been submitted. SP MLA Ziauddin Rizvi's wife's vote was removed. She was told that her name would only be added if "you arrange a meal." "SP has filled 47 Form 7s, BJP has filled 1789 Form 7s. Unknown individuals have filled 128659 Form 7s. These unknown individuals are all BJP members who are cutting the votes of the PDA community." 2- Targeted robbery of PDA voters is happening The SP chief said - When the data for Ayodhya was extracted, 181 notices were found, of which 76% are people associated with the PDA community. Data cannot lie, this is a targeted robbery of PDA votes. When SIR (Special Intensive Revision) has already been done, why is there a need to fill Form-7? 3- BJP finds joy in snatching rights Akhilesh said - BJP is trying to divert attention from the issues. They find joy in snatching rights and entitlements. Our demand is that information on how many forms were submitted at which booth, by whom, and on what basis, should be made public. The public is being diverted from issues like inflation, unemployment, farmers' issues, law and order, and the declining economy. He said that in a democracy, the poor only have their vote, and that right is being snatched away. 4- The fight is not just for the party, but to save democracy The SP chief said - SP MLAs will meet the Election Commission and submit a memorandum. If necessary, the doors of the court will also be knocked on. This fight is not just for the party, but for democracy and the right to equality given in the Constitution.

stories.title: 5 arrested for firing at Rohit Shetty’s residence in Mumbai:All accused from Uttar Pradesh; police cite Lawrence gang threat
stories.summary: Mumbai Police, in coordination with the Special Task Force (STF) of Haryana’s Jhajjar Bahadurgarh unit, have arrested four persons from Uttar Pradesh in connection with the firing at film producer Rohit Shetty’s residence. Police said the incident was carried out as part of an extortion attempt and that the accused are linked to the Lawrence Bishnoi gang. According to officials, three of the accused are residents of Agra and one is from Noida. They were apprehended by the STF with assistance from Mumbai Police and brought under custody for further investigation. Police said the accused were allegedly acting on instructions from members of the Lawrence gang and had been tasked with firing at the residences of film personalities to create fear and pressure them into paying extortion money. Earlier, on February 5, Mumbai Police had arrested another accused, identified as Asaram Fasale, in connection with the case. Investigators said Fasale had been working as a garage mechanic for the past four years and had links with the Lawrence gang. According to the police, Fasale allegedly supplied weapons used in the firing on the instructions of Shubham Lonkar, who is suspected to be a key operative in the gang. Officials said further investigation is under way to identify other persons involved and establish the wider network behind the extortion attempt. All accused are residents of Agra and Noida, UP The arrested accused have been identified as Ritik Yadav, Sunny, Sonu and Vishnu, residents of Bahabijoli, Agra and Deepak, resident of Sector-45 Sadarpur Noida. Vishnu was arrested from Agra while others were caught from Haryana. The accused had fled after the incident. STF In-charge Inspector Rakesh Kumar said that one case each is registered against the arrested accused - Ritik Yadav, Deepak, Sunny and Sonu. Cases have been registered against all under section 109 of BNS, sections 37(1), 37(2) of MPA and sections 3, 25 of Arms Act. Know what is the complete matter? On January 31st night around 12:45, a firing incident occurred outside film director Rohit Shetty's house in Mumbai's Juhu area. According to police, at least five rounds were fired during this time, one of which hit the glass of the gym built in the building. Also, after the attack, a screenshot went viral claiming that this was done by the Lawrence gang. This screenshot is from a Facebook post of an account named Shubham Lonkar Arju Bishnoi. However, Bhaskar App does not verify this. The post stated - Next time the bullet will hit the chest The post stated, "To all brothers, regarding the firing that happened today at film director Rohit Shetty's house (Shetty Tower) in Mumbai, we Shubham Lonkar, Arju Bishnoi, Hari Boxer, and Harman Sandhu take responsibility for it. We messaged him many times not to interfere in our work, but he didn't understand. This is just a small trailer for him. If he doesn't understand and follow our words again, then next time the bullet won't be fired outside the house, but inside his bedroom, on his chest." Further in the same post, it was written, "And a warning to Bollywood that reform while there's time, otherwise the consequences will be severe. We will make your condition worse than Baba Siddiqui. Those whom we have called, either fall in line while there's time, or there won't be enough places to hide. And to all our enemies, be ready, we'll meet soon. Note - There was one, there is one, and there will be only one Lawrence Bishnoi Gang." Who are Shubham Lonkar and Arju Bishnoi? Shubham Lonkar is considered a key operative of the Lawrence gang. Shubham is the main suspect and conspirator in the murder of NCP leader Baba Siddiqui (October 2024). He had also claimed responsibility for that murder on Facebook. Meanwhile, Arju Bishnoi is being described as an active member of the gang, who helps operate the gang's activities through social media and threats.

stories.summary: UP Politics: यूपी की राजनीति में इन दिनों एक बड़ा सवाल घूम रहा है। समाजवादी पार्टी के दिग्गज नेता आजम खान जेल में हैं। उनकी सेहत ठीक नहीं है और राजनीतिक भविष्य अनिश्चित लग रहा है। इसी बीच, पूर्व मंत्री नसीमुद्दीन सिद्दीकी ने सपा जॉइन कर ली है। वे पश्चिमी यूपी में मजबूत मुस्लिम चेहरा माने जाते हैं, खासकर मुजफ्फरनगर, शामली और बागपत इलाके में। वहीं अब सवाल उठ रहे हैं कि क्या अखिलेश यादव ने आजम खान के ‘पॉलिटिकल वैक्यूम’ को भरने के लिए सिद्दीकी को पार्टी में लिया है? या यह आजम के लिए एक ‘सॉफ्ट सिग्नल’ है कि जेल से बाहर आने पर उनकी सीट और प्रभाव सुरक्षित रहेगा? राजनीतिक जानकार कह रहे हैं कि PDA (पिछड़ा, दलित, अल्पसंख्यक) को मजबूत करने के नाम पर मुस्लिम वोट बैंक को ‘डायवर्सिफाई’ किया जा रहा है। आइए इस मुद्दे को विस्तार से समझते हैं।

stories.title: Martyred soldier laid to rest as son performs last rites:Huge crowd gathers to pay final tribute; deceased was posted in Jammu-Kashmir
stories.summary: The mortal remains of an Indian Army soldier, who was posted in Jammu and Kashmir, reached his home in Meerut on Monday. An emotional scene unfolded when his four-and-a-half-year-old son poured Ganga water into his mouth during the final farewell, leaving those present unable to hold back their tears. During the last rites, the young boy was seen alternately gazing at his father’s lifeless body and looking around at the crowd, as if trying to understand the moment. The soldier’s mother and wife were inconsolable, crying uncontrollably beside the body. His father stood silently, staring at his son for one last time, overwhelmed with grief. People from several nearby villages gathered to pay their final respects. As the funeral procession moved forward, residents showered flowers from their homes as a mark of honour. The air echoed with emotional slogans: “As long as the sun and moon endure, Rahul Fauji’s name will live on.” Accident during travel in Himachal Havaldar Rahul Bhadana (33) from Bhadauli village in Kithor was serving in the army and was posted in Akhnoor district of Jammu and Kashmir. According to information received from the army, soldier Rahul was on leave traveling in Himachal Pradesh. During the journey, he passed away in a road accident in Damtal. Farmer leader Pawan Gurjar said - Rahul Bhadana, son of his uncle Hem Singh Bhadana, joined the army in 2016. He was posted at various locations for 10 years. For the past few days, he was posted in the Akhnoor area of Jammu and Kashmir. He died in a road accident on Saturday. Information about the accident was sent by the army. Got married to Sonal 5.5 years ago Rahul got married to Sonal from Amroha about five and a half years ago. They have a four and a half year old son named Divyansh. Rahul was second among three brothers. He has four sisters who are in a terrible state crying.

stories.title: Lucknow court receive bomb threat:Security teams on alert after mail cites LTTE and Pakistan ISI
stories.summary: On Monday morning, Lucknow Court received a bomb threat via email. Upon receiving the information, the police administration went on high alert. Wazirganj police, along with dog and bomb squads, reached the site, and a thorough security check of the court premises was carried out. No suspicious objects or individuals were found. Earlier, similar checks had been conducted on Friday. Pakistan ISI and LTTE written in the email The email, sent around 8:38 AM from an Outlook ID under the name “Sunnia Dasan,” claimed that 12 RDX-based IEDs had been planted in the judges’ chambers, which would detonate soon. The email demanded that the implementation of the EWS reservation in Tamil Nadu be stopped and that the court be vacated by 12:15 PM. The message ended with a mention of LTTE and Pakistan ISI. Intensive search operation conducted in court premises Dog and bomb squads conducted detailed inspections inside and around the court complex. People entering and exiting the premises were screened, and police personnel were deployed at key points within the court for heightened security. Investigation continues, nothing suspicious found so far Preliminary investigations have not revealed any suspicious objects. Police and other security agencies are examining the matter seriously. Cyber Cell assistance is being sought to verify the authenticity of the email and trace its source. Strict security arrangements, police on alert mode All gates of the court have police personnel deployed. Security measures have been tightened, and officers are monitoring the situation continuously. Officials have stated that the situation will become clear only after a thorough investigation.

stories.title: 'Those who forgot, remind them they are Hindu':Mohan Bhagwat in Gorakhpur urges focus on Hindu society over caste
stories.summary: RSS Chief Mohan Bhagwat stated that those who have forgotten their identity must be reminded that they are Hindus, so that Hindu society can stand united. The Sangh speaks for the Hindu community because every person living in this country is connected to it. Hindu society believes that both our path and yours are valid. Within this society, different sects and traditions exist according to individual preferences. Bhagwat said that while paths may differ, the goal remains the same. He added that a society that follows this principle is truly Hindu. The name ‘Hindu’ is linked with India, and through this identity, Sanatan (eternal) consciousness will awaken. “We must fulfil our purpose,” said the RSS chief, addressing an enlightened public symposium at Yogiraj Gambhirnath Auditorium in Gorakhpur on the second day of his visit. Hindu is not a noun but an adjective Bhagwat said that the term ‘Hindu’ is not just a noun but grammatically an adjective describing qualities. It unites people and guides the society, which must function with tolerance and coordination. Acting for others, not personal gain, is the essence of Indian culture. Recognising this truth brings eternal joy. The world has no way to give happiness and peace to society He noted that India is a spiritually-minded nation where dharma forms part of daily conduct. Values and customs have been cultivated generation after generation, forming the basis of culture, which in turn shapes the nation. Understanding unity is essential, and the Sangh’s perspective is rooted entirely in Indian thought. Expectations from the organisation have grown, and the world looks at India with hopeful eyes, as no other model globally ensures social harmony and peace. Western thought had influenced India, attempting to fragment Indian knowledge and impose its own systems. Bhagwat emphasised that Indian knowledge and philosophy remain the solution to societal doubts and challenges. Had dinner with representatives of upper castes, OBCs and Dalit community after harmony meeting After the meeting, Bhagwat dined with representatives from upper-caste, OBC, and Dalit communities. He stressed that a society thrives on genuine connection, not self-interest. “While we focus on caste, we must work for the broader Hindu society. Without goodwill, no society functions, even with laws and police,” he said. He added that in foreign countries, human relationships often operate as transactions, whereas in India, they are rooted in belonging. India embraces diversity in customs and attire, yet unity exists within it. Women are viewed with care and affection, and life’s ultimate truth—understanding God—is the shared goal of society. Hold meetings two to three times at block level Celebrating 100 years of the RSS, Bhagwat urged organising 2–3 block-level meetings annually. He said, “We are part of Hindu society. Consider what we are doing and what more can be done.” Representatives of various castes and sects shared their views, and Bhagwat encouraged action within communities for the larger Hindu society. Gradually, this dialogue should expand, and each segment of society must develop strength independently of the Sangh. Bhagwat emphasised that local leaders must actively guide society, make decisions collectively, and correct errors together. “If the nation thrives, we thrive. Society is responsible, and the Sangh assists,” he said. On stage with Bhagwat were Prant Sanghchalak Dr. Mahendra Agarwal and former vice-chancellor Prof. Chandrashekhar, while Prant Karyavah Vinay introduced guests and Prant Intellectual Head Dr. Arvind Singh presented the agenda. RSS Chief on two-day visit to Lucknow from tomorrow Mohan Bhagwat will visit Lucknow on 17–18 February for a two-day programme marking the Sangh’s centenary, attending family meetings, social harmony discussions, youth dialogues, and the enlightened public symposium. Bhagwat's last 3 notable statements... December 13: Bhagwat said - It's time to live for India, not to die Mohan Bhagwat said that the country should be placed above everything. This is the time to live for India, not to die. We should only have devotion to our own country in our nation. Language like 'You will be broken into pieces' will not work here. Bhagwat had attended a ceremony in Andaman on December 13 marking the 115th anniversary of Damodar Savarkar's song 'Sagar Pran Talmala'. December 1: Bhagwat said - Now the country is getting its rightful place Bhagwat said that today Prime Minister Modi's words are carefully listened to on the world stage, and this shows India's growing global power. India is now gaining its rightful place in the world. Bhagwat was speaking at an event in Pune on December 1 marking 100 years of RSS. During this, he suggested that organizations should not just wait for anniversaries or centenaries, but should focus on completing their work within set timeframes. November 18: Bhagwat said - Not necessary to declare India a Hindu nation Mohan Bhagwat said - India and Hindu are one and the same. There is no need to declare India as a Hindu nation. Our civilization already makes this evident. During an event in Guwahati, Bhagwat said that whoever takes pride in India is a Hindu. stories.summary: Police have reached Bakharia village in Sen Paschim Para following reports of a shocking incident. A retired soldier, Chet Ram Paswan (51), allegedly shot his wife Sunita Verma (40) and their minor son Deep (16) with a licensed double-barrelled gun. After committing the murders, he reportedly rode a bike to the railway tracks near Kathogar-Imalipur underpass and lay down under a passing goods train, ending his own life. The incident occurred on Monday morning around 7:30 am. Police discovered the bodies at home after finding the door open and receiving no response to calls. The double-barrelled gun was found nearby. Police from Sen Paschim Para station, the DCP, and a forensic team have arrived at the scene. Authorities have sent the bodies for post-mortem and are investigating the reasons behind the murder-suicide, but the motive remains unclear.

stories.title: Pankaj Chaudhary to form new team in UP after Holi:Caste equations complicate plans, frontline squad crucial for votes
stories.summary: A major organisational reshuffle in the Uttar Pradesh unit of the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) is expected only after Holi. The first round of discussions regarding the new team of state president Pankaj Chaudhary has been completed. However, balancing caste and regional representation remains a sticking point. Final approval is likely only after further rounds of meetings from Lucknow to Delhi. Questions remain about whether the new team will bring real change or if old faces will simply shift positions. Will Pankaj Chaudhary’s first major team send a strong message ahead of the 2027 assembly elections, or will internal rivalries create fresh challenges for the party? New team critical ahead of 2027 elections Considering the 2027 assembly elections, the new team carries significant importance for both the government and the party organisation. Pankaj Chaudhary has completed two months as UP president. His biggest challenge is preparing for the elections, including building his new team while maintaining caste and regional balance and keeping senior leaders satisfied. Sources indicate that Pankaj Chaudhary and BJP general secretary Organisation, Dharmapal Singh, have already held initial discussions about the state team. It has been decided that there will not be a major overhaul. Experienced office-bearers will largely be retained, although their responsibilities may shift. Some longstanding team members may leave, but provisions are being made to accommodate them in government or national-level positions. Why is the new team more important? The new team will bear full responsibility for the 2027 assembly elections. This will be the first assembly election for both Pankaj Chaudhary and Dharmapal Singh in UP, though Dharmapal Singh brings experience from the Jharkhand elections. The team will handle election campaigning, management, membership drives, and rallies. It will also be responsible for implementing central and state leadership decisions on the ground. Political analysts note that state office-bearers play a ministerial-level role during election years, which is why many senior leaders wish to remain in their positions, while new contenders are vying hard to secure spots in the team. Who is responsible for deciding the team? Know where officials are to be chosen in the organization? Several important positions will see new appointments, including state vice-presidents, general secretaries, and ministers, with increased female representation. New presidents will be appointed for six organisational zones. Some previous team members will retain positions in the state team. Additionally, 14 districts will receive new district presidents, and the state presidents of the Youth and Women’s wings will also be changed. Political appointments in municipal bodies, commissions, corporations, and boards are expected to follow soon. Now learn about the contenders The new UP state team will see strong influence from Defence Minister Rajnath Singh’s political legacy. His elder son Pankaj Singh currently serves as state vice-president, while younger son Neeraj Singh is active in the organisation. The final decision on which son will secure a key position rests with Rajnath Singh. Youth Morcha President Women's Front President Know where the problem lies, what's the challenge? Political activity is intense from Lucknow to Delhi regarding the team’s formation. Contenders are meeting top leadership in Delhi while seeking RSS support in Lucknow. Most candidates are from Brahmin and Thakur communities, making caste balance a key challenge. Female representation is also a priority. To prevent dissatisfaction, the party is reportedly considering allocating a key post to the Brahmin community to balance caste and gender equations. Pankaj Chaudhary faces the challenge of forming a team that can deliver electoral victory. Analysts note that issues such as discontent among upper-caste groups due to UGC matters, Kurmi-Lodh tensions, and other caste and political calculations must be factored in. With five state elections slated next year, including UP, forming a strong, balanced team becomes crucial. BJP must also respond to Mayawati’s proactive engagement with Dalit and Brahmin voters. The party’s commitment to “Sabka Saath, Sabka Vikas” must now be reflected in appointments of senior Dalit leaders like Vidyasagar Sonkar, Kaushal Kishore, and Vinod Sonkar to ensure outreach and credibility. Balancing political equations Senior political analyst Virendra Nath Bhatt notes that Pankaj Chaudhary must account for changing social equations after UGC issues, Brahmin dissatisfaction, and intra-party conflicts while maintaining caste and regional balance. Other controversies, including Shankaracharya Avimukteshwaranand and Alankar Agnihotri, must also be navigated carefully. Failure to resolve these issues on time could create challenges for the upcoming elections.

stories.title: Robbery in Shravasti, father slain before son's eyes:Intruders attack with knives; dacoity of cash and jewellery worth lakhs
stories.summary: In Shravasti, masked intruders entered a house and brutally killed a farmer in front of his son before fleeing with gold and cash. According to the family, around 3 a.m. on Sunday, four masked men broke into the home. The farmer woke up on hearing the noise. He raised an alarm and tried to confront the intruders. Hearing the commotion, his wife and son also woke up. The son ran to the room, but the assailants caught him. In front of him, the men stabbed his father multiple times. Witnessing this, the woman hid under the bed in fear. After the intruders left, the woman shouted for help and alerted neighbours. Police were subsequently informed. Authorities are currently reviewing CCTV footage from the surrounding area. The incident occurred in the Hardatt Nagar Girant police jurisdiction. Neighbours find farmer's body When neighbours arrived, they found the farmer’s body covered in blood, lying on the bed. The intruders fled with jewellery worth several lakhs. The family remains devastated following the murder. Farmer's house outside the village, only 3 people in the home Bhajore Purwa village, located about 30 km from the district headquarters, was home to 49-year-old farmer Nemraj Pathak, who lived with his son Sunil and daughter-in-law Lakshmi. Nemraj’s wife had passed away five years ago. He was the third among his brothers, with another brother living in the village. Nemraj had built a house outside the main village. His son’s marriage had taken place about two years ago. Daughter-in-law said - I remained hidden under the bed out of fear Lakshmi said, “I hid under the bed out of fear. I saw the legs of four intruders. Around 3 a.m., the robbers entered the house while my husband and I were in another room. When my father-in-law screamed, my husband ran to check, and the intruders caught him. I stayed under the bed, terrified.” She added, “In front of my husband, they murdered my father-in-law. I could see the four intruders’ legs from under the bed. They ransacked the house, took all the jewellery, and left. After they left, I screamed and called the neighbours, who informed the police.” SP says - Accused will be arrested soon Superintendent of Police Rahul Bhati arrived at the scene with his team after receiving news of the murder and robbery. The site was inspected and forensic teams collected evidence. The SP confirmed that a case of murder and robbery has been registered against four suspects based on the son’s statement. CCTV footage from nearby areas is being reviewed. Special teams have been formed to track and apprehend the suspects, and the village has been secured with additional police presence.

stories.title: Cong leader Nasimuddin's son helps his entry into SP:Akhilesh's common friend plays crucial role, steers political shift in West UP
stories.summary: Former Congress leader and once-powerful BSP minister Naseemuddin Siddiqui joined the Samajwadi Party (SP) on Sunday. Known as bitter rivals before 2017, the big question after he donned the red cap was: what’s the inside story behind his joining SP? How did this surprise unfold? Did the two leaders speak directly, or was there mediation? If mediated, where did the talks begin? How did it gain momentum? What are the potential gains and risks for SP? What could Naseemuddin gain personally? Dainik Bhaskar tried to find answers to all these questions. Read this special report… A close friend of Naseemuddin’s son Afzal spoke on condition of anonymity. He said that after SP’s success in the 2024 Lok Sabha elections, Naseemuddin was inclined to join the party. A key role was played by Akhilesh Yadav and Afzal’s mutual friend, businessman Rehan. Rehaan is Akhilesh's school time friend Rehaan is Akhilesh's friend from when they were studying in Mysore. Akhilesh Yadav went from Mysore to Australia and then returned to Lucknow. However, his friendship with Rehaan not only remained intact but grew stronger. Rehaan settled in Mumbai. Here he met Nasimuddin's son Afzal. Their friendship also flourished greatly. Afzal praised Akhilesh to Rehan, who in turn called him a visionary leader and a long-term player. In passing, he said, “Ask your father; if he agrees, I’ll take it forward.” That was how the discussions began. Nasimuddin met Akhilesh with Afzal Around six months ago, Afzal met Akhilesh. Later, Naseemuddin, Afzal, and Akhilesh met in Delhi. Continuous talks followed, and it was decided that Naseemuddin would join SP at the start of 2026. The day arrived on 15 February, when he publicly joined the party. Many BSP leaders gradually becoming SP members In 2019, despite the SP-BSP alliance, the Lok Sabha elections were lost. When BSP unilaterally decided to break the alliance, Akhilesh felt the greatest disappointment. This prompted SP to launch “Operation BSP.” Gradually, major BSP leaders began joining SP, including Lalji Verma, Ram Achal Rajbhar, Indrajeet Saroj, Swami Prasad Maurya, Babu Singh Kushwaha, Ram Shiromani Verma, RK Chaudhary, Ram Prasad Chaudhary, Tribhuvan Dutt, and Sukhdev Rajbhar. Naseemuddin Siddiqui had earlier left BSP for Congress. After SP’s success in attracting BSP leaders in 2022 and 2024, Naseemuddin realised joining Congress had been a misstep, though he did not publicly admit it. Meanwhile, his son Afzal Siddiqui had already entered politics. Know whether SP will benefit or lose from Nasimuddin's arrival Senior journalist Siddharth Kalhans says perception matters in elections. Naseemuddin has handled 18 departments as a minister and managed BSP’s organisational responsibilities. Akhilesh highlighted in his address that Naseemuddin had experience across multiple governments, signalling long experience. Naseemuddin also demonstrated that even while in Congress, a large number of BSP supporters aligned with him, which benefits Akhilesh’s perception. He stressed that he is junior to many former BSP leaders already in SP, aiming to resolve any disputes over rank. Nasimuddin joined SP, but what's the future now Political expert Ashok Tripathi says SP gains little beyond adding a senior leader, but Naseemuddin benefits, including planning for his children’s future. While in Congress, he had to fight for tickets. Even now, with SP, he may need to negotiate for seats. Winning was uncertain, but joining SP offers a better chance. Many leaders joined SP along with Naseemuddin, including his wife and son Afzal. Given his stature, he is likely to be appointed party general secretary, a post he held in BSP as well. On 15 February, Naseemuddin officially joined SP.

stories.title: Weather to deteriorate again in UP, 2-day rain alert:Winds at 40 km/h, Banda records 31°C
stories.summary: In Uttar Pradesh, the cold is gradually retreating. Currently, chilly conditions are only being felt in the mornings and nights, while daytime sees bright sunshine. However, the weather is set to deteriorate again, as the Meteorological Department has issued a fresh rain alert. Lucknow scientist Atul Singh said- Western disturbance is becoming active again. Due to this, it may rain in some parts of the state on February 17 and 18. Winds will also blow at a speed of 30 to 40 kilometers per hour. On Sunday, Banda recorded the highest temperature in the state at 31.2°C, followed by Jhansi at 30°C. The weather department has forecast that after 18th February, both maximum and minimum temperatures will rise by 2–3°C. By the end of February, the cold will completely leave Uttar Pradesh. Crops will be damaged if it rains If heavy rain accompanied by strong winds occurs, wheat and mustard crops may be damaged. The grains could weaken, affecting yield. Therefore, the Meteorological Department has advised farmers to remain alert and avoid keeping crops exposed in open areas. How the weather has been so far Mahesh Palawat, a meteorologist at Skymet Weather, Noida, said: “Compared to the past two years, winter was milder this time in UP. Maximum and minimum temperatures in December–January were above average. Between 1st January and 11th February, there was a 36% decrease in cold spells. Extreme cold was not observed due to La Niña not being active.” Mohammed Danish from the Lucknow Meteorological Centre added that the western disturbance was less active this winter, leading to below-normal rainfall during the cold season. Professor Manoj Shrivastava from BHU said: “The cold is now in its final phase. Temperatures will gradually rise in the coming days. We are now in the spring season. For the next 2–3 weeks, the weather will remain relatively stable, with mild chill in mornings and nights, while afternoons will feel warm.” According to Mahesh Palawat, light drizzle may be seen around 18th February in several districts including Hathras, Mathura, Prayagraj, Varanasi, Banda, Lalitpur, and Jhansi. stories.title: Crore-worth Lamborghini, 6 injured; bail in 7 hours:What law says how rare a supercar is in India
stories.summary: On February 8th, a speeding Lamborghini worth 14 crores ran over people on VIP Road in Kanpur. Being a supercar and driven by a billionaire's son, the case gained a lot of attention, but questions are being raised about the subsequent police action and court release of the accused within 7 hours. The most discussed topic is about the alleged driver Mohan, who claimed the car had 9 gears. People are raising various questions about this on social media. Why was bail needed from court in such an accident, why did police ask for 14-day remand, why did court reject it, what were the sections and can they be changed? How legal are supercars like Lamborghini on city roads? What are its features and how many are available in UP? Read the answers to these questions in Bhaskar Explainer... First read what is the matter? A Lamborghini accident occurred on February 8 in Kanpur's VIP Road area. After this, tobacco businessman KK Mishra made all efforts to save his only son Shivam Mishra. First, immediately after the accident, KK Mishra got his son removed from the spot. In conversation with the media, he claimed that his son was not driving the car. After this, Police Commissioner Raghuvir Lal came before the press and said that the investigation has confirmed that Shivam Mishra was driving the Lamborghini car at the time of the accident. On February 11, a person named Mohan reached Kanpur court and claimed to be the driver of the car at the time of the accident. However, the court rejected Mohan's petition. Police arrested Shivam Mishra on February 12, but he was released within about 7 hours. Question: Does a Lamborghini have 9 gears? Answer: No! This question arose because in the Kanpur accident, the driver Mohan, who allegedly claimed to be the accused, had stated this. After this, the truth came out and then Shivam was arrested. Lamborghini is also called 'Lambo'. Generally it has 7 gears, which in auto language is called 7-speed transmission. Some Italian brand cars also come with 8-speed transmission. The Lamborghini Revuelto that accused Shivam Mishra was driving at the time of the incident comes with an 8-speed dual-clutch transmission (DCT). Its gear system is extremely smooth and fast. Question: Which sections did the police impose? Answer: In this case, despite witness statements coming forward, police had registered a case against unknown persons. Sections 281, 125(a), 125(b) and 324(4) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) were imposed. This case is related to negligent driving. Section 281 (BNS): Driving vehicle at high speed or negligently. Section 125(a) and 125(b) (BNS): Committing acts that endanger the life or personal safety of others. Section 324(4) (BNS): Causing injury recklessly through a dangerous object (like a vehicle). Question: How did Shivam Mishra get bail? Answer: Allahabad High Court Advocate Neeraj Pandey explains that typically in road accident cases, sections related to reckless driving are applied, which are bailable offenses. Senior advocate Naresh Chandra Tripathi, who appeared for Shivam Mishra in Kanpur court, said that police had not recorded proper reasons for arrest, especially when the crimes carried provisions for less than 7 years imprisonment. He argued in court that this arrest violates Supreme Court guidelines and provisions of the Indian Civil Protection Code (BNSS). Question: Why did the court reject the remand? Answer: Because legally, police could not establish grounds for police remand. Accused Shivam Mishra's lawyer Anant Sharma said - police had asked for 14 days remand in court. The judge asked why remand was needed when all sections were bailable? The investigating officer could not give any solid answer to this. Due to this, the court rejected the remand application. Then after paying a bail bond of 20 thousand rupees, police released him. Question: What mistake did the police make? Answer: Former DGP Vikram Singh has pointed out serious flaws in this case. He says why section 238 was not applied in the case, when the angle of evidence tampering could have emerged from the evidence. He also raised the question of how the accused was allowed to go to Delhi despite being underground for four days. In this case, deliberately lighter sections were applied, which gave relief to the accused. Vikram Singh also raised the question that even after being present, when Shivam's father said that Shivam was not driving the car, why was no legal section imposed against his father. He says that the police appeared overly lenient in the entire matter, therefore departmental action should be taken against the responsible officers. However, Police Commissioner Raghuvir Lal said that the investigation has made it clear that Shivam was in the driver's seat, which has increased confidence in police credibility and investigation process. The police should still conduct strict questioning in this case. Question: Can police add sections later? Answer: Allahabad High Court Advocate Neeraj Pandey explains that if new and solid evidence emerges during investigation that can prove the case is not just about negligence but a more serious crime, the police can modify existing sections or add new sections. However, for this to happen, it is necessary that the new evidence is legally strong and sustainable in court. Question: Is it valid to drive a supercar like Lamborghini on the road? Answer: Yes, if such cars are registered with RTO in the country, have valid number plates, insurance, pollution certificate and are being driven with a driving license then it is valid. However, there are some conditions associated with it, such as the vehicle should not have any illegal modifications (engine, ECU, silencer etc). Following speed limits and traffic rules is mandatory. In case of rash or negligent driving, action can be taken under Motor Vehicle Act and Indian Penal Code (IPC). Experts say that the law does not look at the car's brand or price, but rather the driver's behavior. When driven within the rules, a supercar is considered as valid as a normal vehicle. Lamborghini-related accidents in India Apart from the Kanpur case, in Mumbai, police had seized a Lamborghini because it was running at speeds over 200 km/h, which was much higher than the prescribed limit. In Bengaluru on August 3, 2025, a video of a Lamborghini Aventador's engine catching fire while running also went viral. However, no one was seriously injured in this incident. In addition, many accidents have occurred abroad due to high-speed driving of supercars like Lamborghini. These include incidents of losing control of the car, getting airborne, and causing severe damage. These cases clearly show that very high speed itself is a major hazard.
