stories.title: Rejected marriage, blocked his number:Father claims Sumit continued calling daughter repeatedly
stories.summary: Rekha did not want to marry Sumit, and the two had separated about a year ago. She had also informed her family about the breakup. Despite this, Sumit continued to call her repeatedly. Frustrated by his persistent calls, Rekha eventually blocked his number. This was stated by Rekha’s father, Dev Chandra Kant, whose daughter was found dead in a car in Noida alongside her former partner. He said, "On February 13, Rekha told her mother on the phone that she would reach home in 15 minutes and not to prepare food for her. But she never returned home. The next day her dead body was found in the afternoon." Rekha did not like Sumit's behavior Dev Chandra Kant said, "Rekha found Sumit's behavior strange. She wanted to maintain distance from him. About a year ago, she had told this to her mother. After this, we explained to Rekha. Then Rekha clearly told Sumit that she does not want to marry him." "Despite this, Sumit kept trying to convince her by calling repeatedly. Rekha was troubled by his constant calls, so she blocked Sumit's number," he added. Asked to talk to brother by calling In May 2025, Sumit called Rekha again, but the call was not received. After this, he called Rekha's brother and brother-in-law requesting to talk to her, but could not speak. Meanwhile, the girl's family was looking for a groom for Rekha. Marriage proposals were being discussed at several places. Her engagement and wedding date were about to be fixed soon. On February 13, Rekha went to office as usual. Around 7:30 in the evening, her mother called and asked when she was coming home. Rekha said that she had left the office and would reach home in 15-20 minutes, asking not to prepare food for her. Rekha used to reach home on time daily, but that day she did not return until late night. Even after calling several times, her call was not received. When Sumit was called, his mobile was found switched off. After this, I filed a missing person report at Noida Sector-58 police station late at night. The next afternoon, we received a phone call informing that Sumit and Rekha's dead bodies were found in a car. Now read the full story... The affair began with school friendship Sumit and Rekha first met at the public school in Trilokpuri. They studied 10th and 12th together. They were in the same campus, conversations began, which turned into a deep relationship. Both families were open-minded, so no one objected to them visiting each other's homes for academic preparations. Initially, they would visit each other's homes only for studies. But later they started participating in family weddings and events as well. The relationship was so close that family members started taking it as routine. Not just studies, Sumit and Rekha shared similar interests. Sumit was a good right-handed batsman. He used to play in events across UP, Madhya Pradesh, Rajasthan and Gujarat. Rekha also liked cricket. She would often talk on the phone. Rekha got a job, Sumit started water supply business After 12th, Rekha did B.Com in graduation. Then she started working in Sector-62. Meanwhile, Sumit set up a water plant with his father's help. Sumit's father Rajiv works as a health inspector in Delhi MCD (Delhi Municipal Corporation). Sumit started supplying water to different societies. Along with this, he continued playing cricket. However, he earned good money. Meanwhile, Sumit started making life plans with Rekha. Both wanted to get married. Sumit's brother said - my brother bought a 1 crore flat in Noida. He wanted to gift it to Rekha. He would give Rekha branded gifts every day. He would pick up and drop Rekha from her office in Sector-62 by car every day. Everything was going well. Cricket career ruined after accident The first U-turn in this love story came in 2019. Sumit had a road accident in Noida's Sector-107. Sumit was badly injured in this. The doctor said that now you cannot go into sports. During this time, Rekha stayed with him from hospital to home. It took him 6 to 7 months to recover. This was the period when both families learned about their love. The biggest obstacle in this affair was their community. Because Sumit was from the Valmiki community, while Rekha was Kayasth. The tension between upper and lower castes had now come between their relationship. Sumit's family was ready for this marriage, but Rekha's family did not want to give their daughter to a lower caste. They slowly started explaining to Rekha that if you marry Sumit, how will you face society. Sumit's brother Sachin alleges - After this, Rekha's family members forbade Sumit from coming to their house. If Sumit was even seen around the house, they would threaten him. This went on for a long time, but there was never a fight between the two families. U-turn came in 2025 Cousin brother threatened - If you harass sister, I will file an FIR According to the family, in early 2025, Sumit was caught near the house by Rekha's family members. The cousin brother threatened that stay away from Rekha. Otherwise, they would file a molestation case with the police. Some chats from that time have also been received by Dainik Bhaskar. In which Sumit is apologizing. He is saying that I made a mistake, now I won't meet. Please don't file a complaint. According to the family, after this incident Rekha also stopped answering Sumit's calls. Sumit had given in writing to her family- I have no relationship with Rekha. If I harass or trouble her in any way, action should be taken against me. I will be personally responsible for this. Marriage stuck due to caste issues, Sumit became troubled However, even after all this happened, both continued to meet, Sumit remained troubled because his marriage to Rekha wasn't happening just because of caste issues. Meanwhile, Rekha also couldn't bear to see her friend troubled. On February 13th at 3 PM, Sumit left home in his car. At 3:39 PM, he messaged Rekha's mobile. He wrote - I am going to die. Rekha messaged him back, then he reached Rekha's office in Noida. Rekha came out of the office and sat in his car. According to family members, Rekha used to return home by 6 PM every evening, but that day she didn't reach home till night. Everyone was worried, they checked with the office. They found out that she had left with someone in a car. The family suspected Sumit. They contacted Sumit's house and learned that he was also not at his home. After this, both families went to the police. A missing persons report was filed at Noida Sector-58 police station. Sumit's phone had been switched off since 6 PM, while Rekha's mobile was on until the morning of February 14th, but she was not receiving anyone's calls. Now the story of death Bodies of both found in car at 1:30 On February 14 at 1:30 PM, Sector-39 police station found a white Altroz car. The car was locked from inside, so police broke the glass to open the gate. Inside, Sumit and Rekha's bodies were found. Sumit had a pistol in his hand, looking at the circumstances it appeared that Sumit shot Rekha, then committed suicide. Both had bullet wounds to their heads. Two shells were lying beside them. After conducting the post-mortem of Sumit and Rekha, police handed over the bodies to their families. Sumit's family performed his last rites in Delhi. Meanwhile, Rekha's last rites were performed in Sector 94 of Noida. DCP says - No signs of physical altercation Noida DCP Yamuna Prasad said - Post-mortem reports of both have been received. The cause of death is head injury. No other injury marks or signs of physical altercation were found on the body. The case is being investigated from every angle. After post-mortem, both Sumit and Rekha's last rites were performed. Sumit's last rites were performed in Delhi, while Rekha's were performed in Noida's Sector-94. Family members have completely dismissed the claim of threats being made through ISD calls. They say that when Rekha was missing, Sumit's family members were called and informed about filing an FIR with the police.

stories.title: Akhilesh Yadav targets Centre, UP government during Fatehpur visit:SP chief questions US trade deal; takes swipe at CM’s Japan tour
stories.summary: Samajwadi Party president and former Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Akhilesh Yadav on Friday launched a sharp attack on the Centre and the BJP-led State government during his visit to Fatehpur, raising concerns over the India-US trade agreement, the Shankaracharya controversy, and the law-and-order situation in Uttar Pradesh. Addressing party workers and speaking to the media, Mr. Yadav alleged that the trade deal with the United States would harm farmers and weaken domestic agriculture. He claimed the agreement would open Indian markets to American agricultural products and animal feed, affecting local producers. Mr. Yadav has earlier demanded transparency from the Centre on the deal, warning that it could adversely impact farmers, labourers and industries and create uncertainty for employment. He also took a swipe at the BJP leadership, alleging that concessions made under the agreement would lead to increased imports of animal feed, edible oil and agricultural products from the United States. Criticism over Shankaracharya controversy Mr. Yadav criticised the Uttar Pradesh government over the ongoing controversy involving Shankaracharya Swami Avimukteshwaranand, which emerged after alleged police action and remarks during the Magh Mela in Prayagraj. The issue has led to political confrontation between the ruling BJP and the Opposition in the State Assembly. He said the Deputy Chief Minister’s post was not a constitutional position and accused the government of failing to protect the dignity of religious figures. Referring to the Magh Mela incident, he termed the alleged insult to Batuks and Brahmins “condemnable” and questioned the State government’s response. The Shankaracharya row has intensified political tensions in Uttar Pradesh, with opposition leaders accusing the government of disrespecting religious figures, while the ruling party has defended its actions citing law-and-order considerations. Remarks on BSP and political alliances Responding to Bahujan Samaj Party (BSP) chief Mayawati’s decision to contest elections independently, Mr. Yadav said his party remained committed to alliances with marginalised and deprived sections of society. Ms. Mayawati recently reiterated that the BSP would contest the 2027 Assembly elections alone and denied speculation about alliances. Mr. Yadav maintained that the Samajwadi Party would continue working with groups that face social and economic discrimination. Attack on State government over law and order The SP chief also criticised the State government over alleged failures in healthcare and law enforcement. Referring to incidents in Gorakhpur and elsewhere, he questioned the government’s ability to ensure public safety and deliver justice. He further alleged that BJP leaders were attempting to weaken constitutional institutions and accused ruling party members of being involved in land encroachment. Swipe at Chief Minister’s Japan visit Mr. Yadav took a dig at Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath’s proposed visit to Japan, questioning the timing and purpose of the trip. He said the State government should clarify under which policy it planned to attract investment after the State Budget had already been passed. He also remarked that the visit could at least help the Chief Minister understand how heritage preservation and development were managed in cities such as Kyoto. Interaction with party workers Mr. Yadav received an enthusiastic welcome from party workers on his arrival in Fatehpur. He briefly stopped his vehicle to greet supporters and later interacted with workers, asking them to sit beside him. The Samajwadi Party chief said economic prosperity would come only if people had income and employment opportunities, and reiterated his criticism of the BJP government’s policies at both the State and Central levels. His remarks come amid heightened political activity in Uttar Pradesh ahead of the 2027 Assembly elections, with major parties sharpening their positions on economic, religious and governance issues.

stories.title: Rahul Chahar confirms divorce from wife Ishani Johar:Cricketer says married young, spent 15 months making rounds of court
stories.summary: Agra-based cricketer Rahul Chahar has confirmed his divorce from fashion designer Ishani Johar. He shared the information through a post on X on Friday, stating that the legal process has now been completed. Rahul and Ishani were married on March 9, 2022, in a destination wedding in Goa. After nearly four years of marriage, the couple decided to separate. Ishani has not made any public statement on the matter so far. Now read what Rahul Chahar wrote? 15 months spent making rounds of court In his post, Rahul said he got married at a young age, at a time when he did not fully understand himself or the life he wanted to build. He wrote that the past 15 months were spent attending court hearings. He said this period taught him patience, tolerance and the strength that comes from truth. Rahul added that this chapter of his life has formally ended after the legal process was completed, and that the decision came at a heavy personal cost. He said he is closing this phase without anger or regret, and is moving forward with clarity and confidence. According to him, some relationships are not meant to last forever but help people learn and grow. Rahul and Ishani met through a common friend Rahul and Ishani met through common friends about three to four years before their marriage. Their friendship gradually turned into a relationship, and they dated for several years. They tied the knot in Goa in 2022 in the presence of cricketers, celebrities and close family members. After marriage, the couple often shared pictures on social media. However, reports of differences had surfaced in recent months. Cricketers Rahul and Deepak Chahar are cousins Rahul Chahar is the cousin of Indian fast bowler Deepak Chahar. Deepak is seven years older than Rahul. The two share both paternal and maternal family ties. Rahul Chahar was born in Rajasthan Rahul was born on August 4, 1999, in Bharatpur, Rajasthan. He is a right-arm leg-spinner and made his first-class debut for Rajasthan in the 2016–17 Ranji Trophy at the age of 16. He later represented India Under-19 and India A teams and performed consistently in domestic cricket. In List A and T20 tournaments, he has regularly been among Rajasthan’s leading wicket-takers. IPL debut with Rising Pune Supergiants Rahul made his IPL debut in 2017 with Rising Pune Supergiant. He gained recognition after joining Mumbai Indians in 2018 and played a key role in their title-winning campaigns in 2019 and 2020. He later represented Punjab Kings, Sunrisers Hyderabad, and Chennai Super Kings. In the IPL, he has taken around 75 wickets in nearly 80 matches with an economy rate of about 7.7. Chennai Super Kings bought him for ₹5.20 crore this season. Looking at international career Rahul made his T20 International debut for India in 2019 and his ODI debut in 2021 against Sri Lanka, where he took three wickets. So far, he has played one ODI and six T20 Internationals. He has not been part of the national team in recent years.

stories.title: Potter gets ₹1.25 crore GST notice in Raebareli:Illiterate artisan alleges identity misuse, fears suicide with family
stories.summary: A potter in Raebareli has received a GST notice of more than ₹1.25 crore, pushing his economically weak family into shock and distress. Mohammad Shahid, who has been practising pottery for three generations, said he has never run any company and alleged that his identity documents were misused to create fake firms. Shahid lives in Raghubirganj market under Harchandpur police station area, about 27 km from the district headquarters. He supports his wife and three children by making clay kulhads, pots, surahis, and toys. Notice arrived by post, villagers explained contents Shahid said he received the GST notice at his address on February 16 but could not understand it as he is illiterate. Villagers later read it out to him and informed him that the GST department had accused him of tax evasion amounting to ₹1,25,000,297. According to the notice, six firms are registered in Bihar under his name and are accused of GST evasion. He has been asked to appear before the GST office on March 16 to record his statement. The notice does not require him to deposit any money immediately but directs him to present his explanation. ‘Even if I sell myself, I cannot arrange such money’ Shahid said the amount mentioned in the notice is unimaginable for him. “I have been making pots for three generations. I have never done any other work. Even if I sell myself, I cannot arrange such money. If the notice is not withdrawn, I will be forced to commit suicide along with my family,” he said. His family said they survive on daily earnings from pottery work and have never owned any firm or business. The notice has caused severe mental stress to the entire family. Family survives on traditional pottery work Shahid and his wife Sajida make clay kulhads, pots, surahis, and toys to support their family. Their income is limited and uncertain, and they depend entirely on this traditional occupation. The family said they have never conducted large-scale business or opened any company, making the GST notice shocking and difficult to comprehend. Suspected misuse of PAN and Aadhaar documents Shahid suspects that his PAN and Aadhaar cards were misused to register fake firms in Bihar. He said his identity documents were lost about eight years ago, and he obtained new ones around five years ago. Sources in the GST department said the registrations appear to have been done through cyber fraud. Fraudsters may have used his identity details and OTP access to create firms without his knowledge. Legal experts advise filing fraud complaint GST lawyers said such fraud cases often involve misuse of identity documents, especially of illiterate and economically vulnerable individuals. Victims usually learn about the fraud only after receiving tax notices. Legal experts advised Shahid to file a fraud complaint at the local police station and submit a written statement to the GST department clarifying that he has no connection with the firms. Officials are expected to verify his claim during his appearance on March 16 and determine whether the registrations were fraudulent.

stories.title: Aniruddhacharya narrates Hanumant katha in Chicago:Visits Hanuman temple, sings bhajans atop glass tower, tours historic sites
stories.summary: Vrindavan-based kathavachak Aniruddhacharya Maharaj is currently in Chicago, United States, where he narrated the Sri Hanumant Katha at the Hanuman Temple in Greater Chicago from February 17 to 20. During his visit, Aniruddhacharya toured several prominent locations across the city. In one of the highlights, he sang bhajans while standing on a glass observation deck on the 103rd floor of a skyscraper. Speaking about the experience, he said he was standing not on the strength of the glass, but on his faith in God. He also visited an art gallery where he saw idols of Lord Shiva, Brahma, Vishnu and Maa Saraswati believed to be 800 to 1,000 years old. The kathavachak later visited the historic venue where Swami Vivekananda delivered his famous speech during the Parliament of the World’s Religions. Videos of his visit and religious discourse have been shared widely on social media.

stories.summary: Bhaskar English brings you the biggest updates from Uttar Pradesh and around the world. Here are the top news headlines of the day: 1. Youth Cong workers storm India AI Summit, raise anti-Modi slogans over US trade deal Workers of the Indian Youth Congress (IYC) staged a protest on Friday at the India AI Impact Summit 2026 being held at Bharat Mandapam in New Delhi, opposing the India-US trade deal and raising slogans against Prime Minister Narendra Modi. 2. Rahul Gandhi denies charges in Amit Shah defamation case Congress leader Rahul Gandhi appears before the MP/MLA court in Sultanpur, Uttar Pradesh, over alleged remarks against Union Home Minister Amit Shah. His lawyer says Rahul denies all charges, calling the case politically motivated and baseless. He also meets the family of a late cobbler to whom he had gifted a sewing machine. 2. UPSIDA grants land amid alleged ₹300 crore fraud The UP State Industrial Development Authority (UPSIDA) faces allegations of major irregularities in land allocation for industries. Officials allocated land arbitrarily, ignoring rules. Similar irregularities are also reported in the AYUSH department in hospital operations and medicine procurement. 4. Delhi HC directs MCD to demolish open garbage and urinals in 4 weeks for violating right to dignified life The Delhi High Court has held that the existence of a public urinal and an open garbage bin immediately adjacent to a residential property amounts to a violation of the fundamental right to life under Article 21 of the Constitution, which includes the right to live with dignity in a clean and healthy environment. 5. Dhirendra Shastri’s Divya Darbar cancelled in Lucknow The Divya Darbar planned by preacher Dhirendra Shastri in March will not be held. The Lucknow Development Authority (LDA) denied permission to use the Rashtra Prerna Sthal ground, informing organisers via letter on February 19. 6. Hospital guards beat lawyer over parking dispute Around 30 bouncers and guards at a private hospital in Lucknow severely beat a lawyer and two friends over a parking dispute. The lawyer suffered a head injury; his friends were also hurt. All three were hospitalised. CCTV captured the assault, and several guards have been detained for police interrogation. 7. India joins Trump’s ‘Board of Peace’ meeting India participated as an observer country in the first meeting of the ‘Board of Peace’ convened by US President Donald Trump on Thursday. The meeting was held in Washington, DC Representing India, Namgya C Khampa, Charge d’Affaires (senior officer) at the Indian Embassy, attended the meeting. 8. Hindu new year 2026 to have 13 months The Hindu New Year begins on March 19, marking Samvatsar 2083. Unlike a regular year, this Vikram Samvat will have 13 months. Religious beliefs consider this year very special. Uttar Pradesh is expected to face severe heat in April-May, with the monsoon likely delayed. 9. 19 lose sight after cataract surgeries in Gorakhpur At least 19 patients in Gorakhpur develop severe bacterial infections after cataract surgeries at a private hospital on February 1 under the Ayushman Bharat scheme. Nine patients required eye removal, and ten others lost vision. Families fall into debt after the incident at New Rajesh Hi-Tech Hospital in Sikariganj. 10. No Pakistan players in The Hundred 2026? Reports suggest that franchises owned by Indian Premier League (IPL) teams may not consider Pakistan players in the upcoming player auction scheduled for next month.

stories.title: MBA-qualified man murdered and buried inside home in Jhansi:100 kg of salt poured into grave; father was teacher, mother a retired court clerk
stories.summary: An MBA-qualified man in Jhansi was allegedly murdered by his younger brother following a dispute in which he was abused. After the killing, the accused dug a 5-foot-deep grave behind their house and buried the body, pouring 100 kg of salt over it in an attempt to hasten decomposition. The incident occurred on 9 February, when only the two brothers were at home; their mother had gone to her maternal residence. The following day, when she called, the elder son’s phone was switched off. The younger brother claimed he had gone out. For four days, he misled relatives, before filing a missing person report himself. See 3 pictures related to the incident- Suspicion and police interrogation Family members searched extensively, but the accused appeared indifferent, arousing suspicion in their maternal uncle, who alerted police. On 19 February, officers summoned the younger brother for questioning. Under sustained interrogation, he confessed. Police escorted him home, where he continued to misdirect them for three hours. Around midnight, the Senior Superintendent of Police (SSP) and a magistrate arrived. Under mounting pressure, he disclosed the burial site. The body was subsequently exhumed. His wife and brother-in-law are currently absconding, and their role is under investigation. The case falls under Premnagar Police Station in the Biharipura locality. Family Background Biharipura lies about 5 km from Jhansi Railway Station. The brothers’ father, Mirza Akil Beg, was a primary school teacher who built a two-storey house on a 2,500 sq ft plot. He died in a road accident in 2022. He is survived by two sons, Tariq Beg (40) and Mashariq. Following their father’s death, Tariq was offered a peon’s post on compassionate grounds. Having completed an MBA and preparing for competitive examinations, he declined. The job was then given to Mashariq. Their mother, a retired court clerk in Jhansi, often stayed with relatives due to unstable mental health. Mashariq entered into a love marriage on 9 December 2025. Murder and concealment Mashariq, posted as a peon in Bajna village for over a year, told police that on the morning of 9 February, an argument broke out after his brother allegedly abused him. Tariq reportedly picked up a knife; Mashariq seized an axe and struck him on the forehead and throat. Tariq died shortly afterwards. Fearing consequences, the accused removed interlocking tiles behind the house, dug a pit and purchased one quintal of rock salt. He buried the body, covered it with salt and soil, placed stones above it, hid the weapons and cleaned bloodstains. He later lodged a missing person complaint and even posted social media appeals to deflect suspicion. Official statement SSP B B G T S Murthy confirmed that the brother confessed during questioning. The body has been sent for post-mortem, forensic evidence collected, and investigations are continuing. Authorities stated that strict action will be taken against all those found guilty.

stories.title: Shankaracharya counters Mohan Bhagwat’s 3-children call:Says culture and values safeguard religion, not population
stories.summary: Shankaracharya Swami Avimukteshwaranand Saraswati has disagreed with RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat’s statement encouraging couples to have at least three children. He said society does not survive or progress because of numbers, but because of its culture, civilisation and religious values. Responding to Bhagwat’s remarks, the Shankaracharya said numerical strength alone cannot ensure the protection or growth of a religion. “No one wins by numbers. Dogs are greater in number, but when a lion roars, everyone runs away,” he said, stressing that strength comes from values, not population. Bhagwat had urged couples to have three children RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat made the statement during his visit to Lucknow on February 17 and 18. He said newly married couples should be encouraged to have at least three children. According to him, the purpose of marriage is to continue creation and fulfil social responsibility, not just personal desire. Bhagwat also expressed concern over divisions in society based on caste and called for unity. He said declining population in some communities could pose challenges in the future and urged people to focus on social harmony. ‘Increasing numbers alone is not enough’ Shankaracharya Avimukteshwaranand said religious scriptures emphasise values, discipline and unity, not merely increasing population. He warned that simply having more children without giving them proper values would not strengthen society. He said parents must ensure that their children grow up with strong religious and cultural values so they can uphold their faith in any situation. “A hundred stars do not give as much light as one moon,” he said, adding that quality matters more than quantity. He also said the decision on how many children to have should be left to parents. “Whether someone has one child or four is their personal choice. There should be no restriction,” he said. Warns against internal conflicts weakening society The Shankaracharya said history shows that societies can weaken due to internal conflicts, even if their population is large. He cited the example of Lord Krishna’s descendants, the Yadavas, who were destroyed due to internal disputes rather than external enemies. He said lack of discipline and unity can weaken a community from within. “When numbers increase without unity and values, people may end up fighting among themselves,” he said. He also said increasing population alone cannot solve social or religious challenges. According to him, only those who do not fully understand Sanatan Dharma focus solely on increasing numbers. Muslim cleric also responds to Bhagwat’s remarks All India Muslim Jamaat president Maulana Shahabuddin Rizvi Barelvi also reacted to Bhagwat’s statement. He said population growth is a serious issue and all communities should discuss it responsibly instead of politicising it. He said rising population is putting pressure on resources and many families, including Muslims, are choosing to have fewer children due to rising expenses and the cost of education. Rizvi said families should make decisions based on their ability to provide proper upbringing and education to their children. Background: tensions between Shankaracharya and authorities The Shankaracharya has been critical of the BJP and RSS in recent weeks. The tension increased after an incident at the Magh Mela in Prayagraj on January 18, when police stopped his palanquin and asked him to walk to the Sangam. This led to a confrontation between his followers and the police. Several disciples were detained, and the Shankaracharya later staged a protest. He returned to Varanasi on January 28 after ending the protest. Since then, he has continued to express strong views on religious and social issues. Debate highlights differing views on population and religion Bhagwat’s remarks and the Shankaracharya’s response have highlighted differing views within religious and social circles on the role of population in preserving religion and society. While Bhagwat stressed the importance of having more children to sustain society, the Shankaracharya emphasised that culture, unity and values are more important than numbers in ensuring long-term strength and continuity.

stories.title: UP raises Shiksha Mitra honorarium to ₹18,000:Instructors to get ₹17,000 monthly, cashless health cover from April
stories.summary: The Uttar Pradesh government has increased the monthly honorarium of Shiksha Mitras and instructors, Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath announced in the State Assembly on Friday. Under the decision, the honorarium of Shiksha Mitras has been raised from ₹10,000 to ₹18,000 per month. The honorarium of instructors has been increased to ₹17,000 per month. The revised payments will come into effect from April. Announcement made in Assembly Mr. Adityanath said the previous Samajwadi Party government had paid ₹3,000 per month to Shiksha Mitras and instructors. “Our government increased it to ₹10,000. Now, it will be raised to ₹18,000 for Shiksha Mitras and ₹17,000 for instructors,” he said. He also announced that teachers would be provided a cashless medical treatment facility of up to ₹5 lakh. Over 1.75 lakh beneficiaries in State According to official figures, Uttar Pradesh has about 1.47 lakh Shiksha Mitras and more than 28,000 instructors. The increase in honorarium comes after a gap of nearly nine years. The government said the decision would benefit over 1.75 lakh teaching staff associated with primary education in the State.

stories.title: UP couple sentenced to death for child sex abuse:Engineer exploited 50 children, made obscene videos sold them online
stories.summary: A husband and wife convicted of sexually abusing children in Chitrakoot have been sentenced to death by the court. The pair sold videos and photographs of children abroad through the dark web. The husband, Ram Bhawan, was employed as a Junior Engineer (JE) in the Uttar Pradesh Irrigation Department. POCSO Court Judge Pradeep Kumar Mishra ruled that both should be hanged until death. The court had convicted JE Ram Bhawan and his wife Durgavati two days earlier. The CBI arrested Ram Bhawan on 18 November 2020. Durgavati was accused of pressuring witnesses and attempting to force compromises. The POCSO Court in Banda convicted both on 18 February 2026 and remanded them to jail, following which today’s sentencing order was delivered. Case registration and FIR 31 October 2020: The Central Bureau of Investigation registered a case against Ram Bhawan, a junior engineer in the Uttar Pradesh Irrigation Department. He was accused of sexually exploiting children aged between 5 and 16, creating videos and photographs of the abuse, and distributing them via the dark web to an international paedophile network. Arrest, Suspension and Investigation 17 November 2020: The CBI’s Special Unit for Online Child Sexual Abuse Exploitation (OCSAE) arrested Ram Bhawan. Investigators alleged that he had been abusing children in Chitrakoot, Banda and Hamirpur districts for nearly a decade. Before his arrest, eight mobile phones, a laptop, pen drives, webcams, sex toys and ₹8 lakh in cash were recovered from his residence. 18 November 2020: The Irrigation Department immediately suspended Ram Bhawan following his arrest and the serious allegations, stating that the step was necessary to prevent interference with the investigation and to uphold departmental discipline. 26 November 2020: The CBI took the accused to the alleged crime scenes to verify his modus operandi. December 2020: His wife, Durgavati, was also taken into custody on allegations of attempting to influence witnesses and obstruct the investigation. 7 January 2021: The POCSO Court extended CBI custody of the accused by one week to facilitate physical and voice sampling, expert examination at AIIMS, and detailed forensic scrutiny of digital evidence. 12 February 2021: The CBI filed a chargesheet against Ram Bhawan and Durgavati, alleging sexual abuse of children and production and dissemination of obscene material. Proceedings were initiated under relevant provisions of the POCSO Act and the Information Technology Act. Evidence involving 50 children The investigation uncovered evidence of sexual abuse involving at least 50 children. Videos and photographs were allegedly transmitted digitally to contacts in 45 countries through dark web and cloud-based platforms. The eight mobile phones, laptop, pen drives, sex toys and ₹8 lakh in cash seized from the accused’s home formed part of the evidence traced by the CBI’s OCSAE unit. Investigators stated that the accused lured children with items such as mobile phones, chocolates and watches, and maintained links with foreign paedophile networks via the internet, the dark web and email. Statements from more than 50 children were recorded before the court. On 18 February 2026, the court found JE Ram Bhawan and his wife Durgavati guilty.

stories.title: CM Yogi laughs at Galgotias 'dog' remark:Opposition slams university credibility, demands law to regulate private education fees
stories.summary: Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath on Friday defended the Uttar Pradesh budget and highlighted improvements in investment, employment and financial management, while taking political jibes at the opposition during the final day of the State Legislature’s budget session. Speaking during the debate on the budget in the Assembly, Mr. Adityanath targeted Leader of the Opposition Mata Prasad Pandey, describing him as a “true socialist” who followed socialist ideology. In a sharp remark, he said leaders like Shivpal Yadav had also “tried to walk alongside him”. The Chief Minister said Uttar Pradesh’s image had improved significantly in recent years. “Earlier, some districts had such a reputation that people from Uttar Pradesh were denied hotel rooms. We changed the system and the perception. Today, people respond positively when someone says they are from Uttar Pradesh,” he said. Opposition raises issue of private school fees Earlier, Mr. Pandey raised concerns over rising fees in private schools and colleges and demanded a law to regulate them. He warned that failure to introduce regulation could lead to controversies similar to the recent incident involving Galgotias University. Referring to the episode, Mr. Pandey made a sarcastic remark, which led to laughter in the House, including from the Chief Minister. The controversy relates to an AI summit where Galgotias University displayed a robot manufactured in China but claimed it had been developed by its students. After the claim was found to be incorrect, the State government removed the university from the summit. Government highlights MSME growth and employment Mr. Adityanath said the State had taken steps to improve the investment climate and promote local employment. He said that before 2017, investors were hesitant due to poor perception and lack of confidence. “In 2018, we launched the One District One Product scheme. Today, Uttar Pradesh has 9.6 million MSME units. Each registered unit is being provided insurance cover of ₹5 lakh. This has strengthened confidence among entrepreneurs,” he said. He added that about 110,000 youths had received interest-free and collateral-free loans under the Chief Minister’s loan scheme to promote self-employment. The Chief Minister also noted that Uttar Pradesh had presented its economic survey for the first time, reflecting transparency and accountability in governance. CM explains funding and financial management Responding to opposition questions about funding the large budget, Mr. Adityanath said similar doubts were raised when his government announced farm loan waivers in 2017. “We reviewed the financial situation and implemented reforms. As a result, loans of up to ₹1 lakh were waived for 860,000 farmers,” he said. He added that the State’s financial management had improved, with the debt ratio declining from 4.39% in 2016–17 to 2.9% at present. “This reflects stronger financial discipline and increased trust from financial institutions,” he said. Opposition raises concerns over healthcare and employment Mr. Pandey also criticised the healthcare system, particularly the practice of referring patients from one hospital to another. He said this caused inconvenience and delays in treatment. Samajwadi Party MLA Ragini Sonkar raised the issue of contractual and outsourced employees, expressing concern over job security and regularisation. Other opposition members raised questions related to inflation, migration, and employment opportunities. Congress MLA Aradhana Mishra expressed concern about youths from Uttar Pradesh being sent to Israel for employment amid security risks. Responding to this, Labour Minister Anil Rajbhar said Uttar Pradesh workers were in high demand and had been sent only after ensuring their safety. Sharp exchanges and lighter moments in Assembly The debate saw sharp exchanges as well as moments of humour. Members from both sides engaged in political criticism, while occasional remarks drew laughter across the House. The budget session began on February 11, when Finance Minister Suresh Khanna presented a budget of ₹9.12 lakh crore. The final day of the session witnessed continued debate, with the government defending its economic record and the opposition raising concerns over governance, education, healthcare, and employment.

stories.title: Tax evasion of ₹37 lakhs through fake GST firm:3 accused arrested in Lucknow; 4, including mastermind absconding
stories.summary: A case has emerged in Lucknow involving GST firm registration through fake documents, fraudulent transactions worth crores, and tax evasion of ₹37 lakh. Police have arrested 3 fraudsters. The main accused, along with 4 other suspects, are still at large. DCP Crime Kamlesh Dixit said that on November 3, 2025, Bhagwati Charan Verma obtained a GST number under the name M/S K S Enterprises using a fake address in Mahanagar. Purchases and sales worth crores were shown under the firm's name. Investigation revealed that there is neither an office at the given address nor does the firm exist. The property owner also confirmed it as fake. ₹4.70 Cr transactions, wrongful ITC benefit During the investigation, it was discovered that a youth named Deepak, along with his associates, conducted transactions of about ₹4 crore 70 lakh through the fake firm using their bank accounts. By wrongfully claiming Input Tax Credit (ITC), they caused a total revenue loss of ₹37,52,545 to the government. ₹15 lakh transferred by check The investigation revealed that out of the transaction amount, about ₹15 lakh was given to Prashant Tiwari through four checks, which he used for household work. Kailash Maurya is accused of creating fake seals, opening bank accounts, and assisting in GST theft. The accused created fake electricity bills in the greed of making quick money. GST registration was obtained based on these bills.

stories.title: Minister Ashish Patel sits roadside awaiting Dayashankar’s arrival:Says, 'Those surrounded by important people naturally arrive late'
stories.summary: In Lucknow, Minister Ashish Patel got tired waiting for Transport Minister Daya Shankar Singh. He waited for 20 minutes, standing by the roadside. When he got tired, he ordered a chair from his house, which was a short distance from the event venue. He placed the chair under a tree and sat down. Daya Shankar Singh arrived an hour later. Upon his late arrival, Technical Education Minister Ashish Patel said, Those with a big heart have important people around them. When people are important, it is natural to arrive late. The new Lucknow–Chitrakoot bus service was scheduled to begin at 10 AM from Mal Avenue-1, with Ministers Dayashankar Singh and Ashish Patel set to flag off the bus to Chitrakoot (Hanumanganj). While Ashish Patel arrived on time, Dayashankar Singh arrived at 11 AM. The two later jointly inaugurated the service. Dayashankar Singh’s habit of arriving late at events is not new. CM Yogi has previously taken a jibe at him, remarking, ‘Minister arrived on time today. It seems he will fix the bus timings too.’ 3 pictures Ashish Patel defends transport minister Minister Ashish Patel said the Transport Minister has a very big heart and never refuses anyone who approaches him with a request. He added that the Minister fulfilled his demand regarding the bus service. On the issue of the Minister’s late arrival, Patel remarked that those with big hearts have many people around them, and when leaders are important, delays are natural. He said it is in the Minister’s nature that he cannot say no to anyone. Bus to pass through these major places Religious and rural passengers to benefit Chitrakoot is an extremely important religious site. This new bus service will provide devotees and local passengers with an easy travel option. Additionally, it will facilitate access to employment, education, and medical facilities for people in rural areas. According to the Transport Department, regular operations will be ensured on this route, keeping in mind passenger demand. If necessary, the number of buses can also be increased to further strengthen regional connectivity. CM told Dayashankar Singh, ‘I thought he would arrive 1 hour late’ In September 2025, a major program of the Transport Department was held at the Indira Gandhi Pratishthan in Lucknow. It saw the inauguration of 400 new buses, 8 e-buses for Lucknow, a digital bus tracking system, and several other projects. There, CM Yogi Adityanath said on stage for Dayashankar Singh, The program was scheduled to start at 11 AM, but I believed that the minister would arrive an hour late, by 12 PM. I was in a meeting when I was informed that the minister had arrived at 10 AM. They arrived ahead of time, which is a big deal. Now they will also fix the bus timings. This means that now they also want the bus stations of the transport department to become beautiful and organized in the same way.

stories.title: Hospital guards beat lawyer after parking dispute:Around 30 bouncers chase and assault advocate and his friends; several guards detained
stories.summary: Around 30 bouncers and guards of a private hospital severely beat up a lawyer and his two friends in Lucknow. The lawyer was chased and beaten. His friends were knocked to the ground and beaten with sticks, rods, and iron. The lawyer's head was split open. His friends were also injured. All 3 injured were taken to the hospital for treatment. The incident was captured on CCTV camera. The lawyer complained to the police about the matter. Police have detained several guards and started interrogation. The incident occurred on February 19, at night, at Era Hospital in the Thakurganj area. Advocate Adarsh Singh from New Haiderganj had gone to visit his friend Shubham Yadav's mother, who was undergoing treatment at Era Hospital. The guards beat him and his friends in a dispute over parking the Scorpio. Understand the sequence of events through 5 pictures... Advocate Adarsh Singh lives with his family in New Haiderganj. His friend Shubham Yadav's mother is admitted to Era Hospital. On the night of February 19, he went to Era Hospital to see Shubham Yadav's mother. Shubham Yadav and another friend, Pradeep Yadav, were also with him. They parked their Scorpio near the hospital gate. The hospital guards objected to this. Beaten up after minor argument It is alleged that an argument started between the guards and Adarsh Singh over parking the Scorpio. Soon, the minor argument turned into verbal abuse. After this, the fighting began. It is alleged that around 30 guards arrived at the spot with sticks and iron rods. They started beating Adarsh Singh, Shubham, and Pradeep. When the 3 tried to escape, the guards chased and beat them. All three fell to the ground, and the guards continued beating them. Head split, money also stolen It is alleged that lawyer Adarsh Singh's head was split due to the beating by the guards. The guards looted his ₹10K. Both his friends were also injured. All were admitted to the hospital for treatment. Adarsh Singh has received several stitches in his head. Local police arrived at the scene upon receiving information. Police took several guards into custody. They were taken to the police station for questioning. Police also questioned nearby people and examined CCTV cameras. The Incident of Violence Captured in CCTV Cameras The entire incident of violence has been captured on CCTV cameras. It shows that a dispute started with a guard regarding parking. After that, fighting begins. Several guards come running out of the hospital with sticks and rods. Then they start beating Adarsh Singh and his friends. Adarsh Singh and his friends run here and there. The guards chase and beat them. In one CCTV footage, police can be seen taking the guards into custody. Thakurganj Inspector Omvir Singh Chauhan said that there was a dispute between both parties regarding vehicle parking. A complaint has been received from the advocate's side. Legal action is being taken after investigating the matter.

stories.title: Bride calls off wedding after groom’s guest kicks her dog:Couple were together for over two years, had already married at an Arya Samaj temple
stories.summary: A shocking incident has come to light from Fatehpur in Uttar Pradesh, where a bride called off her wedding after a guest from the groom’s side allegedly kicked her pet dog. The wedding was a love marriage, and the couple had been in a relationship for two years. According to reports, the bride had eloped with her partner a month ago and married him at an Arya Samaj temple. Later, both families agreed to hold a formal ceremony. The wedding was fixed for February 18, and the groom’s side arrived from Prayagraj to Fatehpur for the function. After the garland exchange ceremony, the wedding rituals were going on. During this time, a dog sitting near the mandap started barking. It is alleged that a guest from the groom’s side kicked the dog. When the bride saw this, she became very angry. Soon, an argument broke out between the two families, and the situation turned violent. Several people suffered head injuries in the clash, and the bride also fractured her finger. Police were called to the spot. Despite efforts by the police to settle the matter, the bride refused to continue with the marriage. The groom was reportedly in tears, but she did not change her decision. The incident took place on Wednesday night at Kanha Guest House in the Khaga Kotwali area. The whole matter started with this dog. Its name is Sixer. Groom said - We were in a relationship for two years, eloped and got married The boy, Sumit Kesarwani (25), is a resident of Khaga Kotwali area of Fatehpur. He has a jewellery shop in Khaga Sarafa Bazaar. His entire family works there. Sumit said - Two years ago, he met Tanu Kesarwani, who lives in Katra, Prayagraj. Tanu has a BA degree. Both were in a relationship for two years. Both wanted to get married. I told Tanu - wait a few days, we will convince everyone at home and then get married. But she didn't wait. Tanu ran away and came to my house on January 18. After that, we both ran away from home. We got married in Kanpur according to Arya Samaj rituals. We registered for a court marriage in Allahabad. After this, Tanu returned to her home. 'When we returned home, we convinced the family, then set the wedding date' The groom said - We both had both decided that we would get engaged on January 23, but it couldn't happen. After that, on January 26, Tanu ran away and came to my house again. After that, we talked to both our families about the marriage. On February 7, Tanu's uncle and aunt came home. Both families together set the wedding date for February 18. On Wednesday, the bride's side arrived with the baraat (wedding procession) at Kanha Guest House with great fanfare. The Jaimala (garland exchange) took place, then the wedding rituals began. At four in the morning, Tanu's dog Sixer, tied a short distance from the mandap, started barking. Convinced the bride, made her take vows, but she didn't agree The groom said - People tried to calm him down, but he didn't. Meanwhile, a wedding guest kicked him. At this, Tanu and her family got angry and an argument ensued. The dispute escalated into a fight. Several people from both sides were injured in this. Three people's heads were split open, one's hand was broken. Someone informed the police about the fight. Police reached the spot. The injured were admitted to the hospital. The next morning, people from both sides reached the police station. Police tried to mediate between the two, but it didn't work out. I then made every effort to persuade the bride. I made her take vows of love. But she refused to marry. After this, a panchayat (community meeting) was held between both parties. But it was in vain. The bride's family returned the jewellery and belongings. Bride injured in an assault, brother's hand was also broken The bride was also injured in the assault. Her brother Rishabh's hand was broken. Rishabh said that they are residents of Katra, Prayagraj. The whole family works in jewellery. His sister Tanu was getting married to Sumit, a resident of Khaga. It was a love marriage for both. A quarrel started due to a small mistake and led to a fight. They were beaten so badly that many people were injured, hands were broken, and heads were split open. The fight escalated so much that the wedding was cancelled. The boy was already married, but his family was not informed of this. His sister Tanu was also enticed away from home. Tanu was also injured in the fight. Woman said - Action should be taken against those who beat me A woman from the bride's side said - The quarrel did not start for any particular reason, but over a small matter. The people from the other side had come after drinking alcohol, which escalated the fight. Many people were injured. We just want strict action to be taken against those who beat us. Khaga Kotwali Station In-charge Ramesh Patel says- There has been a mutual reconciliation between both parties. No complaint has been filed by either party. An agreement has been reached to return the transaction that took place between both parties.

stories.title: Rahul Gandhi rejects charges in Amit Shah defamation case:Meets Sultanpur family of late cobbler whom he gifted a sewing machine
stories.summary: Congress leader Rahul Gandhi appears before the MP/MLA court in Sultanpur, Uttar Pradesh, in connection with a case over alleged remarks against Union Home Minister Amit Shah. According to his lawyer, Rahul denies all charges and says the case has been filed out of political malice and lacks any solid basis. Rahul records statement in court Rahul remains in court for about 20 minutes and records his statement. The next hearing is scheduled for March 9. Lawyers present say that upon arrival, Rahul greets the judge with folded hands and later thanks the court after the proceedings conclude. Visits Ramchet Mochi’s family After leaving the court, Rahul visits the shop of Ramchet Mochi and meets his family. He lifts Mochi’s granddaughter Shraddha in his arms and, noticing an injury on her leg, asks about her condition. The family informs him that the wound is not healing properly. Rahul then asks UP Congress president Ajay Rai to ensure proper medical treatment for the child. Ramchet Mochi had died of cancer three months ago. A year earlier, Rahul Gandhi had visited his shop, sat with him, and stitched shoes. He had later sent him a sewing machine as well. Pictures related to Rahul's hearing Arrival and security arrangements Rahul arrives in Lucknow from Delhi by flight and then travels by car to the court. Party workers attempt to garland him, but he declines. After the hearing, a crowd of around a thousand gathers outside the court premises, prompting security personnel to escort him out through another gate. Case details The matter dates back to 2018. Rahul is accused of making allegedly derogatory remarks about Amit Shah during the Karnataka Assembly elections. He had said that the party that talks about honesty has a president who is an accused in a murder case. Following the statement, BJP leader Vijay Mishra from Sultanpur filed a defamation case against Rahul Gandhi on August 4, 2018. On January 19, the Sultanpur court ordered Rahul to appear in person and warned his counsel, Kashi Shukla, that it was the final opportunity, failing which strict action would be taken.

stories.title: UP Board exams monitored live from Lucknow:Computer systems increased from 53 to 70, strong rooms under 24×7 CCTV watch
stories.summary: UP Board 10th and 12th examinations began on Wednesday, February 18. More than 49 lakh candidates are taking the exam at 8033 centers. On the very first day, 3 cheaters and 5 impersonators were caught. This raised the question: how is such a large examination being monitored? To find the answer, a Bhaskar reporter reached the state-level control room. He understood how the control room works and spoke with the in-charge. It was revealed that the capacity of the control room has been increased this time. While monitoring was done with 53 computer systems until last year, this time 70 systems have been installed. Dedicated systems and expert manpower are deployed for almost all 75 districts. 6 in-charges are deployed division-wise. Read the full report First, read what the Bhaskar reporter saw in the control room Firozabad Counter of the State-Level Control Room Time: 9:10 AM The system in-charge was monitoring examination center number 1162 on the computer. In the examination room, female students were taking the high school paper. There were only female students in the room. A male invigilator was deployed. Seeing this, an objection was raised from the control room to the center in-charge. After some time, a female invigilator was deployed in the examination room. Pratapgarh Counter of State Level Control Room Time : 9:25 AM Two female students were seen talking to each other in an examination center. The invigilator's attention was elsewhere. Seeing this on the system, an alert was issued from the state-level control room. They were asked to keep an eye on both students. Balrampur Counter of State Level Control Room Time: 9:55 AM The invigilator was not seen walking in the examination room. An objection was immediately raised from the control room. Instructions were given to walk around the room and keep an eye everywhere. After this, he started looking around the room. Order issued to prevent psychological pressure Meanwhile, Deputy Director of Education and Control Room In-charge Vivek Nautiyal was seen giving instructions from the control room to the in-charges and invigilators of all examination centers. He instructed them to speak politely with the children. Room invigilators were told that they should not behave unpleasantly with children for any mistake. They should not be given any kind of stress or psychological pressure. Now read and understand how the control room is working Increase in the capacity of the state-level control room Vivek Nautiyal says that until last year, we monitored all 75 districts by installing about 53 computers. This time, we have increased this number and installed 70 working systems. A dedicated system has been provided for almost all 75 districts. Except for Jhansi and Mahoba districts of Jhansi division. These two districts are being covered by one system. We have deployed dedicated manpower on all 70 systems. They are experts in their work. They are deployed in shifts. 6 Mandal Prabhari (Circle In-charges) have been appointed over them. The Mandal Prabharis have been given full responsibility for their respective circles. Continuous discussions are held with the district-level control rooms, mobile teams, or District School Inspectors established in all districts regarding any objections related to any work. CCTV and live webcast are being done in every room Vivek Nautiyal informed that to monitor the examination, two CCTV cameras with voice recorders have been installed in each examination room, along with router, DVR, and high-speed internet facility. Live monitoring of the entire examination period is being done through webcasting. CCTV cameras have been installed for 24x7 surveillance of the strong rooms set up at the examination centers. Online monitoring is also being done for the strong rooms, question paper distribution rooms, and answer sheet sealing-packing rooms of every examination center in all 75 districts. Control Centers from Lucknow to Regional Centers State-level control rooms have issued toll-free helpline numbers 18001806607 and 18001806608. In addition, the toll-free numbers 18001805310 and 18001805312 of the Madhyamik Shiksha Parishad, Prayagraj, are also active. For social media monitoring, complaints and suggestions are also being registered through email, Facebook, X handle, and WhatsApp. Control centers have also been established in the regional offices of Varanasi, Meerut, Bareilly, and Gorakhpur, along with the Prayagraj headquarters. Instructions to open question papers under camera surveillance Instructions are to open the question papers kept in the strong room's cupboard under camera surveillance. During this, the Centre Superintendent, External, and Static Magistrates are present. The time of opening the question papers and the signatures of the present officials are recorded in the register. The strong room is also being monitored from the control room. After this, question papers are being distributed class-wise. As soon as the bell rings at 8:30 AM, the invigilators have to give the question papers to the examinees. 18 districts declared sensitive For this year's board examination, 18 districts have been declared sensitive, while 222 examination centers have been placed in the highly sensitive category and 683 in the sensitive category. STF and LIU will be kept active at these centers throughout the entire examination period, and inspection of highly sensitive centers has been ensured twice a day. Greater Strictness at Sensitive Centers Greater strictness was observed at centers declared sensitive for the board examination. The presence of regional police is higher at these centers. At these centers, zonal, sector, and static magistrates went into classrooms and conducted searches of the examinees. Additionally, five teams from the mobile squad inspected these centers and checked the arrangements. Cheaters caught on the first day On the first day, during the high school examination, 3 students were caught under UFM (Unfair Means). These included 2 from Hapur and one student from Bareilly. 5 such 'Munna Bhais' (impersonators) were caught who were giving the exam in someone else's name. These included Agra, Fatehpur, Kannauj, Kaushambi, and Etawah. FIRs have also been registered against all these 5 people in their respective districts. The control room played a crucial role in catching them. In such a situation, it is important to understand how the state-level control room is monitoring all 8033 examination centers in all 75 districts.

stories.title: On-the-spot solutions in Smart Meter Programme:Consumer complaints are being addressed on spot by officials and technical teams
stories.summary: Under an awareness campaign for smart meters, Madhyanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam is observing a “Smart Meter Fortnight” from February 9 to February 23. As part of this special drive, several large-scale programmes are being organised to inform consumers about smart meters. Smart Meter fortnight launched across region Ravi Agarwal, Chief Engineer of the Central Lucknow Zone, said that during the fortnight, consumers are being informed in detail about the benefits of smart meters. Their doubts are also being resolved on the spot. Consumers given detailed information and support Consumers are being informed about the features of smart meters, including an easy payment system, real-time information on electricity consumption, better control over usage, accurate and transparent billing, and faster services. In the Central Zone, 26,743 consumers recharged through the UPPCL Smart App between February 1 and February 18. UPPCL Smart app sees massive usage During the fortnight, consumers are also being given live demonstrations of the Uttar Pradesh Power Corporation Limited’s UPPCL SMART app. Officials are helping them download the app so they can easily use online services. Door to door campaign in full swing Meanwhile, electricity department officials and staff are visiting homes to explain how smart meters work. Awareness is also being spread through pamphlets, posters, videos and social media platforms. Help desks set up across divisions To ensure transparency and accuracy, check that meters are being installed and compared with traditional meters. This is being done to remove any confusion among consumers. Help desks have also been set up in all divisions of Central Lucknow, including Chowk, Aminabad and Raj Bhavan, to inform consumers about the benefits of smart meters and to register complaints.

stories.title: Rain in UP's Bhadohi, alert in 10 districts:Kanpur breaks 55-year record with warmest february night
stories.summary: The weather may deteriorate again in UP today. Rain is expected in 10 cities, including Agra, Mathura, Lucknow, and Prayagraj. The Meteorological Department says clouds will remain in many districts of Purvanchal. During this time, winds can blow at a speed of 20 to 30 kmph. IMD says the weather will remain clear for the next 4 days. Talking about Thursday, Banda was the hottest. The temperature here was recorded at 31.4 degrees. Prayagraj was second with 30.4 degrees. Lucknow meteorologist Atul Singh said- If it snows in Uttarakhand, there will be a drop in temperature. Currently, there are no signs of any major weather system becoming active in UP. In such a situation, after light rain, the weather is likely to become dry and clear. In the coming days, mild warmth may persist during the day, while night temperatures will continue to fluctuate slightly. Night temperature increased, will fall again On Thursday, a drop of 2 to 4 degrees was recorded in day temperatures in western UP's Agra, Meerut, and Moradabad divisions. Meanwhile, daytime temperatures remained above normal in many districts of Purvanchal and Bundelkhand. In the last 24 hours, night temperatures increased by 2 to 4 degrees in Ayodhya, Kanpur, Lucknow, and Bareilly divisions. The Meteorological Department says that minimum temperatures may again drop by 2 to 4 degrees in the next 2 to 3 days, making nights colder. If wheat-mustard crops fall, yield will be reduced Experts have advised farmers to remain alert. They say that if it rains with strong winds, wheat and mustard crops may fall. This can weaken the grains and affect the yield. The Meteorological Department has advised not to keep harvested crops in the open and to store them in a safe place. How has the weather been so far Mahesh Palawat, weather expert at Skymet Weather in Noida, says, ‘UP experienced less cold this time compared to 2 years ago’. The average maximum and minimum temperatures in December-January remained above normal. A 36 percent decrease was observed between January 1 and February 11. Extreme cold was not seen this time. Due to La Niña not being active, it couldn't get very cold. Mohammad Danish, a scientist at Lucknow Meteorological Center, also says that this time the activity of Western Disturbance was less during the winter season in the state. This resulted in below-normal rainfall during the cold season. BHU meteorologist Professor Manoj Srivastava says - Winter is now in its final phase. The temperature will gradually increase in the coming days. The spring season is currently ongoing. There won't be major weather changes for the next 2-3 weeks. During this time, there will be mild cold in the morning and night, while the afternoon sun will feel slightly intense. According to weather expert Mahesh Palawat, light drizzle may be seen in many districts of UP around February 18. This includes areas like Hathras, Mathura, Prayagraj, Varanasi, Banda, Lalitpur, and Jhansi. Now read when intense heat will start and how high the temperature will reach 1- Summer begins from first week of March BHU meteorologist Manoj Srivastava says, weather will start changing completely from the first week of March, and the summer season will begin. The temperature will rise rapidly during both day and night. By the last week of March, the maximum temperature in many districts of UP could reach 35 to 38 degrees Celsius. 2- Mercury will reach 42 to 45 degrees in May-June Manoj Srivastava says - temperature is likely to remain around 40 degrees Celsius in April. In May-June, the maximum temperature in many districts could reach 42 to 45 degrees. This means there will be less relief from heat, not only during the day but also at night, and humidity will persist. However, this will largely depend on the El Niño conditions. If El Niño conditions persist or strengthen, the heat situation could become even more serious. 3- Heat wave will last longer During March to May, maximum and minimum temperatures will remain above normal across the country, including UP. Only in March, both maximum and minimum temperatures are likely to remain above normal throughout the country. Additionally, the number of heat wave days will also be higher than normal. Heat wave days will remain normal only in northeastern India and peninsular states like Maharashtra, Karnataka, Kerala, Odisha, and Andhra Pradesh. 4- Crops will be damaged due to heat BHU's Agriculture Department Professor PK Singh says - March month could prove challenging for farmers. The rise in temperature will affect the Rabi crop. Especially wheat. Due to heat, the grains will not develop fully. This will result in lower yield. According to PK Singh, hot winds can also damage crops like mustard, chickpea, and peas. Due to rising temperatures, the soil in fields dries up quickly. This increases irrigation costs. Crops face stress. 5- Early rise in temperature, conditions will worsen further According to Dhruvsen Singh, Head of the Department of Earth Sciences at Lucknow University, temperatures have increased earlier than usual in 2026. Heat wave events may occur more frequently and for longer durations. Conditions could become more severe in urban areas due to the urban heat island effect. All these factors combined are continuously pushing temperatures upward.

stories.title: Dhirendra Shastri's Divya Darbar cancelled in Lucknow:Preacher had earlier urged public to be ready
stories.summary: The Divya Darbar of Dhirendra Shastri will not be held in Lucknow in March. The Lucknow Development Authority (LDA) has refused permission to use the Rashtra Prerna Sthal ground for the event. The organisers had applied to the LDA to hold the programme at Rashtra Prerna Sthal. On February 19, the authority sent a letter to the organisers and clearly denied giving the land for the event. The Katha and Divya Darbar were planned from March 14 to March 18. The application for the ground was made by Help You Educational and Charitable Trust. A large number of devotees were expected to attend the programme. Rashtra Prerna Sthal can accommodate more than two lakh people. Organizers were preparing Regarding the event, the organizers had first started preparations on social media. Dhirendra Shastri Maharaj had also informed devotees about his arrival in Lucknow in March through his Facebook page. However, now due to the non-allocation, the event has been put on hold. In fact, until the necessary permissions are obtained from the police and administration, no public venue is made available for any large event. Currently, no official statement has come from the organizers regarding the future strategy. 4 days of Hanumant Katha, 1 day of Divya Darbar Bageshwar Peethadhishwar Dhirendra Shastri had announced his visit to Lucknow a few days ago on the Dham's Facebook page. He had released a video saying - Jai Siyaram, Jai Bageshwar Dham. We are coming to Lucknow, the capital of Uttar Pradesh, to narrate the divine and auspicious story of Hanumanji. This story, based on Sundarkand, is going to be divine, grand, and wonderful. Make divine and grand preparations, people of Lucknow, the Mugdhardhari (one who holds a mace, referring to Hanuman) will be in Lucknow from March 14-18. This Katha (story narration) is going to be organized at Rashtra Prerna Sthal. Katha removes the sorrows of life and connects one with God. Come, let's bless our lives in Satsang (spiritual gathering). The Katha is in Lucknow from March 14 to 18. A one-day divine court (Divya Darbar) will also be held. LDA said - repairs are underway, Police said - reviewing According to sources, LDA took this step due to not receiving a No Objection Certificate (NOC) from the police. The authority did not make the allocation due to not receiving permission regarding security and crowd management at the administrative level. Meanwhile, Executive Engineer LDA Nishant Chandra stated that repair work is to be done at Rashtra Prerna Sthal. For this reason, the allocation was not made, and there is no other specific reason. Meanwhile, Joint Commissioner of Police Bablu Kumar stated that the permission for Dhirendra Shastri's Katha (discourse) is being reviewed.

stories.title: Company worth ₹1.04 lakhs gets land for ₹300 cr project:CAG report reveals UPSIDA grants land amid major fraud allegations
stories.summary: UP State Industrial Development Authority (UPSIDA) was involved in irregularities worth crores of rupees in land allocation for industries. UPSIDA officials arbitrarily allocated land while ignoring rules. In the AYUSH department too, irregularities have come to light in hospital operations and medicine procurement. The State AYUSH Society showed such trust in pharmaceutical companies that it approved the purchase of medicines without sample testing. This was revealed in the Comptroller and Auditor General (CAG) of India's report. CAG has also advised UPSIDA and the AYUSH department to improve their functioning. Know what's in the CAG report... Finance and Parliamentary Affairs Minister Suresh Khanna presented the CAG report in the Assembly on Thursday covering the AYUSH department from 2018-19 to 2022-23 and UPCIDA from 2017-18 to March 2024. No land acquisition even after Investors Summit The Yogi government organised an Investors Summit in UP in February 2018. MOUs worth more than ₹8 lakh crores were signed in it. The government also organised a Global Investors Summit in February 2022. Domestic and foreign companies and industrial groups signed MOUs worth ₹33.50 lakh crores in this summit. The first requirement for investors to set up an industrial unit is land. UPSIDA is responsible for providing land for setting up industries. The CAG report revealed that no new land was acquired in 2019-20 and 2022-23. Between 2017-18 and 2022-23, the target was met only in one year. The government says land acquisition faced difficulties due to opposition from farmers and local people. Allocation on fake documents CAG revealed that UPSIDA allocated land to bidders participating in auctions based on fake documents. Moreover, no action was taken against the responsible officers. Contract bonds worth ₹1 crore to 63.41 crore were issued to contractors without assessing their bidding capacity. 11 works were completed with delays ranging from 61 to 2612 days. 14 works remained incomplete until March 2024. Only 39 percent land allocated UPSIDA was supposed to provide 5263 acres of land between 2017-18 and 2022-23, but only 2052 acres (about 39%) could be acquired. ₹6,714.4 crore was to be recovered from allottees, but only ₹4,185.06 crore (about 62%) could be recovered. The CAG report revealed that ₹184.43 crore had to be paid as income tax due to failure in obtaining income tax exemption. Loans of ₹52.84 crore were given to two state public institutions without loan agreements. Company worth ₹1.04 lakhs gets land for 300 crore project According to the CAG report, in Kosi Kotwan-2, land measuring 28,011.15 square meters was given to a company with a net worth of only ₹1.04 lakh for a ₹300 crore project. Later, its timeline was extended till September 2024. In Kosi Kotwan Extension-1, plots were also given to low-income companies in the name of projects worth ₹40-41 crores. The companies could not deposit money on time, yet the matter was continued after taking a penalty after 864 days. Finally, the allocation had to be cancelled after changes in policy and rates. Land given to ineligible company, ignoring IRCTC For the allotment of a 5,018 sq meter plot in Jaunpur Industrial Area, M/s Jai Bhagwati Traders and the Indian Railway Catering and Tourism Corporation Limited applied. The PEC formed for land allotment considered M/s Bhagwati's DPR without reviewing applications and data from both parties. As a result, IRCTC was eliminated from the race and the land was allotted to an ineligible firm. Thousands of square meters of extra land allotted in Jhansi According to UPSIDA rules, 2000 square meters of land can be allotted to a company for investing ₹1 crore. However, UPSIDA allotted thousands of square meters of additional land in Jhansi. B-02 Orai-2 firm investing ₹3.57 crore could have been allocated 7,140 square meters of land. However, the firm was allocated 11,250 square meters of land. The firm was allocated 4,110 square meters of excess land. In Sumerpur, a firm investing ₹2.26 crore was to be allocated 4,520 square meters of land, but 15,062 square meters of land was allocated. 10,542 square meters of excess land was allocated. In Orai-Jhansi, a firm investing ₹ 2.71 crore was allocated 3,992 square meters instead of 3,629 square meters, and a firm investing ₹1 crore was allocated 3,992 square meters instead of 2,000 square meters of land. UPSIDA could not provide proof of employment generation UPSIDA has claimed to have facilitated investments ranging from ₹322 to 2,694 crore from 2017 to 2022. During this period, they also claimed to have generated employment for 2,945 to 35,545 people. However, the basis for these claims was not provided to CAG. CAG also found several irregularities in AYUSH department.. Medicine production target not met Between 2018-19 and 2022-23, the AYUSH department was supposed to produce 525.13 tons of 217 Ayurvedic medicines. However, only 268.98 tons of 125 medicines could be produced. Similarly, against a target of 160.36 tons for 145 Unani medicines, only 88.17 tons were prepared. This means in both cases, only about half of the target production was achieved. Arbitrary medicine purchases The CAG report revealed that from 2018-19 to 2022-23, the AYUSH department purchased Ayurvedic and Unani medicines worth ₹389.37 crore from the Pharmaceutical Corporation without inviting tenders. Homoeopathic medicines worth ₹108.53 crore were purchased from Goa Antibiotics and Pharmaceuticals Limited. Due to a lack of a tender process, medicines could not be purchased at competitive and transparent rates. Minimal use was made of the government's own medicine manufacturing facility. Crores at play in medicine kits In 2021-22, improper purchase of homoeopathic medicines worth ₹31.14 crore was revealed. Additionally, during the 2022 Assembly elections, safety kits (masks, sanitisers, face shields and gloves) were given to polling teams for protection from COVID. However, the Election Commission had not requested these. The AYUSH department decided to provide 7.50 lakh Ayuraksha kits at a cost of ₹20 crores. The Pharmaceutical Corporation supplied 1.48 lakh kits worth ₹3.71 crores until after the voting was completed. While 3.75 lakh kits worth ₹9.38 crores were not supplied at all. CAG revealed that despite having an adequate budget, medicines were not purchased according to targets and improper purchases were made. As per rules, at least 5 medicine samples should have been taken for testing each time. However, the State AYUSH Society did not take any samples for testing. The medicines were not sent to the lab for testing at all.
