stories.title: Shankaracharya dispute exposes tensions within UP BJP:Deputy CMs outreach seen as damage control to calm Brahmin resentment over insult
stories.summary: 'Not everyone can become Shankaracharya. Not everyone can go to the head of every seat and spoil the atmosphere here and there. Everyone will have to follow those boundaries. No one is above the law.'Yogi Adityanath, CM UP 'I can pray that they end the dispute and take a bath in the Sangam. Pranaam to Shankaracharya at the feet of God. These fake Shankaracharyas who are shedding crocodile tears in this matter are enemies of saints, enemies of Hindus.'Keshav Prasad Maurya, Deputy CM 'The hair should not have been pulled. Whoever is guilty, strict action should be taken against them. Pulling hair is a great crime. You will see it will be a great sin.'Brajesh Pathak, Deputy CM These three statements are from the CM and both Deputy CMs regarding the incident of insulting Shankaracharya and the beating of his disciples by pulling their hair at the Prayagraj Magh Mela. The question is that on one side, the CM's stand is clear. Then why are both his Deputy CMs trying to walk on a new line? Is all this action happening after intervention from the BJP's top leadership? Is this an exercise to address the displeasure of Brahmins in the state due to the Shankaracharya controversy? Or are there signs of deepening conflict within the government on this issue? Read this report.... Why are Brahmins unhappy with UP BJP? Brahmin anger surfaces in form of Alankar Agnihotri's resignation BJP in Uttar Pradesh faces a perceived vacuum in Brahmin leadership after former Governor Kalraj Mishra. Despite having seven Brahmin ministers, including Deputy CM Brajesh Pathak, many in the community feel disconnected from the party’s leadership. Warnings issued after a meeting of Brahmin MLAs in Lucknow during the winter session reinforced the perception of inadequate respect within the government. The alleged insult of Avimukteshwaranand, followed by the assault on his disciples, and the UGC controversy further deepened resentment. These incidents collectively signalled to many that Brahmins were being sidelined, with the discontent surfacing in the resignation of Bareilly City Magistrate Alankar Agnihotri. SP-BSP trying to capitalize on Brahmins' displeasure Not a single Brahmin minister from the BJP spoke on these three issues. Even Deputy CM Brajesh Pathak remained silent. As a result, parties like SP and BSP became active in capitalizing on Brahmins' displeasure. Leaders of both parties have even invited Brahmins to join their fold. BJP is feeling uncomfortable with Brahmins' displeasure. In the 2022 assembly elections, it had received 89% support from Brahmins. Before the 2027 assembly elections, Brahmins' displeasure could prove to be a major headache for the BJP. Those BJP Brahmin leaders who have remained silent on these issues so far may also have to face the consequences. Brajesh Pathak became active on Delhi's signals During the Governor’s address on 13 February, Yogi Adityanath questioned Shankaracharya’s presence in the House and defended police action. Days later, Brajesh Pathak responded publicly, calling hair-pulling a serious crime. Party sources say Pathak spoke after consulting leaders in Delhi and, with their approval, adopted an unusually sharp tone. On 19 February, he invited 101 batuks to his residence for Shikha Pujan, seen as part of the same outreach. He is also expected to meet Shankaracharya and apologize for the alleged insult at the Prayagraj Magh Mela. Senior journalist Rajendra Kumar says Pathak’s strong remarks, followed by honouring batuks, signal his emergence as an active Brahmin face within the BJP, reassuring the community of representation and support. Observers see two clear messages: Pathak may consolidate Brahmin leadership for the party, and the fallout from the Shankaracharya and UGC controversies could be contained. He had also voiced pro-Brahmin positions during the government’s first term. Pathak has been vocal on Brahmin issues before This is not the first time Brajesh Pathak has taken a strong stand on Brahmin-related issues. During Yogi Adityanath’s first term, he intervened in several high-profile cases. In Lucknow, after the police shooting death of Apple manager Vivek Tiwari was termed accidental, Pathak’s intervention led to a murder case being registered and compensation and a municipal job for the widow. In Raebareli, action followed his involvement in the murder of three Brahmins. Similar police action was triggered in a Brahmin murder case in Kanpur after he stepped in. His assertive role contributed to his elevation as Deputy CM in the second term, with the party projecting him as a key Brahmin face. Senior journalist Rajendra Kumar says Pathak had struggled to emerge as a dominant Brahmin leader in the BJP, but his recent sharp remarks and outreach to Brahmins signal an attempt to consolidate that position. Earlier, in the BSP, he was regarded as a major Brahmin leader after Satish Chandra Mishra. After joining the BJP, he was seen more as a former BSP figure, but the recent Shankaracharya row has allowed him to expand his stature while addressing Brahmin discontent within the party. Both Deputy CMs' efforts seen as damage control The Brahmins in the state are deeply upset with BJP due to the insult of Shankaracharya, the beating of Batuk students by pulling their hair, and then the UGC controversy. Senior journalist Akhilesh Bajpayee says - This is not the first time, whenever BJP makes a major mistake, damage control is done in this way. This is also strategically correct. BJP is a disciplined party. No one can draw their own separate line here. Everything happens with the unanimous decision of the organization and government. Yogi Adityanath also did not make any wrong statements in the House. He just said how the administration could let Shankaracharya go from the exit gate? It is also true that Shankaracharya was doing politics there. Otherwise, what was the reason that when the administration took the initiative for the Sangam bath with an apology, he returned without bathing. When the administration officials apologized, it is certain that this too must have happened only at the CM's initiative. What is the Shankaracharya insult and hair controversy? On 18 January (Mauni Amavasya), Avimukteshwaranand was heading for a Sangam bath with disciples in a palanquin when police stopped them, citing crowd concerns, and asked them to proceed on foot. The objection led to a clash, after which police allegedly beat disciples by pulling their hair. In protest, the seer staged a sit-in and left the Magh Mela after 10 days without taking the ritual bath. Importance of the Brahmin vote for BJP Brahmins constitute about 9–11% of Uttar Pradesh’s population and are influential in 31 of 75 districts, especially in Purvanchal, Central UP and Bundelkhand, where their support often shapes electoral outcomes. Traditionally a swing vote bank, Brahmins are socially and economically influential and can affect broader voting patterns. Their backing has historically given parties a decisive edge, though they have not remained permanently aligned with any single party. Reports indicate that around 115 seats across 31 districts, including Balrampur, Basti, Sant Kabir Nagar, Maharajganj, Gorakhpur, Deoria, Jaunpur, Amethi, Varanasi, Chandauli, Kanpur Nagar, Kanpur Dehat, Prayagraj, Banda, Ballia, and Sultanpur are Brahmin-influenced, with community voters ranging from 30,000 to 1.6 lakh. How Brahmins became BJP's charioteer after leaving Congress? After Independence until 1980, Brahmins largely backed the Congress. The Ram Temple movement and Mandal politics later drove them towards the BJP, helping it secure a full majority in Uttar Pradesh in 1991. When the BJP weakened, Brahmins shifted to the BSP, contributing to its 2007 majority. They later returned to the BJP, aiding its strong performances in the 2014 Lok Sabha polls and the 2017, 2019, 2022 and 2024 elections. A CSDS report estimates the BJP received 83% of Brahmin votes in 2017 and 89% in 2022. Signs of discontent emerged in 2024, with support slipping to about 79% and a notable share moving to the opposition alliance. Analysts warn that if dissatisfaction grows, the BJP could face significant losses. In 2022, 114 seats were decided by margins under 10,000 votes. Given that Brahmins form 9–11% of the population, even a small shift could alter results. Experts estimate a 10% swing in Brahmin votes could cost the BJP 12–15 seats, while a larger shift could push losses towards 50.

stories.title: Hindu New Year to have 13 months in 2026:Uttar Pradesh to face severe heat in April-May, monsoon likely to arrive late
stories.summary: The world celebrates the New Year on January 1, but in Hindu tradition, the New Year begins on the Pratipada of the Shukla Paksha in the month of Chaitra. This year, the Hindu New Year will start on March 19. With this, the New Samvatsar 2083 will begin. According to religious beliefs and the Hindu calendar, this year is considered very special. Unlike a normal year of 12 months, the Vikram Samvat this time will have 13 months instead of 12. In such a situation, it is important to know what will be special in Nav Samvatsar 2083? Which planet will have more influence? What will be the effect of having 13 months on the lives of common people? Read in this report When and on which day will Nav Samvatsar 2083 begin? According to BHU astrologer Prof. Vinay Pandey, Vikram Samvat 2083 will begin on the Pratipada of the Shukla Paksha of Chaitra month. This will fall on Thursday, March 19th. Gudi Padwa and Ugadi festivals will be celebrated on March 19th in different parts of the country. Along with this, Chaitra Navratri will also begin. It starts every year from the Pratipada Tithi of Chaitra month. This time, Chaitra Navratri will run from March 19 to March 27. Why is Vikram Samvat 2083 special? According to Vinay Pandey, Vikram Samvat 2083 is considered special because an extra month will be added to the Hindu calendar this year. This means that this Samvatsar will not be of the usual 12 months, but of 13 months. This extra month is called Adhik Maas. It is also known as Malmas or Purushottam Maas. According to Prof. Pandey, in the Indian calendar system, we observe months like Chaitra-Vaishakh based on the lunar calendar, and the year based on the solar calendar. Therefore, to reconcile the solar and lunar calendars, an extra month is added every third year. This is why Vikram Samvat 2083 is considered very important from a religious and almanac perspective. When will Adhik Maas occur? Gorakhpur astrologer Narendra Upadhyay says - Adhik Maas will occur in the month of Jyeshtha in Vikram Samvat 2083. This Adhik Maas will start from May 17 and last until June 15. Due to the occurrence of Adhik Maas, the dates of upcoming fasts and festivals of the year will shift forward by 15 to 20 days. This year, there will not be one, but two months of Jyeshtha. The first 15 days will be the normal Jyeshtha month, followed by 30 days of Adhik Jyeshtha Maas. The last 15 days will again be the normal Jyeshtha month. Which planet's influence will be more prominent during this period? In Vikram Samvat 2083, the influence of the planet Guru (Jupiter) is considered to be more significant. According to Narendra Upadhyay, Jupiter is considered the causative planet of knowledge, religion, policy, and expansion. In such a situation, this year people's inclination may be more towards religious, spiritual, and learning-oriented activities. Under the influence of Jupiter, education, consultation, justice, and well-thought-out decisions may be promoted. Meanwhile, in major decisions, patience and balance may be observed instead of haste. Due to Adhik Maas (intercalary month), this effect may become even clearer, leading people to focus more on self-reflection and improvement. What will be its effect on UP's weather and events? Due to Adhik Maas falling in Vikram Samvat 2083, the year's almanac will shift slightly forward. Its effect can also be seen on UP's weather. Scorching Heat in Jyeshtha Month In UP this year, the effect of summer may last longer than usual. According to Prof. Manoj Srivastava of BHU's Meteorology Department, the heat of April-May is likely to be prolonged. Meanwhile, the monsoon might be slightly delayed. Or, rainfall in the initial days might be uneven. Some areas might experience heavy rain, while others might see less rainfall. This will directly impact agriculture as well. The sowing dates for Kharif crops might be shifted. Farmers will have to make decisions considering the weather. However, if the monsoon becomes active properly, conditions for crops could also improve. According to Varanasi astrologer Sridhar Pandey, due to Adhik Maas, this year in UP might see fluctuating weather. Changes can be observed in both summer and rain. Therefore, people will need to exercise extra caution in matters related to health, water, and agriculture.

19 lose sight after Cataract surgeries in Gorakhpur:Families fall into debt; 9 patients undergo eye removal following severe infections
stories.summary: At least 19 people in Gorakhpur district suffered severe bacterial infections following cataract surgeries conducted at a private hospital, leaving nine patients with their eyes surgically removed and ten others losing vision. The patients had undergone cataract operations on February 1 at New Rajesh Hi-Tech Hospital in Sikariganj during a free camp organised under the Ayushman Bharat scheme. Out of 30 surgeries performed that day, 19 patients developed serious infections within 24 hours. “We went to improve vision, returned in debt” Mahima, whose 80-year-old father-in-law Ramdarash underwent surgery, recounted the ordeal. “My father-in-law suddenly began screaming in pain. Blood started oozing from his eye. We panicked. We had to take a loan and rush to Delhi. Doctors there had to remove one of his eyes to relieve the pain,” she said. She added, “We went to get his eyesight improved. Now we are burdened with debt.” Ramdarash developed a bacterial infection within a day of the surgery and was later treated in Delhi, where his infected eye was removed. District Administration orders probe, OT sealed After the matter reached Lucknow, Gorakhpur District Magistrate Deepak Meena ordered an inquiry and directed the Additional District Magistrate (ADM) to submit a report within 24 hours. The hospital’s operating theatre (OT) has been sealed. Preliminary investigation revealed shocking findings. According to the DM, bacterial infection was detected in the OT where the surgeries were conducted, as well as on the surgical instruments used. The hospital’s registration is now set to be cancelled. Patients’ stories: Pain, panic, and financial ruin Devaraji Devi, 60 Eye removed after severe infection Devaraji Devi from Barigaon underwent cataract surgery on her left eye. Her daughter-in-law Sanjita said she began vomiting and experiencing severe pain the same night. She was referred from one hospital to another before being taken to AIIMS Delhi, where doctors confirmed bacterial infection and removed her eye on February 6. “Even after surgery, the pain persists. We’ve already spent a large amount on treatment. Despite everything, she will never see from that eye again,” Sanjita said. Dinanath, 75 Writhing in pain all night Dinanath from Bankata village experienced intense pain around 1 am after being discharged. Despite painkillers, his condition worsened. He was eventually taken to AIIMS Delhi, where his eye was removed on February 11. “We never imagined this would happen,” said his grandson Satish Vishwakarma. Meera Devi, 55 Both eyes infected; one removed Meera Devi from Rampur developed vomiting and severe pain the morning after surgery. Doctors at AIIMS confirmed infection in both eyes. One eye was removed after her condition stabilized. Her son Bhimnath said, “We’ve spent around ₹40,000 so far. Doctors’ negligence has cost us dearly.” Rajendra Kumar, 71 Hope fading for vision recovery Rajendra from Innadih lost his eyesight after infection spread. Doctors at SGPGI Lucknow reportedly said the damage was irreversible. “We are still hoping for a miracle, but doctors say the infection has destroyed his vision,” his son said. Ranjeet, 71 Bleeding from eye after surgery Ranjeet from Bharsi noticed bleeding from his eye at night. He was later admitted to Gorakhpur AIIMS, where his eye was removed after a week of treatment. “I didn’t have money for treatment. Initially, I had to arrange ₹4,000–5,000. Later, the hospital provided ₹15,000 in assistance. I lost an eye, but at least I survived,” he said. Bahidun Nisha, 60 One eye saved, one lost Bahidun Nisha had gone only for a check-up but was advised surgery. Two days later, she developed pain. Both eyes were infected, but doctors managed to save vision in one eye. She continues treatment in Delhi. Ramdarash, 80 Treatment amid family wedding preparations Ramdarash’s family is struggling financially. “We are taking loans for treatment, and there’s a wedding in the family next month. We don’t know how we’ll manage,” said Mahima. Mohammad Ali, 69 Escaped infection, relieved after check-up Mohammad Ali, who underwent surgery the following day, said he was frightened after seeing news reports but was later relieved when a follow-up check-up confirmed no infection. Now read Akhilesh Yadav's post Health officials confirm bacterial contamination Chief Medical Officer Dr. Rajesh Jha termed the incident a “serious case of negligence.” He confirmed bacterial contamination was found in the operation theatre and surgical instruments. A magisterial inquiry is underway, and further action will be decided after the final report. What is Cataract? Cataract is a condition in which the eye’s natural lens becomes cloudy, leading to blurred vision and difficulty performing routine tasks such as reading or driving. Surgery is required to prevent blindness. Why does bacterial infection occur after Cataract surgery? Post-surgical bacterial infection may occur due to: Doctors advise immediate consultation if pain or blurred vision occurs after surgery. Special precautions are necessary for patients with diabetes or cancer.

stories.title: Brahmin BJP leader receives elephant ‘Jatra Singh’ as gift:Brought from Arunachal Pradesh to Pratapgarh at cost of ₹1.5 lakh; welcomed with band and music
stories.summary: In Pratapgarh, a Brahmin BJP leader, Ashok Tripathi, has received an elephant as a gift. Its name is 'Jatra Singh', and it is 8 years old. The elephant was brought to Pratapgarh from Arunachal Pradesh, passing through Assam, West Bengal, and Bihar. The elephant covered a distance of about 2,000 km, and it cost one and a half lakh rupees to bring it here. The elephant was given to BJP leader Ashok Tripathi's mother, Kewal Devi, in memory of his father. When the elephant Jatra Singh was brought to the village, it was welcomed with chants of 'Ganpati Bappa Morya'. It was unloaded from the truck with a band playing. After this, it was bathed according to rituals. Ashok Tripathi, his mother, and others applied a tilak to the elephant in the temple premises. Worship was performed with the chanting of mantras. Prasad was distributed. A crowd gathered to see and worship the elephant. An enclosure has also been prepared for the elephant in the village. The incident is from Chhintpur village in the Raniganj assembly constituency. See three photos Actually, Ashok Tripathi had contested elections from the Sadar assembly seat in 2017. In 2019, he was also a candidate from the SP-BSP alliance, but had to face defeat. Before the 2022 assembly elections, he joined the BJP. Ashok Tripathi's father, Ram Prakash Tripathi, served as a principal in several districts of Arunachal Pradesh. After his demise, in his memory, the people of Namsai district in Arunachal Pradesh gifted the elephant 'Jatra Singh' as a donation to Ashok's mother, Kewal Devi, in May 2023. Since then, the elephant was being looked after in Arunachal Pradesh under the supervision of two mahouts. During this period, Ashok Tripathi himself had arranged for proper food and accommodation. Permission granted after a year and a half of legal process In October 2024, Ashok Tripathi applied as per rules to bring the elephant to Pratapgarh. After completing all legal procedures, on the recommendation of the High Power Committee (HPC) constituted by the Supreme Court, the Arunachal Pradesh Forest Department granted permission on February 6, 2026, to bring the elephant to Chhintpur village in Pratapgarh. Subsequently, under due process, the elephant was dispatched from Namsai (Arunachal Pradesh) to Pratapgarh on February 9, 2026. On Tuesday afternoon around 2 PM, 'Jatra Singh' reached Pratapgarh. Elephants cannot be bought or sold Unlike dogs, cats, or horses, elephants cannot be bought or sold. Buying and selling is considered a violation of the Wildlife Protection Act and carries a provision for strict punishment. Therefore, its price is not fixed. In the past, in some illegal trade cases, the price of elephants has been observed to be between 10 lakh and 1.5 crore. In states like Kerala, elephants are leased for long periods (e.g., 99 years), which can be valued at over 1 crore. The original family that donated to BJP leader Ashok Tripathi is a resident of Namsai district, Arunachal Pradesh. This family has traditionally been associated with elephant rearing. This elephant was donated by the same family. An open area of approximately 8,000 to 10,000 square feet should be available for the elephant to live in. The BJP leader has built an enclosure of about the same size. Water arrangements have been made. A fountain has also been installed to provide relief in the summer. Two mahouts, Waris Khan and Mukhtar, have been appointed to care for the elephant. The elephant's diet includes paddy, sugarcane, gram, jaggery, peepal, and pakar leaves. Regular arrangements have been made for daily meals. 1.5 lakh spent on bringing by truck The elephant was brought from Arunachal Pradesh to Pratapgarh via truck. stories.title: Former Bareilly City Magistrate launches ‘Sanatani Culture’ party:Alankar Agnihotri to contest elections, says alliances possible if required
stories.summary: Former Bareilly City Magistrate launches ‘Sanatani Culture’ party Eighteen days after resigning from service, former City Magistrate Alankar Agnihotri on Sunday announced the formation of a new political party named Sanatani Culture. Speaking in Vrindavan, he said the party would contest elections and consider alliances if required. Agnihotri said the party’s stated aim was the protection of Sanatan culture, alleging that recent government policies and projects were undermining long-established religious and social institutions. He accused the government of pursuing decisions that were deepening divisions in society. Three-point agenda Outlining the party’s agenda, Agnihotri said it would focus on three issues: the University Grants Commission (UGC) Regulation, alleged misuse of the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, and the proposed Banke Bihari corridor in Vrindavan. He described the present dispensation as “anti-Sanatan” and said smaller regional parties such as Apna Dal and Rajbhar had built their own political space. “They have their own respect. We will also establish ours,” he said. Resignation from office Agnihotri resigned as City Magistrate of Bareilly on January 26. He said his resignation was prompted by his objection to what he described as the insult of a Shankaracharya and his opposition to the UGC’s new regulations. Claims of misuse of SC/ST Act Agnihotri alleged that people were being harassed through false cases under the SC/ST Act. He said he had issued an email ID to collect complaints from those who claimed to be falsely implicated and to help them seek justice. “More than 40 emails have been received since Thursday night,” he said, adding that people were detailing their grievances through these messages. He cited instances from Bihar to support his claim that the law was being misused. Banke Bihari corridor On the Banke Bihari corridor project, Agnihotri said the religious and cultural traditions of Vrindavan had been shaped over centuries by Goswamis, priests and sevadars. He alleged that the corridor project threatened to dilute this heritage. He said religious institutions born out of faith and tradition needed protection and criticised the government’s approach to Ayodhya, Kashi and Mathura-Vrindavan. Objection to UGC Regulation 2026 Agnihotri termed the UGC Regulation dated January 13, 2026, as discriminatory. He alleged that meritorious students from the general category were being treated unfairly and warned of the potential for misuse of equity committees. He questioned whether parents would want to send their children into an education system where, he claimed, careers could be damaged by unverified complaints. He also criticised elected representatives for remaining silent after seeking votes in the name of the Brahmin community. Agnihotri announced the formation of the party on the occasion of Vijaya Ekadashi, saying it marked the beginning of a political platform centred on Sanatan culture and social issues he believes are being ignored.

stories.title: Langur stops DM by pulling her sari:IAS officer sits on ground in Baghpat, gently says 'No Matru' while trying to calm it
stories.summary: Baghpat DM Asmita Lal was stopped by a langur pulling her saree. It started preventing her from going away. The female DM smiled seeing this. She sat down near the langur. As she affectionately extended her hand towards it, the langur also held her finger. The DM sat with the langur named Matru for five minutes. She laughed and played with it. This entire incident is from the Collectorate last Thursday, whose video surfaced today. Here, Kisan Union workers had arrived with their problems. Hearing this, the DM herself came to the farmers. Matru stays near the DM's office Around 1:30 PM on Thursday afternoon, workers of the Bhartiya Kisan Union reached the Collectorate to submit a memorandum to the CM. They sat on a protest within the Collectorate premises. As soon as DM Asmita Lal received this information, she herself went to the farmers. During this, a langur also came and sat there. This langur is often seen near the DM's office. People have named it Matru. When the DM's eyes fell on the langur, she sat on the ground and started playing with it. The langur caught the DM's hand. To this, she said - No Matru. Then the farmers sitting nearby laughed. The farmers said - Madam, it won't listen if you say no. Hearing this, the DM also laughed. The woman DM is an animal lover She played with the DM langur for about five minutes. When she was about to leave, the langur caught her saree. During this, the DM tried to free her saree from the langur. The langur did not leave the saree at once, after which the farmers freed the DM's saree from its hand. After this, the DM went back to her office. IAS Asmita Lal is known for her love for animals. She has constructed temporary night shelters in Baghpat to protect voiceless animals from the cold. Apart from this, artificial nests have also been prepared for birds in the collectorate. Asmita Lal is an IAS officer of the 2015 batch Asmita Lal, a resident of Delhi, is a 2015 batch IAS officer. She has been given the charge of District Magistrate for the first time. Prior to this, she was working as the Chief Development Officer (CDO) in Ghaziabad. While serving as the CDO of Ghaziabad, she did a lot of work for the 'Beti Padhao-Beti Bachao' (Educate Daughter-Save Daughter) campaign. She often remains in discussion regarding this.

stories.title: Wife commits suicide after caught talking to boyfriend:Husband beats her with belts, she informs mother, then consumes poison
stories.summary: In Jhansi, a dispute broke out between husband and wife over a phone conversation. The husband caught his wife speaking on the phone late at night. The wife revealed to him that she had a romantic relationship. On hearing this, the husband beat her with belts. The next day, the wife consumed poison. Family members rushed her to Jhansi Medical College, where she was declared dead on Friday. Police have taken the body into custody and started an investigation. The incident took place in Niboda village, Shivpuri area of Madhya Pradesh. The deceased woman’s name was Rakhi. Details of the case Married four years ago Rakhi (25) was a resident of Niboda village. She had married Ramkumar Kushwaha on 10 May 2022. The couple had a one-and-a-half-year-old son. The husband, Ramkumar, told police that his wife had a romantic affair with a man from her parental home and was secretly communicating with him. On Wednesday, he went to drive a truck. At night, he called his wife and spoke with her for about an hour before going to sleep. Around midnight, he called her again, but her line was busy. After calling three times, she disconnected twice. Husband claims wife was talking to lover On the fourth call, she answered. When he asked who she was talking to so late at night, she admitted it was her boyfriend. She said, “Come home, or I will die.” He went home and she revealed the affair. In anger, he beat her. The wife had informed her mother about the situation during the night. The next day, Thursday, he went to the fields. In the afternoon, the family was informed that Rakhi had consumed poison. She was taken to Jhansi Medical College, where she died. Troubled since marriage Rakhi’s mother told police that her daughter had been troubled since marriage. The husband often quarreled with her and physically abused her. On Wednesday night, Rakhi was talking to someone. When Narayani called her, she scolded her daughter. After that, the husband beat her severely with a belt and threatened to kill her. Rakhi then consumed poison. “My daughter is dead now. I want justice. The husband must be held accountable,” said Narayani.

stories.title: Girl who disappeared as 'Nagin' reaches police station:Says she secretly married while family placed snake skin on her bed
stories.summary: In Auraiya, a girl who disappeared in a dramatic ‘Nagini’ act reached the police station. She told the police, “I married in Kanpur. The story of me disappearing as a Nagini was made up by my family. They even placed a snake skin on my bed. The villagers were told I went missing.” Friday morning, the girl arrived at the station wearing a blue saree, a bindi on her forehead, and bangles on her hands. She said she had gone secretly with her lover to reach the station. “I used to keep a snake at home, and I had kept its skin there. My family knew about it. But the skin on the bed is different. How it got there, only my family knows. I want to live with my husband now,” she said. The case is from Singanpur village, Fafund. Now the complete matter in detail... Reena belongs to Rakesh Valmiki’s family in Singanpur village, which has five daughters and two sons. Four daughters are already married. Reena (21) studied up to class 8 in a local school. She had a relationship with local youth Shyam Ji Sharma. Her family had arranged a marriage elsewhere, but she wanted to marry her lover. To run away, she planned her disappearance in a dramatic, film-like manner. On the night of February 10, she wrapped a snake skin in clothes and placed it on her bed, then left home. The next morning, when her family found the skin, rumors spread in the village that she had transformed into a ‘Nagini’. Used to talk to lover from mother's mobile Reena did not have a mobile phone of her own. She used her mother’s keypad phone to communicate with her lover. The police traced the number under surveillance, which led to a youth. After the incident, his family’s phones were switched off, and his home was locked. Had gone to Sheshnag temple 3 months ago According to her family, about three months ago, Reena visited the Sheshnag Temple in Kumhel, Mainpuri, and brought a Sheshnag statue. She often spoke about seeing snakes in dreams and lying near them at night. After her disappearance, relatives and villagers gathered around her home, adding to the rumors. Wedding video goes viral on Instagram Around 2 PM on Thursday, Reena posted two videos on Instagram via Shyam Ji Sharma’s account “Jai Mahakal” The first video was 11 seconds, the second 34 seconds. In the first, she appeared with her husband and said, “I got married. This is my husband. If there’s trouble with their family, my family will be blamed.” In the second video, she said, “I wanted to marry him. I told him today we will get married. I forced him to marry me. I married of my own will, without anyone else’s hand. Please do not torture us. This is my only wish.” Reena emphasized in the videos that neither her lover nor her family should be harassed. She married by her own choice. Now read what Reena said at the police station... On Friday morning, Reena reached Fafund police station and said, “I ran away with my lover. The snake slept with me. I had informed my family about it. I did not place the snake skin on the bed. The one on the bed is not mine. How it got there, only my family knows. I did not take anything with me. I married in Kalyanpur, Kanpur Dehat, and came here secretly.” Mongoose and scorpion bit me, they died themselves Now I want to go with my husband. We had an affair for 4 years. Neither my family nor his family knew about this. First a snake had bitten me, I survived. Later, a mongoose and scorpion bit me, but they died themselves.

stories.title: CM Yogi breaks silence on Avimukteshwaranand controversy:Says not everyone can be Shankaracharya; Akhilesh asks who gave them Yogi’s certificate?
stories.summary: Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath broke his silence for the first time on the Avimukteshwaranand controversy in the state assembly. Referring to the dispute, Yogi said a non-issue was deliberately turned into a controversy. “Can anyone roam the state claiming to be Chief Minister? Ministers cannot just put up boards and move freely, and neither can anyone claim to be the SP national president. The Shankaracharya position is sacred in Sanatan Dharma, guided by tradition and rules,” he said. The CM further added that misusing the title of Shankaracharya could disturb public order. “If he was truly a Shankaracharya, why was there a lathi charge in Varanasi?” he asked, underlining that the position is revered. Highlighting the scale of religious gatherings, he noted that over 45 million devotees attend the Magh Mela during Mouni Amavasya, and arrangements are made for all. “The law applies equally to everyone. There is no special law for me. If I commit a crime, I will be treated like any common citizen,” Yogi said. He concluded by reiterating that in India, everyone, without exception, must respect the law.

stories.title: UP Evening Wrap:Tarique Rahman set to become Bangladesh PM, BNP wins two-thirds majority; Bomb threats to 5 courts including Lucknow and Varanasi more
stories.summary: Bhaskar English brings you the biggest news from Uttar Pradesh and around the world. Here are the top news headlines of the day: 1. Parliament adjourned until March 9; BJP MP asks, ‘Is Rahul plotting India’s partition to gain power?’ Lok Sabha proceedings lasted only about 10 minutes on the 13th day of the Budget Session. As soon as the House began on Friday, opposition MPs shouted, “Hardeep Puri, resign!” The House was adjourned five minutes later. The House resumed at 12 noon. Amid continued uproar, some bills related to the Education and Law Ministries were introduced. Chairperson Sandhya Rai then adjourned the Lok Sabha until 9 March. Rajya Sabha also adjourned until the same date. 2. Yogi Adityanath on speaks on ‘Vande Mataram’ in Assembly on day 5; pensions of 1 crore women to rise Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath is speaking in the Assembly on the Day 5 of the Uttar Pradesh Budget session. He tells LoP Mata Prasad Pandey he raises valid points, but questions his rift with Sanjay Nishad. CM remarks that it seems even Pandey’s pond has been leased by Nishad. The comment comes after a sharp exchange between the two over the reservation. 3. Bomb threats to 5 courts including Lucknow and Varanasi The Varanasi District and Sessions Court premises have received a bomb threat. The threatening email came on the government mail on Friday. As soon as this was discovered, panic ensued. More than 200 police personnel rushed to the court immediately. The District Judge also came out of the campus. Police evacuated the entire premises. Every corner of the court is being searched. Court proceedings have been suspended. 4. PM unveils ‘Seva Teerth’ as new name for PMO Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Friday unveiled the name of the new building complex housing the Prime Minister’s Office (PMO), the National Security Council Secretariat (NSCS), and the Cabinet Secretariat as ‘Seva Tirth’. PM Modi will shift to the new PMO today. He will inaugurate Karya Bhavan-1 and 2, along with Seva Tirth, around 6 pm. He will then address a public event. Karya Bhavan-1 and 2 will house the offices of various central government ministries. 5. 20K positions to be outsourced in UP, budget increased by ₹426 cr, minimum salary to be ₹16K Before the election, the Yogi government of UP had prepared to fill more than 20 thousand positions through outsourcing. Indications of this have come from the increased budget of this department. The government has released ₹2223.84 crore this time by increasing the budget by ₹426 crore. 6. Former Congressman Naseemuddin to join Samajwadi Party UP Congress heavyweight Muslim leader Nasimuddin Siddiqui, who resigned on January 24, will now join the Samajwadi Party. On Friday after prayers, he will meet with his supporters and then announce joining SP. For 20 days, there were various discussions about his political move. Finally, after touring different districts and having long discussions with his supporters, he has made this decision. 7. Bangladesh EC announces results for 297 parliamentary seats; BNP chief Tarique set to become PM The Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP) achieved a decisive victory in Thursday’s general elections, winning 209 of the 299 parliamentary seats—well above the 150-seat majority threshold. Results for 286 seats have been declared so far. 8. Man who eloped with mother-in-law, claims her affair with brother-in-law The man who eloped with his mother-in-law now says he regrets his decision in Aligarh. He claims that falling in love with her was the biggest mistake of his life. Within nine months, she allegedly developed an affair with his brother-in-law. She began speaking to him secretly and eventually ran away. 9. Man kills family, calls priest, dies by electrocution, ashes found inside Mathura home The mystery surrounding the deaths of 5 members of a family in Mathura has led police to a temple located about 2 km from their home. Before the incident, Manish reportedly made a call to the son of temple priest Karua Baba. Police have detained the priest and are trying to determine what was discussed in that final conversation. 10. ‘Better to shut down RERA, it has become a "rehabilitation centre for retired bureaucrats’, says the Supreme Court The Supreme Court of India has strongly questioned the functioning of the Real Estate Regulatory Authority (RERA), remarking that it may be better to shut the body down as it is failing to help homebuyers and instead benefiting defaulting builders.

stories.title: 'He put his hand on my waist, says let’s party':KGMU victim alleges senior doctor called her to chamber and touched her inappropriately
stories.summary: A few days ago, a child in critical condition was brought to the pediatric department for treatment. A critical procedure was needed to save the child's life. Along with the Additional Professor, I was also a part of that procedure. Thanks to the doctors' efforts, the child's life was saved and he recovered. During the child's treatment, the professor looked at me inappropriately several times. I kept ignoring this. Later, when the child recovered, the professor congratulated me and said that he would now give me a party. I said, 'Yes, we can have a party any day.' To this, he said, 'No, I will give you a party privately.' When I refused, one day he called for the complete file of the child's case in his cabin. He told me that it needed to be submitted to a journal for publication. When I arrived there, the professor grabbed my hand and pulled me towards him with inappropriate intentions. I said, 'Sir, you are like my father. I cannot see you as anything other than that.' To this, he said, 'You were also giving me hints.' I said, 'You must have misunderstood. I never thought of you that way.' This ordeal was narrated by a female doctor from KGMU to the Vishakha Committee. She even started crying while narrating all this before the Vishakha Committee. Actually, she has accused Additional Professor Sanjeev Kumar Verma of molestation. Subsequently, the professor has also been suspended. What has happened so far in this case On Wednesday, after a new case of molestation of a resident doctor came to light, the campus atmosphere suddenly changed once again. This incident was discussed everywhere. Meanwhile, on Thursday, the Visakha Committee meeting was held for the second consecutive day. During this, statements of several doctors and residents from the Pediatric department were also recorded. Seven members of the Visakha Committee were present in the meeting that lasted for about 4 hours. The arguments of the accused Additional Professor were also discussed in response to the complaint of the victim resident doctor. The Visakha Committee also tried to reach out to eyewitnesses of the incident. However, according to sources, no eyewitness was found as the incident occurred inside the chamber, but the evidence related to it appears to be in favor of the victim resident doctor. Now read what else the victim told I came out of the chamber and started crying The victim doctor alleged that the Additional Professor called her to the chamber with a file. As soon as she reached there, he grabbed her hand and tried to forcibly touch her. After this sudden incident, the resident doctor came out of the chamber and complained about it to a female faculty doctor in the department. Father met the Vice-Chancellor and pressed for action The very next day, the resident doctor's parents reached the KGMU campus. Meeting with Vice-Chancellor Dr Sonia Nityanand, they demanded strict action in the matter. Meanwhile, based on the victim's written complaint, a meeting of the Vishakha Committee was called for investigation. The first meeting was held on Wednesday. During this, statements of the victim resident doctor and the accused additional professor, were recorded. Considering the seriousness of the matter, the Vice-Chancellor suspended the accused additional professor until the investigation was complete. His entry into the department was also banned. Complaint on February 11, Action on 12 The victim doctor (MD student) had lodged a complaint with the KGMU administration on February 11, accompanied by her family. The doctor alleged that the professor misbehaved with her and also sent messages on her mobile. Following this, on the orders of Vice-Chancellor Dr Sonia Nityanand, the Vishakha Committee recorded the victim doctor's statement and interrogated the Additional Professor. In the committee's preliminary investigation, the allegations were found to be true. Based on its report, the accused, Additional Professor Dr Sanjeev Kumar Verma ,was suspended. During his suspension, he was attached to the Deanof Medicine's office. Called into the chamber, held her hand, molested her KGMU spokesperson Dr. K.K. Singh said- On the day of the incident, Additional Professor Dr Sanjeev Kumar Verma called the resident doctor into his chamber on the pretext of some work. First, he held her hand and then molested her. This left the resident doctor shocked and distressed. She immediately left the chamber. Then she narrated the entire incident to a female faculty member of the department. Upon the complaint of the victim doctor, a Vishakha Committee was immediately formed. After an initial investigation, the accused was suspended. He has also been attached to the Dean's office until the investigation is complete. Police searched for Rameez for 18 days On December 23, 2025, an MD Pathology student filed a complaint at Chowk police station, alleging that her senior, Dr. Rameez, had physical relations with her on the pretext of marriage. He also forced an abortion and pressured her to convert her religion. Police were able to arrest Rameez 18 days after the complaint. A reward of 50 thousand had been declared for him. He was living in Thakurganj, while police teams were searching for him in 4 states: UP, Uttarakhand, Delhi, and Himachal Pradesh. Police had pasted attachment notices on houses in Lucknow, Pilibhit and Khatima on January 7. On January 5, his father Salimuddin and mother Khatija were arrested. After this, Rameez was caught on the night of January 9.

stories.summary: UP Politics: अप्रैल 2024 की बात है, जब लोकसभा चुनाव की तैयारी चल रही थी। उस समय BSP के नेता और मायावती के भतीजे आकाश आनंद यूपी के सीतापुर में रैली करने पहुंचे। रैली में उन्होंने BJP को नफरत फैलाने वाली और आतंकवादियों की पार्टी बताया। इस बयान से मायावती बेहद नाराज हुईं। उन्होंने तुरंत आकाश आनंद को नेशनल को आर्डिनेटर पद से हटा दिया। मायावती ने इस फैसले को सिर्फ दफ्तर के अंदर तक नहीं रखा, बल्कि सोशल मीडिया प्लेटफार्म X पर भी लिखा कि आकाश आनंद से पद ले लिया गया है। अभी उन्हें पूरी तरह परिपक्व होने में वक्त लगेगा। यहां ध्यान देने वाली बात है कि आकाश आनंद सपा के खिलाफ भी बयान दे रहे थे, लेकिन मायावती ने उन पर कोई कार्रवाई नहीं की। इसका मतलब साफ था कि मायावती BJP पर सीधे हमला करने से बच रही थीं, जबकि राजनीतिक बयान दे रहीं थीं।

stories.title: UP Budget Session Day 5:Yogi says, 'Those who refuse to sing Vande Mataram should be thrown out'
stories.summary: On the fifth day of the Uttar Pradesh Legislature’s Budget Session, Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath announced a proposed hike in pensions for 1.06 crore destitute women across the state. Speaking during the discussion on the Governor’s address, he said beneficiaries currently receive ₹12,000 annually and that the government plans to increase the amount soon. He added that Finance Minister Suresh Khanna would formally announce the revised pension in the upcoming budget presentation on February 15. Sharp remarks over Vande Mataram During his speech, the Chief Minister also raised the issue of Vande Mataram, alleging that MPs from the Samajwadi Party and Congress had opposed it. “No one can insult Vande Mataram. They eat from this country but refuse to sing it,” he said, adding that those opposing it should not claim the right to stay here. Dig at Opposition leader In a lighter yet pointed exchange, the CM addressed Leader of the Opposition Mata Prasad Pandey, saying he generally makes reasonable points but appears to have differences with Sanjay Nishad. Referring to their earlier heated debate over reservation, Yogi remarked that it seemed even Pandey’s “pond” had been leased out by Nishad — a comment that drew reactions in the House. Speaker loses cool, poetry eases tensions The day also saw tense moments when Speaker Satish Mahana rebuked BJP MLA Ketki Singh for interruptions. Visibly upset, he removed and threw his headphones and adjourned the House for 10 minutes. When proceedings resumed, Congress MLA Aradhana Mishra tried to lighten the mood, prompting a poetic exchange. SP MLA Kamal Akhtar recited a couplet, followed by Finance Minister Suresh Khanna, whose verse about replacing enmity with love brought some laughter and calm to an otherwise stormy session.

stories.title: Lucknow woman accuses tenant family of honey-trap plot:Son held hostage for 1 lakh, FIR registered on court's instructions
stories.summary: A case of honey trap, blackmailing and assault has come to light from the Krishnanagar area of Lucknow. Kakoli Malik, a resident of Azad Nagar, has accused the tenant family living in her own house of trapping her son in a love trap, holding him hostage and demanding a ransom of one lakh rupees. After no police action, the victim has sought refuge in court. Following this, a case has been registered at Krishnanagar police station. Serious allegations against tenant family According to Kakoli Malik, she lives in house number 552 on Sanjay Gandhi Marg in Azad Nagar. In another portion of the same house lives Sneha Kanojia along with her mother Shashi Kanojia and other relatives. The complaint alleges that Sneha and her family trap young men in honey traps, implicate them in false cases and blackmail them. The complainant claims her son Abhishek Kumar Malik was lured into a relationship and separated from his family. He was allegedly threatened with false cases under the SC/ST Act and rape charges to pressure him. It is also alleged that he was married at an Arya Samaj temple without the family’s knowledge, though no documents of the marriage are available with them. Demand for ₹1 lakh, attack on refusal According to the petition, on the evening of 17 October, Sneha arrived at their door with two to three outsiders and said their son was in her custody. She allegedly demanded ₹1 lakh if they wanted to see him safe. When they refused, she and her associates allegedly attacked the complainant with an iron rod, fracturing her right hand. The medical report has been submitted in court. The complainant said the accused also threatened to kill them before leaving. She stated that she had submitted a written complaint at Krishnanagar police station and sent representations by registered post to senior officials, but no FIR was registered. She then approached the court, after whose order the case has now been registered.

stories.title: Ashutosh Maharaj exits court crying:Alleges sexual exploitation by Avimukteshwaranand, court to deliver verdict soon
stories.summary: A decision has been reserved in the case alleging sexual exploitation of minor children at the camp of Shankaracharya Swami Avimukteshwaranand. It will be decided at 5 pm whether an FIR will be registered against the Shankaracharya or the case will be dismissed. Ashutosh Maharaj himself is arguing the case as counsel. The hearing began at 2 pm on Friday. Before Judge Vinod Kumar Chaurasia, he said two disciples had approached him and narrated their ordeal of sexual abuse. He urged that an FIR be filed against the Shankaracharya and an investigation conducted. He added that he expects justice only from the judiciary. After this, the Shankaracharya’s lawyer cross-examined him, saying these were only allegations and they needed time to prepare the case. Ashutosh Maharaj responded that he was receiving threats, including one to blow up his car with a bomb, and feared he might be killed. He insisted the statements of the children should be heard. Court room cleared, judge heard children's statements The judge then ordered the POCSO courtroom to be vacated, leaving only lawyers from both sides. The children were brought in and narrated their accounts before the judge. All statements were recorded in camera. After hearing them, the judge reserved the order and will reconvene at 5 pm to decide the next course of action. Two minor boys accompanied Ashutosh Maharaj, their faces covered. Their statements were also recorded inside. When he stepped out, the children were still with him. Speaking to reporters, he said the court had heard them and the decision now rested with the judge. When asked about CDs submitted as evidence, he said he could not make them public, adding there were several and they were already before the court. It may be noted that Ashutosh Brahmachari Maharaj, a disciple of Jagadguru Rambhadracharya, has accused the Shankaracharya’s camp of abusing children. On 8 February he filed a complaint in the special POCSO court alleging that child abuse was being carried out under the guise of a gurukul. He said- Avimukteshwaranand is involved in illegal activities. He has assets more than his income. An impartial investigation should be conducted into this. In response to a court notice, Avimukteshwaranand’s lawyer submitted a reply on 10 February. Speaking earlier, the Shankaracharya said they had presented all evidence in court and had full faith in the judiciary. He claimed that ever since he began raising his voice for cow protection, some people and the government had been displeased. Both sides’ lawyers will appear again on 20 February. Ashutosh Brahmachari is also the main petitioner and party in the Shri Krishna Janmabhoomi–Shahi Masjid Idgah dispute. After a controversy during the Magh fair, Rambhadracharya and Avimukteshwaranand had come face to face. First complained to Police Commissioner, then went to court Six days after Mauni Amavasya, on 24 January, Ashutosh Maharaj lodged two complaints with the police commissioner in Prayagraj. The first alleged minors were kept in Avimukteshwaranand’s camp and gurukul and made to perform personal service, gather crowds, attend events and carry palanquins. He also suspected sexual abuse. He alleged children were made to work even during large events like the Magh fair, violating child rights and labour laws. He further suspected illegal weapons in the camp and demanded investigation into assets and bank accounts beyond known income, as well as the role of a person named Mukundanand. In the second complaint he accused Avimukteshwaranand of using fake letterheads and documents, claiming he was presenting himself in the Magh fair area as the Shankaracharya of Jyotishpeeth and issuing letters to officials in that name. These letterheads dated 24 January 2026 were described as fake and misleading. Read what Ashutosh Maharaj filed in court When authorities took no action, he filed a court complaint on 8 February. He wrote that his trust was conducting a ritual during the Magh fair for liberation of the Shri Krishna Janmabhoomi site. Two minor disciples came to his camp and made disclosures, sought to become his disciples and requested police protection and judicial help, saying they felt unsafe. They alleged that Avimukteshwaranand and associates kept them and repeatedly assaulted them over a year, including during the 2025 Kumbh and again during the 2026 Magh fair. They claimed disciples pressured them, saying it was “guru service” that would bring blessings, and told them to sleep beside Avimukteshwaranand. They said they escaped and reached his camp. Complaints were submitted at Jhunsi police station on 24 January, emailed to the police commissioner and Magh fair SP on 25 January, and posted to the SP on 27 January, but no FIR was registered. After that, he said, threats began. Who is Ashutosh Maharaj? Ashutosh Brahmachari Maharaj was born in a Brahmin family in Kandhla town of Shamli district. His father Rajendra Pandey worked as a conductor on private buses. Ashutosh is associated with the committee of the ancient Shakambhari Siddhpeeth temple in Kandhla and currently serves as its manager. His uncle Pradeep Pandey is a priest there. In 2022 he took initiation from Jagadguru Rambhadracharya and has lived an ascetic life since. Administration stopped Avimukteshwaranand's palanquin on Mauni Amavasya On 18 January during the Magh fair, Avimukteshwaranand was heading in a palanquin for a ritual bath when police stopped it and asked him to walk to the Sangam. Disciples refused and tried to proceed, leading to pushing and jostling with police. Several disciples were detained and one sadhu was allegedly beaten at a police outpost, angering the Shankaracharya, who insisted on their release. Police later detained more supporters and pulled the palanquin about 1 km away from the Sangam, during which its canopy broke. He could not take the holy dip and left the fair without bathing. Shankaracharya departed from Magh Mela without taking a dip in the Ganges Rambhadracharya had opposed him On the issue, Rambhadracharya said no injustice had been done to Avimukteshwaranand and that rules do not permit going to the Sangam by palanquin, so the notice was justified. Avimukteshwaranand responded that Rambhadracharya was merely maintaining friendships and people did not take him seriously. He added that Rambhadracharya was not of his tradition and would otherwise have understood his pain. He claimed that historically even Peshwas carried his palanquin.

stories.title: Shoaib, linked to Mukhtar Ansari, killed in daylight:15 bullets sprayed at car in Barabanki; gunmen came on bike
stories.summary: In Barabanki, Shoaib Kidwai alias Bobby, a shooter linked to mafia don Mukhtar Ansari, was shot dead. He was 50 years old. The incident took place at around 1.30 pm on Friday when he was travelling by car from Lucknow to Barabanki. Just 100 metres ahead on the highway, two men on a motorbike intercepted him. Before Shoaib could react, they opened indiscriminate fire on his car with pistols. According to police sources, more than 15 bullets were fired at him. After carrying out the attack, the assailants fled towards Ayodhya. Police reached the spot soon after receiving information and rushed Shoaib to the hospital, where doctors declared him dead. The shooting took place near Aseni turn on the Lucknow–Ayodhya highway under the Kotwali police station area. The car bore bullet marks at several places. Police sealed off the crime scene, and the forensic team collected evidence. On receiving news of the murder, IG Praveen Kumar, the District Magistrate and the Superintendent of Police reached the spot. Bobby had several cases registered against him, including murder, extortion and gang rivalry. Sources said that after the death of Mukhtar Ansari, there had been an internal power struggle and personal enmity within the gang. Shoaib was also a lawyer. Lawyers created a ruckus at the district hospital in protest against his killing and demanded the arrest of the attackers within 48 hours. One of Shoaib’s brothers lives in England. Shoaib had a house in the Civil Lines area of Barabanki. He was the second among three brothers. His family includes his wife, Shazia Khan and 15-year-old son Armaan Kidwai, who studies in Class 9 at a school in Lucknow. His in-laws live in Malihabad in Lucknow, and the family also owns a house in Gomti Nagar. His elder brother Javed is a lawyer in Barabanki, while the younger brother lives in England. He also has a married sister. Apart from being a shooter, Shoaib practised law and was active in politics. He had contested the election for Block Pramukh of Banki block in Barabanki as an independent candidate but lost. He was said to play an important role in land grabbing, interfering in contracts and targeting rivals for the Mukhtar gang. Surveillance began soon after leaving Lucknow According to police sources, Shoaib was on his way to Barabanki from Lucknow and was allegedly being followed from the moment he left the city. The attackers could not strike while the car was speeding on the highway. As soon as Bobby moved the car into the service lane and slowed down, the assailants seized the opportunity and carried out the attack.

stories.summary: Sexual Harassment Row Rocks KGMU: प्रदेश की राजधानी स्थित किंग जॉर्ज मेडिकल यूनिवर्सिटी (केजीएमयू) एक बार फिर गंभीर आरोपों के कारण सुर्खियों में है। विश्वविद्यालय प्रशासन ने एक रेजिडेंट डॉक्टर की शिकायत पर एक अतिरिक्त प्रोफेसर को निलंबित कर दिया है। शिकायत में प्रोफेसर पर कथित तौर पर पीछा करने (स्टॉकिंग), अनुचित संदेश भेजने और कार्यस्थल पर आपत्तिजनक इशारे करने के आरोप लगाए गए हैं। विश्वविद्यालय के प्रवक्ता डॉ. के. के. सिंह के अनुसार, “रेज़िडेंट डॉक्टर ने बुधवार को लिखित शिकायत दी थी। प्रारंभिक स्तर पर आरोप यौन उत्पीड़न की श्रेणी में आते हैं। निष्पक्ष जांच सुनिश्चित करने और किसी भी प्रकार के प्रभाव से बचाने के लिए संबंधित अतिरिक्त प्रोफेसर को तत्काल प्रभाव से निलंबित किया गया है।”

stories.title: Mahapanchayat in Meerut over Hindu girl-Muslim boy marriage:Right wing leader under house arrest; girl says, 'It is my choice'
stories.summary: Hindu organisations have opened a front against the marriage of bank employee Akanksha and Shahvez Rana in Meerut. Both were supposed to get married today. However, fearing unrest, both families have cancelled the wedding. Meanwhile, Hindu organisations have called for a Mahapanchayat in protest, declaring it love jihad. Police have gone into alert mode in view of the Mahapanchayat announcement. In Ghaziabad, Hindu Raksha Dal president Pinky Chaudhary has been placed under house arrest after he announced his participation in the Mahapanchayat. The organisation's national president, Sachin Sirohi, said that this panchayat is being organised to protect Hindu sisters and daughters and prevent them from getting trapped in 'love jihad'. The girl's uncle has filed a complaint alleging 'love jihad', conspiracy for religious conversion and property grabbing, on which the police have registered an FIR. While the girl says she will only marry Sahil and will fight a legal battle against the FIR filed by her uncle. First, read what the bank employee girl said... Girl said - I am getting married by my own choice Bank employee Akanksha said - I am an adult and getting married by my own choice. I am not Sanatani, I am an Ambedkarite. I follow Buddhism. This marriage will be performed according to Buddhist customs. The family has known the boy from the beginning. Sahil was the nickname given by her mother. Some organisations are pressuring to cancel the banquet hall booking. They are being stopped on the way, and unnecessary disputes are being created. Actually, Akanksha Gautam, who belongs to the Dalit community, is an accounts manager in a private bank. Her father was a development officer in LIC Insurance. After spending most of his service time in Bijnor, he retired from Meerut. After retirement, he built a house in a posh society here. This family follows Buddhism. In 2023, her father passed away due to a heart attack. Akanksha's neighbourhood is also home to Shahvez Rana. Shahvez, from a Muslim family, is a manager at a private hospital. His father passed away about 10 years ago. Both families have known each other for a long time. Recently, both families had arranged the marriage between Akanksha and Shahvez. Applied for marriage, got approval from authorities... Family members say that Akanksha and Shahvez followed all legal procedures for marriage. First, they applied for a civil marriage under the Special Marriage Act of 1954. Both submitted their personal documents, including Aadhar cards, proof of being unmarried, and address proof on November 17, 2025. After applying at the ADM-City office in Meerut, both finalised their wedding date. Akanksha said that by January 2026, they received information from the ADM office that the Police Local Intelligence Unit (LIU) had given approval. After this, both families accelerated their preparations. Two wedding cards became a dispute Actually, two cards were printed for the wedding, which were sent to friends and relatives. Shahvez's family had printed his name as Shahvez Rana, while on the cards printed from Akanksha's side, Shahvez's name was printed as Sahil. A dispute arose over the name Sahil. People from Hindu organisations created a ruckus claiming religious conversion and love jihad. Meanwhile, the uncle also filed an FIR alleging brainwashing of his niece and love jihad. According to the FIR, Shahvez had hidden his real name on the wedding card, and this was part of love jihad. We have known the entire family for 6 years Akanksha's mother, Lata Gautam, said - We know the boy's entire family. I have known the boy for 6 years. His name is Shahvez. I had given him the nickname Sahil. Which was printed on the wedding card. All relatives are coming to attend the wedding. Police investigating based on uncle's complaint The girl's uncle, Premchand, has filed a complaint with the police and DM office. He alleged that his niece was lured and trapped in a religious conversion so that her property could be seized. Based on his complaint, a conversion case was registered late at night at the Ganganagar police station. Police are now thoroughly investigating the claims of both parties and the different names on the wedding cards.

stories.title: Bomb threats to 5 courts including Lucknow and Varanasi:Campuses evacuated; judges step out as ATS and STF launch investigation
stories.summary: Courts in Lucknow, Varanasi, Ayodhya, Meerut and Mirzapur received bomb threats on official government email IDs, triggering panic and immediate security action on Friday. Following the threat emails, police evacuated all five court campuses. Court proceedings were suspended as a precautionary measure. Campuses cleared, thousands evacuated In Varanasi alone, more than 3,000 lawyers and around 5,000 litigants hurriedly vacated the premises. The District Judge and other judicial officers also stepped out of the campus. Police teams, along with dog squads and bomb disposal squads, conducted thorough searches of every corner of the court complexes. However, nothing suspicious had been found at the time of reporting. Similar email pattern, probe underway According to police officials, the threat emails received at different locations follow a similar pattern. Authorities are yet to determine who sent the emails and from where. Investigators are examining why the emails were sent simultaneously and whether there is a larger conspiracy behind the threats. Senior officials in Lucknow are closely monitoring the situation. The cyber cell and other security agencies have joined the investigation. Past attack raises alarm The threat has been taken extremely seriously, especially in light of the November 23, 2007, bomb blast at the Varanasi court, in which nine people — including three lawyers — were killed and around 50 others were injured. Given the history, Anti-Terrorism Squad (ATS) and Special Task Force (STF) teams have also been deployed to assist in the investigation. Authorities continue to maintain heightened security across all five court complexes.

stories.summary: The gem-like appearance of Durgam Cheruvu hides a sinister, calculated assault. As evening lights and rooftop views sell the lake as a tourist spot, a multi-agency process seems to be killing it softly. One civic body lowers the water level to free up land, another lays a 10-metre-wide walking track on the exposed lake bed and yet another releases organically loaded effluents that fuel decay. Once a source of drinking water and part of Golconda Fort’s hydrological system, the lake is now trapped in a bureaucratic tic-tac-toe, writes Serish Nanisetti

stories.title: Former Congressman Naseemuddin to join SP:Left Congress 20 days ago; vowed to defeat communal forces
stories.summary: UP Congress heavyweight Muslim leader Nasimuddin Siddiqui, who resigned on January 24, will now join SP. On Friday after prayers, he will meet with his supporters and then announce joining SP. For 20 days, there were various discussions about his political move. Finally, after touring different districts and having long discussions with his supporters, he has made this decision. In an interview given to Dainik Bhaskar, he had also indicated that he would either join a party with a similar ideology to defeat communal forces or form a new party. Siddiqui, who started his politics from BSP, wielded considerable power as a cabinet minister in Mayawati's government. He is considered to have a strong political influence in western UP. Nasimuddin sent his resignation to Congress National President Mallikarjun Kharge and other senior leaders on January 24. At that time, 73 other leaders also left the Congress party with him. This included several former MLAs. Nasimuddin's resignation was seen as a major loss for Congress in UP. However, even after leaving the party, he maintained a soft stance towards Congress. Nasimuddin said - I came to Congress to fight casteism Nasimuddin Siddiqui was also the Provincial President of Western Uttar Pradesh Congress. He is considered to have a strong hold on the Muslim vote bank in districts around Saharanpur and Muzaffarnagar. In his resignation, Siddiqui wrote - 'I came to Congress to fight against casteism. Could not work on the ground for 8 years. I was getting rusty.' I respect Rahul Gandhi, Mallikarjun Kharge, and Sonia Gandhi, and will continue to do so. But there was no work for me in the party. I joined Congress so that I could fight against communalism. But now that was not possible.' Did not get attention in Lok Sabha elections There was dissatisfaction regarding Nasimuddin's role and influence in Congress. He did not receive attention in the 2024 Lok Sabha elections either. With the 2027 assembly elections approaching, Nasimuddin was worried about his future in Congress. The stature of Congress MP Imran Masood from Saharanpur has risen rapidly. He is counted among Priyanka's special lieutenants. Siddiqui was quite troubled by this, too. Recently, while receiving Rahul Gandhi at Amausi airport, he was not given entry ahead of other leaders, including Pramod Tiwari and Aradhana Mishra. Mayawati had expelled from BSP Nasimuddin's resignation is being considered a big loss for Congress before the 2027 assembly elections. Siddiqui was earlier in BSP, from where Mayawati expelled him in 2017. After that, he joined Congress in 2018, and the party promoted him as a Muslim face. According to sources, after the resignation, Congress state president Ajay Rai is trying to persuade him, but for now Siddiqui has clearly refused to change his decision. Now all eyes were fixed on Siddiqui's next move. There were speculations about whether he would join a new party or do independent politics? There was also a discussion that he might join Chandrashekhar's Azad Samaj Party, but Siddiqui has decided to join SP, putting an end to all speculations. Dainik Bhaskar In conversation with, Nasimuddin Siddiqui had said - 73 leaders from Delhi, Uttarakhand, Ghaziabad, including western UP have left the party with me. This includes former MLAs and other senior people. We will take a decision after discussing with everyone. Career started as a railway contractor Nasimuddin Siddiqui's name has long been prominent in Uttar Pradesh politics. His journey, which began as a railway contractor, reached its peak when he became one of Mayawati's closest associates in BSP. After being expelled from BSP, he formed a new party. Shortly after, he joined Congress along with his wife and son. Now, one year before the assembly elections, he has bid farewell to Congress as well. Nasimuddin Siddiqui was born on June 4, 1959. There was no political background in the family. After leaving his army job due to his mother's illness, he became active in railway contracting. Around 1990, Nasimuddin came in contact with BSP founder Kanshi Ram. The beginning was with the Palika (municipality) election. In 1991, he contested from the BSP from the Banda Sadar assembly seat and won. After this, he remained active in the West.

stories.title: 12th-grade student arrested in hit and run case:Accused was returning from a party with girlfriend; 6-yr-old dies, 5 seriously hurt
stories.summary: A Class 12 student has been arrested in Lucknow for mowing down 6 people while ramming vehicles with a Swift Dzire car. CCTV footage of the hit-and-run has surfaced. A six-year-old boy died on the spot, while five others remain in critical condition. The deceased child has been identified as Dikshant, son of Sadhana from Unnao. He had come to the market with his grandmother for the first time. When his mother reached the hospital, and the shroud was removed from his body, she screamed in grief. The accused fled the scene after the accident but was arrested within an hour. During questioning, he said he was returning from a farewell party. A female classmate was also in the car but got out immediately after the accident. Locals caught her and handed her over to the police. Accident near Hanuman temple The incident took place around 7 pm on Thursday near Hanuman Temple on Kanpur Road in the Banthra police station area. As the car stopped, the girl got down while the student sped away. According to ACP Krishna Nagar Rajneesh Verma, police traced the car and arrested the accused, Gaurav Singh, and seized the vehicle. He is a Class 12 student at Avadh Collegiate. He and his classmate were returning from a farewell party on Mohan Road when the accident occurred. Sequence of the incident Pramod Kumar of Sahijanpur had parked his bike by the roadside and was buying items from a shop when a speeding car travelling from Lucknow to Kanpur hit his bike. When people ran to catch the driver, he accelerated and hit 12-year-old Armaan, son of Pape alias Pauwa of Banthra, who had come to the market. About 100 metres ahead, the car struck Sadhana Patel (35), her mother Meena Devi (60), and her son Dikshant (6) from Atwa Khurd in Unnao. The driver also ran over e-rickshaw driver Avadh Bihari (42) from Pathraha village in Sohramau, Unnao, and then crashed into a stationary auto. He fled with the car before people could catch him. Injured and eyewitness accounts Pramod Kumar suffered serious head and facial injuries and is undergoing treatment at Sarojini Nagar CHC. Avadh Bihari said he was waiting for passengers near Banthra crossing when a vehicle rammed into his auto from behind, throwing him out. His wife, Shiv Devi, said she was informed by police that her husband had met with an accident. He has a head injury and is not fully conscious. Accused borrowed car; father is businessman According to information, the accused student’s father runs a cement and iron business. The student had borrowed someone else’s car to attend the party. The child’s mother, Sadhana, has filed a written complaint with the police based on the car number. Police continue to investigate the incident.
